Resolve a workspace_id on one frame, write it on the other, and the row lands in a tuple nothing publishes — silently, because the pot-membership trigger FAILS OPEN for an unknown workspace. harness_shared.substrate_outbox.drained_at is the one-query discriminator: undrained = your write was mis-targeted; drained-but-unarrived = a real replication failure. Also: a 90s poll window can expire before a HEALTHY link delivers.

## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) A two-machine federation probe writes a row on frame A, polls frame B, and reports: 
```plaintext
=== VERDICT forward=1 reverse=0 ===
```
 One direction works, the other reads 0. That asymmetry looks exactly like a half-open data path, so the investigation goes to the transport layer: holepunch, DHT universe, relayed-vs-direct paths, socket churn. On WI-6209 that reflex was **right once and wrong twice**. There genuinely was a transport bug (two VMs running different bundles — one lacked the `samePrivateIPv4Subnet24` holepunch fix, so the leg *it* dialled never came up). But after that was fixed and verified — `never_came_up=0` on both frames, direct non-relayed paths, channels open — the reverse leg *still* read 0. That surviving 0 was not a second defect. It was the probe writing to a tuple that publishes nothing. ## Why the write goes nowhere, silently [Section titled “Why the write goes nowhere, silently”](#why-the-write-goes-nowhere-silently) **A pot has one identity but two local names.** `harness_shared.pots.public_key` is byte-identical on every frame in the pot. `(workspace_id, pot_home_slug)` is **local to each machine**: | frame | workspace\_id | pot\_home\_slug | | ----- | -------------------- | --------------------- | | fed-a | `workspace-319be5e5` | `spoon-knife-pot` | | fed-b | `workspace-b31a7a01` | `octocat-spoon-knife` | So a probe that resolves the workspace on one frame and reuses it on the other — 
```bash
# WRONG: WS is resolved on fed-a…
WS="$(sql a "SELECT workspace_id FROM harness_shared.pot_members
             WHERE coalesce(origin,'local')='local' ORDER BY joined_at LIMIT 1;")"
# …then written on BOTH frames
write_row a "$WS" "$FWD"   # fine, it is A's own workspace
write_row b "$WS" "$REV"   # lands in a tuple fed-b has never booted
```
 — writes the reverse row into `workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife` **on fed-b**, a `(workspace_id, harness_slug)` fed-b does not have booted. No substrate binding owns it, so nothing ever drains it. The row sits in the table forever as `origin='local'` and the poll on A reads a clean, confident `0`. **And it does not even error.** `assert_work_item_pot_membership` rejects a made-up harness slug — but only after this guard: 
```sql
-- Fail OPEN for a workspace with no platform Pot (isolated fixtures / un-potted tenant).
v_platform := harness_shared.workspace_platform_pot(NEW.workspace_id);
IF v_platform IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;
```
 An unknown workspace has no platform pot, so the trigger **fails open** and accepts the row. The one case that most needs rejecting is the one waved through. (Write the same bogus slug under a workspace that *does* have a platform pot and you get a loud rejection — which is how the trap was finally noticed.) ## The discriminator: `substrate_outbox.drained_at` [Section titled “The discriminator: substrate\_outbox.drained\_at”](#the-discriminator-substrate_outboxdrained_at) A local write destined to federate is captured into `harness_shared.substrate_outbox` and later drained to a peer log. One query separates the two causes: 
```sql
SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug,
       (drained_at     IS NOT NULL) AS drained,
       (quarantined_at IS NOT NULL) AS quarantined
FROM harness_shared.substrate_outbox
WHERE key = '<the feature_id you wrote>';
```
 Measured on the live rig, this cleanly split the probes: | probe | tuple written | drained | reality | | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------- | | `F-6209-REV-…` | `workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife` on **B** | `f` | mis-targeted — never publishable | | `F-6209-REVTRUE-…` | `workspace-b31a7a01/octocat-spoon-knife` | `t` | arrived on A in **6s** | | `F-6209-SK-REV-…` | `workspace-b31a7a01/spoon-knife` | `t` | arrived on A, but **after 90s** | Read it as: * **no outbox row** → the capture trigger never fired; the INSERT targeted something not federated at all. * **row, `drained_at IS NULL`** → your write is mis-targeted. No booted binding owns that `(workspace_id, harness_slug)` on that frame. **A test bug, not a replication failure.** * **row, `drained_at` set, still unarrived** → a genuine replication/transport failure *or* a poll window that expired too early. * **`quarantined_at` set** → the substrate refused to publish it. ## The second false negative: a poll window shorter than a healthy delivery [Section titled “The second false negative: a poll window shorter than a healthy delivery”](#the-second-false-negative-a-poll-window-shorter-than-a-healthy-delivery) `fed_merge_assert` defaults to `tries=30` at 3s — exactly 90 seconds. On the repaired rig one legitimate reverse write landed **after** that window closed: the probe reported `0`, and the row was sitting on the destination `origin='remote'` minutes later. A healthy link can exceed 90s. Treat a bare timeout as “not yet observed”, never as “did not replicate” — check `drained_at` before concluding anything. ## Do this instead [Section titled “Do this instead”](#do-this-instead) 1. **Resolve each frame’s own scope.** Pair frames by `harness_shared.pots.public_key`; never copy a `workspace_id` or a `pot_home_slug` across machines. Resolve the write target on the frame you are about to write to. 2. **Poll destination-side slug-agnostically.** Federation may remap `harness_slug` across peers, so match on `feature_id AND origin='remote'` rather than pinning the source slug (`fed_hive_merge_probe` already does). 3. **On a negative, diagnose before you blame the wire.** `fed_diagnose_unmerged <frame> <key>` in `bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh` runs the query above and prints which class it is. It is wired into the failure path of `fed_merge_assert` and `fed_hive_merge_probe`, so a bare `0` no longer reaches a human undiagnosed. ## A trap inside the trap [Section titled “A trap inside the trap”](#a-trap-inside-the-trap) The first cut of `fed_diagnose_unmerged` built its verdict from `(drained_at IS NOT NULL)` concatenated into a text column and compared the result against `'t'`. That is wrong: `boolean || text` casts through `boolean::text`, which renders **`true`/`false`** — psql’s `t`/`f` is a *display* convention of the table formatter, not the value. The guard therefore misclassified every row. The fixture test did not catch it, because the fixtures had been hand-written with the same wrong assumption (`…|t|f`) and passed happily. Only running the guard against the live database exposed it. The fix was to stop depending on boolean rendering at all: 
```sql
CASE WHEN drained_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END
```
 **A fixture you authored from your own mental model tests your model, not the system.** When a guard parses real output, pin at least one assertion to bytes the real source produced. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * `replication-liveness.ts` — the in-process detector ladder (`no_replicator` / `frozen` / `connected_never_replicated` / `expected_never_admitted`). It watches the *substrate*; the outbox check above watches whether your write ever entered it. Different questions — a probe can fail while every liveness axis is correctly green. * [raw SQL plan reads need workspace+harness scope](/internal/docs/agent-insights/raw-sql-plan-slug-needs-workspace-harness-scope) — the same multi-tenant hazard on the read side.

# Decompose federation "X never crossed" reds in ONE query — group substrate_outbox by scope × drained-state

> A live differential (WI-971) separated three co-mingled causes behind identical federation-matrix reds (smoke wrong-workspace writes / receive-side backfill latency / joiner home-view drain gap) in minutes, once the LIVE pair's substrate_outbox was grouped by (workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, drained_at IS NULL). Prior sessions burned hours theorizing from smoke stdout alone.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) When a federation/replication test reports “content never crossed A→B” (or a whole matrix of federation smokes goes red at once), the instinct is to theorize from the smoke test’s own stdout — but the smoke output can’t distinguish three completely different root causes that all present as the same symptom. A live WI-971 differential separated all three in minutes by querying the LIVE pair’s `harness_shared.substrate_outbox` directly instead: 
```sql
SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name,
       (drained_at IS NULL) AS undrained,
       count(*)
  FROM harness_shared.substrate_outbox
 GROUP BY workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, (drained_at IS NULL)
 ORDER BY workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name, undrained;
```
 ## Reading the result — three distinct root causes, one query [Section titled “Reading the result — three distinct root causes, one query”](#reading-the-result--three-distinct-root-causes-one-query) * **Undrained rows sit in a scope with NO booted substrate handle** → this is a **capture/scope bug on the SEND side** (writes are landing in the outbox under the wrong scope, or a scope that was never wired to a running handle). The send side is otherwise fine — the row is captured, it’s just captured under a scope nothing is draining. * **Rows show `drained_at` set (drained INSTANTLY) but are still missing on the peer** → this is a **RECEIVE-side problem**: the row left the sender’s outbox correctly, so look at backfill latency or the joiner’s home-view drain gap on the receiving end, not the sender. * **The undrained/missing pattern is per-TABLE selective** (some tables cross fine, others never do) → this is almost always a **mapping or scope bug** for the affected table specifically — never “the drain is down” globally, since a globally-down drain would affect every table uniformly. ## Where to get the LIVE pair’s DSN [Section titled “Where to get the LIVE pair’s DSN”](#where-to-get-the-live-pairs-dsn) The two-instance smoke tests leave the pair **running** after they finish — don’t tear them down to theorize, query them directly. Their connection strings live in `instances.env`: `harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:<pg-port>/papercusp` (one DSN per instance). Point `dev:pg_query` (or a direct `psql`) at each pair member with the query above before writing a single line of theory. ## The detector this spec-shapes (WI-183-class) [Section titled “The detector this spec-shapes (WI-183-class)”](#the-detector-this-spec-shapes-wi-183-class) The “undrained rows sitting in a scope with no booted handle, forever” case above is exactly the input shape for a **replication-liveness detector**: alert when `undrained_age = now() - min(ts) WHERE drained_at IS NULL` exceeds a threshold, grouped per `(workspace_id, harness_slug, table_name)` scope. No such detector exists yet (as of this doc) — this query is effectively its manual, on-demand form. If you’re about to build that detector, the GROUP BY shape above is the query to automate. ## Consequence [Section titled “Consequence”](#consequence) Before spending more than a few minutes theorizing about a federation “never crossed” red from smoke-test output alone, run the GROUP BY query above against the live pair. It costs one query and immediately tells you WHICH of the three root-cause classes you’re in, instead of guessing from indirect symptoms.

# Federation public-release: known limitations + release-criteria gate

> The honest release calibration for cross-machine p2p shared-pot federation — what is proven LIVE vs proven IN-PROCESS ONLY, the standing known limitations (multi-device identity, coord control-plane local-only, revocation read-cut, LWW divergence, NAT, bg-host leak, 2-server cap), the forceReFold mechanism + its cost, and the explicit public-release checklist (which hardening briefs must be green to ship).

This is the **honest release calibration** for cross-machine peer-to-peer shared-pot federation: what is proven **live** (over real, separate machines on the public DHT), what is proven **in-process only**, the standing **known limitations**, the **`forceReFold` mechanism + its cost**, and the explicit **public-release checklist** — which of the federation-release-hardening briefs must be green before we can call federation shippable. It deliberately supersedes the optimistic “FULLY WORKING + RELEASE-READY” claim (memory `a02714f1`) with the calibrated view (memory `f64a176d`, the calibration correction — **read that one**). The core path is real and reproducible; it is **not yet at a defensible public-release bar**. Read this before telling anyone federation is done. > **The one rule this page exists to enforce: in-process green ≠ live green.** The A→B owner-admit race passed *every* in-process test and still failed live. So an in-process-green scenario is *necessary but not sufficient* evidence — every release-gating scenario must be **reproduced over real VMs**, not just asserted in the in-process matrix. *** ## Status snapshot [Section titled “Status snapshot”](#status-snapshot) | Capability | Status | Evidence | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Base federation (content/features + per-part plans + coord **data**), A→B **and** B→A | ✅ **Proven LIVE — no-restart blocker RESOLVED** | run33/34/35 + Briefs 4/3/7 (2026-07-01/02). The no-restart roster-empty class (blocker #9 / WI-1378) is fixed by THREE stacked fixes: the fresh home-resolve (3030bfd13), the directory self-echo guard (WI-1422), and the **deterministic join-time owner-device binding** (verified coords extracted from the member links + stamped on the registry view — no directory-timing dependence; Brief 7’s baseline federated FIRST-poll). WI-1329 | *** ## What is proven LIVE (the core path) [Section titled “What is proven LIVE (the core path)”](#what-is-proven-live-the-core-path) Over **2 separate Hetzner cpx31 VMs**, production config (trace flags OFF), real public DHT, three consecutive green runs (run33/34/35): * **Content** — features (`origin=remote` both ways), per-part plans (P-001 both ways), and **coord data** (threads/posts/events) all federate **A→B and B→A**. * It is a **controlled** result: run32 (production, *no* fix) A→B = FAIL; run33 (production, *with* fix) A→B = PASS — the only difference was the fix. * The working stack: `connection.ts` PG-port crash fix + boot-enum (D-040/D-057) * D-007 link-seed + reader-merge + join-pot rekey (the rig joins via `POST /api/discovery/join-pot`, **not** `/api/harness/join-link`) + recv-during-rekey owner-admit + the `forceReFold` re-fold. This is the strongest evidence we have, and it is genuine. But it is a **thin sample**: N≈3 runs, a **single easy topology** (public-IP VMs, same region, a single joiner), no NAT/firewall/geo diversity, and the extended scenarios below were *not* exercised in these runs. ## What is proven IN-PROCESS only [Section titled “What is proven IN-PROCESS only”](#what-is-proven-in-process-only) The full extended matrix is green **in-process** (single box, in-process swarm, two separate Postgres DBs): `federation-{content,comms,issues-assignments}-matrix`, `federation-multimember-sidecar`, `federation-security-drops-sidecar`, `federation-revocation-kcut-sidecar`, `federation-reconnect-catchup-sidecar`, `federation-restart-durability-sidecar`, `federation-concurrent-writes-sidecar` (28 tests under `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/`). These are real, teeth-proven tests — but **the whole point of the live-hardening effort is that the A→B race passed all of them and still failed live.** Treat in-process green as a *prerequisite*, never as the live proof. Each of these scenarios needs a live VM reproduction before it gates a release claim (Briefs 2–7, consolidated into the live-matrix runner, Brief 13). *** ## The `forceReFold` mechanism + its cost [Section titled “The forceReFold mechanism + its cost”](#the-forcerefold-mechanism--its-cost) `forceReFold` is the deterministic fix for the live A→B owner-admit timing race. **Root cause.** The joiner (B) bootstrap-admits the owner’s (A’s) log during the `home=<none>` boot window. It folds A’s `hive_members` op through the **member-slug-bound** projection, so A’s roster row is **dropped** at `projections/pot-members.ts` (`row.hive_home_slug !== member slug`) and the merge cursor marks the op done. When the rekey rebinds the projections to the **pot-home** slug, `retryPendingOnce` only re-*admits* still-pending peers — it does **not** re-apply an already-admitted-and-folded op. Result: empty roster → A’s content defers forever. **The fix** (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/boot.ts`): 1. A one-shot `let forceReFold = false` flag. 2. Set `forceReFold = true` in `rekey()`’s rebind block, *after* the `hive_members`/`hive_settings` projections rebind from the member slug to the pot-home slug. 3. Consumed at the top of the merge pass, under the merge gate: it resets the merge cursor (`mergeCursor = createMergeCursor()`) and clears the flag, so the next pass **re-folds every admitted log** through the now-pot-home-bound projection — A’s roster row re-applies and the deferred content drains. 4. Driven by a terminal `mergeNow()` at the end of `rekey()` (this is what makes it deterministic, rather than depending on the 5s periodic tick — the latency that `PAPERCUSP_A003_TRACE`’s stderr delay accidentally flipped green in run31 vs the red run32). Regression test: `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/owner-roster-rebind-race.repro.integration.test.ts` (deterministic, RED-without / GREEN-with). Adversarial review verdict: **SAFE TO SHIP** — no CRITICAL/HIGH, race-freedom sound (the terminal `mergeNow()` always delivers the re-fold with the new binding), projections are LWW-guarded, revocation ordering correct, `pendingMemberContent` drain fires once (review record: memory `4d1db206`). ### The cost (and the one open follow-up) [Section titled “The cost (and the one open follow-up)”](#the-cost-and-the-one-open-follow-up) `forceReFold` re-folds **all admitted logs** on **each home-resolving rekey rebind**. It is **one-shot** — the flag is cleared immediately under the merge gate, so steady-state passes are unaffected — but the re-fold itself is `O(total ops across all admitted logs)`. At scale (many members, large logs, repeated rekeys) this is the thing to watch for a perf cliff; Brief 9 is characterizing it (in-process, since live many-member is blocked by the quota cap). No cliff/leak has been attributed to it yet. > **Snapshot interaction — the gating follow-up (Brief 11).** The `forceReFold` cursor reset is placed *before* `seedCursorFromSnapshots`. With `FLAGS.SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT` ON, the re-fold must still re-apply the dropped `hive_members` op (a snapshot op summarizes all current rows, so it should). An integration test covering `forceReFold` reset → `seedCursorFromSnapshots` with the snapshot flag ON **must land before the log-compaction/snapshot flag ships.** This is the only open review item. *** ## Known limitations (standing, document-honestly) [Section titled “Known limitations (standing, document-honestly)”](#known-limitations-standing-document-honestly) ### 0. Coordination control plane — BRIDGED for pot-scoped sends (updated 2026-07-01) [Section titled “1. Coordination control plane — BRIDGED for pot-scoped sends (updated 2026-07-01)”](#1-coordination-control-plane--bridged-for-pot-scoped-sends-updated-2026-07-01) The original Brief-7 finding (“a wake fired on A does not wake a live agent on B”) is **no longer the architecture** — it was the send-side gates, and `cross-machine-coord-parity-and-trust-2026-07-01` closed them (Phases 0–2): pot-scoped `coord:send` federates with the persisted wake intent and the receiving projection fires the wake fan on arrival (EI-279 + P-001 scope stamping); wake-on-reply bridges back (P-002); `events:emit {scope:'pot'}` re-fires keys into every machine’s await store (P-009); directed required-wakes get delivery receipts (`coord:receipt:<msg_id>`, P-008); remote agents are addressable via the federated session roster (P-005/P-007). Residual caveats: UN-scoped (operator-local) sends still never leave the machine — the send result’s `federated:` field is the truth; cross-machine wakes are budget-capped per author device (P-003); presence still rides the log until the `papercusp-presence-gossip` cutover flag flips; and the whole bridge’s LIVE 2-machine proof is still owed (the in-process suites are green — in-process ≠ live, this page’s own rule). **Handoffs are trust-gated, not broken (WI-1510 disposition, 2026-07-02).** The handoffs surface federates on the wire like messages/escalations, but the receiver-side P-013 comms-tier gate (`sync/hyperbee/projections/coord-message.ts` + `comms-tier-gate.ts`) requires the *author* to resolve to tier `steer` — via a **local** `comms_trust_list` grant or the owner-signed pot-policy default — before a remote handoff applies; below that it lands in `harness_shared.coord_quarantine` (reason `handoff-below-steer`): visible and grantable, never silently applied or dropped. There is deliberately **no owner special-case** (steer grants are per-user, per-machine, and never federate). Messages/escalations need only the `message` fallback tier, which is why they pass ungranted. Both legs live-proven in the matrix (`deb-hetzner-coord-controlplane.sh`: ungranted → QUARANTINE, steer-granted → FEDERATED). Tier lookups are TTL-cached \~30s (`PAPERCUSP_COMMS_TIER_CACHE_MS`) — a fresh grant takes up to that long to take effect. ### 2. Multi-device, same identity [Section titled “2. Multi-device, same identity”](#2-multi-device-same-identity) Federation identity is **per-device keypair**, not per-GitHub-account. The substrate is “Model B” — per-device single-writer logs + read-merge (`sync/hyperbee/peer-log.ts`), *not* Autobase — so sharing one pot keypair across a user’s devices is *safe* (no writer conflict), but **discovery and merge are separate gates**: the shared keypair grants topic discovery, while the actual merge is gated by membership (`classifySameHiveMember` admits a remote log only if its `device_pubkey` is in `hive_members`). So one human on two devices = two distinct device pubkeys, each needing its own membership admission. The dogfood per-owner pot solves the same-owner case (Solution C, `harness/papercusp-pot-share.ts`: a per-owner private identity gist + an owner-signed allowlist policy auto-admits the owner’s login). **UPDATE 2026-07-10 (WI-3546 / p2p-rest-lanes-2026-07-09 P-009): the two-device data-merge is now WITNESSED LIVE, BOTH directions, with a real second device** — superseding the prior “only single-box-smoke-verified, never witnessed live” gap. Rig: Linux tower (`dev-box-linux`) ↔ mac VM (`aviweiss@172.31.44.2`), one owner identity, both device pubkeys admitted (the VM’s registry row was backfilled to `harness_kind:'hive'` / `remote_hive:true` per **WI-3891** so `isRegisteredHive` flips true). A genuine coord write on each side federated and merged on the other, attributed by author pubkey + machine, verified by direct `psql` on BOTH boxes (not a peer report), sustained (paired markers \~3.5 min apart, no re-freeze): * **VM→tower:** tower `harness_shared.coord_event_log` rows **463624** (22:47:13Z) * **463662** (22:50:45Z), `origin='remote'`, `author_pubkey ef7a8160…` (the VM’s writer log), payload = the VM-authored `VMREAL20260710-2246` markers — landing **8h15m past the prior freeze** (id 458509, 10:32:45 EDT). * **tower→VM:** the VM’s OWN `coord_event_log` rows **415** (22:47:19Z) + **419** (22:50:51Z), `origin='remote'`, `author_pubkey 5b00878b…` (the tower’s writer log), payload = `coord:receipt` fed\_events self-identifying `machine:dev-box-linux`, `delivered:true`. > **Do NOT use `probe:emit` / `harness_shared.federation_probes` hop-advance as the live-federation discriminant (WI-3962).** `probe:emit` only stamps the `federation_probes` side-table and `probe:record-hop` was never wired into the real pipeline stages, so a probe stalls at `captured` forever regardless of actual health — an unconditional false-NO-GO. Read live federation health from fresh `origin='remote'` `coord_event_log` rows + `substrate_merge_cursor` advancement, as above. The stricter “private key never leaves the creating device” remote-JOIN variant (share only the pubkey) is deliberately not built. The historical phase1b multi-device collision (contributor-file login-key overwrite) is *obsolete* — admission is now keyed by the stable numeric `github_user_id` + a device-signed announce/attestation ([phase1b-federation-limitations](/internal/docs/agent-insights/phase1b-federation-limitations)). ### 3. Revocation is WRITE + DISCOVERY-plane only (hard read cut-off rides the re-key) [Section titled “3. Revocation is WRITE + DISCOVERY-plane only (hard read cut-off rides the re-key)”](#3-revocation-is-write--discovery-plane-only-hard-read-cut-off-rides-the-re-key) A revoked/banned member stops being *aggregated* and stops *discovering* new content, but `swarm.ts`’s `store.replicate(socket)` serves cores to any topic peer, so a removed member (or anyone who got the link while the pot was public) keeps **reading** future content until the pot **re-keys** (C-001) or is **dissolved**. The in-place re-key epoch **K-cut** that closes the read plane is now **enabled by default in production** (`papercusp-pot-rekey` — no longer dark; built in `pot-epoch-boot-deps.ts` / `buildHiveRekeyBootDeps`, consumed on the in-place `rekey()` rebind, never a reboot). But its **cross-machine LIVE proof is still pending (Brief 3)** — today only the in-process `federation-revocation-kcut-sidecar` + `pot-late-join-epoch-decrypt-federation` tests cover the K-cut. This is a conscious product decision, not a silent hole. ([substrate-revocation-model](/internal/docs/agent-insights/substrate-revocation-model).) ### 4. LWW convergence under clock skew — the four ordering sources are FIXED (2026-07-02); one presence gap remains (§ 4a) [Section titled “4. LWW convergence under clock skew — the four ordering sources are FIXED (2026-07-02); one presence gap remains (§ 4a)”](#4-lww-convergence-under-clock-skew--the-four-ordering-sources-are-fixed-2026-07-02-one-presence-gap-remains--4a) The S0 class (“two honest peers silently materialize different rows for the same key”) had **four** distinct sources, all now fixed: 1. **Capture-boundary two-clock bug (mig 446):** two clock reads in the *same transaction* stamped the same op — the mig-314 BEFORE trigger stamps the row’s `fed_ts` with `clock_timestamp()` while the AFTER capture triggers stamped the outbox wire `ts` with `now()` (txn start), so author ≠ every receiver forever. Mig 446 threads the ROW’s `fed_ts` as the put-op wire ts in **both** capture functions. Live-verified (concurrent\_lww PASS, m1783013203). 2. **HLC-fold vs fed\_ts-guard order split (mig 458, EI-1698):** the merge winners-fold ordered by HLC while the PG guards ordered by wall-clock `fed_ts` (and later, non-transitively, by a mixed rule). Mig 458 introduces `harness_shared.fed_order_key(hlc, ts)` — an immutable SQL mirror of `lwwPick`’s derivation — and applies it to all 40 guard clauses (put+delete) across the 20 mutable projection writers: one ordering key of record end-to-end. ([hlc-merge-vs-fed-ts-guard-divergence](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hlc-merge-vs-fed-ts-guard-divergence).) 3. **Exact fed\_hlc ties swap winners (WI-1672, mig 459):** after any recv-ratchet episode, peers advance clocks by counter only in near-lockstep and routinely mint IDENTICAL `(ms, count)` stamps; every tie-accepting `>=` guard then accepts the incoming op on BOTH peers and two honest peers stably SWAP winners (observed live on the wi1544 3-frame rig). Fixed by a node-id total order: 3-segment HLC `<15-digit ms>:<5-digit count>:<16-hex node>` (locks-core `hlc.ts` + mig 459’s `hlc_clock.node_id` / 3-segment `hlc_now()`/`hlc_recv()`); a genuine full tie can now only be the same stamp replayed, where tie-accept is correct (idempotent). Legacy 2-segment stamps lose ties deterministically on every peer. 4. **The recv-ratchet amplifier (mig 460):** `hlc_recv`/`HlcClock.recv` blindly adopted any remote `ms`, so ONE absurd-future stamp pinned the clock — and, re-propagated, the whole pot — years ahead, permanently (self-demonstrated live on the dev DB during WI-1672 verification). Both now refuse to ratchet past `now + 600s` (2× the D-007 announce-admission window, so every legitimately-admitted peer still ratchets); the op’s DATA still applies, only the clock advance is skipped. Evidence for 3+4: the convergence-fuzz rig now models the REAL production topology (`localAuthorApply` = skipOwnOps + the unguarded trigger write path; `lockstep` = the ratcheted counter-lockstep) — node-LESS stamps split-brain across a 120-seed sweep (teeth), node-carrying stamps converge on all 120 seeds, monotone AND skew; plus the forced-tie two-device swarm + migrated-PG integration test (`federation-concurrent-writes-sidecar.repro.integration.test.ts`). ### 4a. Local-del resurrection under skipOwnOps — row-PRESENCE split-brain (WI-1684, FIXED 2026-07-09) [Section titled “4a. Local-del resurrection under skipOwnOps — row-PRESENCE split-brain (WI-1684, FIXED 2026-07-09)”](#4a-local-del-resurrection-under-skipownops--row-presence-split-brain-wi-1684-fixed-2026-07-09) Found by the production-topology fuzz rig while verifying the WI-1672 fix, and **not** fixed by node ids: an author DELETES a row locally (trigger path — row gone, **no tombstone**) and its own del is skipOwnOps-excluded from its own fold; a CONCURRENT foreign put with a LOWER fed\_hlc then wins the author’s fold among foreign ops alone and hits the projection’s no-row insert path, which has nothing to arbitrate against → the row is RESURRECTED on the author peer only, while every other peer folds del + put together and keeps it deleted. Classic LWW-set missing-tombstone gap, specific to the local-write path bypassing the merge’s winners map. Needs genuinely concurrent cross-peer writes straddling a delete, so lower frequency than WI-1672 — but silent, permanent divergence when it hits. **FIX SHIPPED**: `skipOwnOps` narrowed to PUTS ONLY in `projection.ts`’s `applyOpVia` — a winning own DEL is now always re-applied (a fed\_hlc-guarded delete that removes the resurrected row), which is echo-safe (a 0-row delete never fires the capture trigger’s `FOR EACH ROW`; a resurrected row is `origin='remote'` so capture’s echo-guard skips it) and orthogonal to WI-1672 (own PUTs stay skipped, so its teeth stay green). Regression pinned as a HARD test (not a characterisation) in `convergence-fuzz.test.ts`’s `WI-1684` describe block: `TEETH` proves the bug reproduces with `applyOwnDels:false`, `FIXED` asserts `expect(failures).toEqual([])` across the full 120-seed sweep with the shipped fix — both green as of 2026-07-09. ### 5. NAT / firewall / geo assumptions — LIVE-PROVEN with one caveat (Brief 8, 2026-07-02) [Section titled “5. NAT / firewall / geo assumptions — LIVE-PROVEN with one caveat (Brief 8, 2026-07-02)”](#5-nat--firewall--geo-assumptions--live-proven-with-one-caveat-brief-8-2026-07-02) Brief 8 lifted this from the easy topology: 2 Hetzner frames **cross-region** (ash↔hil) with a **stateful restricted-cone NAT** (nftables masquerade + established/related-only inbound) in front of the member frame, real public DHT. Verdict: **holepunch PASS both directions; member→owner content PASS; owner→member content is LATE, not never** — ops the owner appends while the joiner is still in its owner-binding-null admit-refusal window stall indefinitely (80+ min observed, survives a cold restart of the member) until the **next owner-side append** kicks the replication/fold, after which the entire backlog folds within minutes. No data loss; the log is intact. Filed as **WI-1534** (unbounded staleness on quiescent pots). **MITIGATION SHIPPED (2026-07-09):** root-caused to the WI-752/FED-2 self-heal re-peer loop (`joinHarnessSwarm`’s `discovery.refresh()` cadence) settling into its 60s SLOW keepalive once the post-join/post-peer-loss FAST window lapses — on a QUIESCENT pot (no connection churn to naturally re-arm the fast window) that is the only thing that ever retries a stalled/zombie/never-attached admitted remote’s reconnect, so the peer sits at 0 live replicator peers for as long as it takes an UNRELATED event (the next owner append) to coincidentally land alongside a working DHT/holepunch retry. The merge pass itself was already correct (`core.update({wait:true})` + `changed` re-fold run unconditionally every 1s poll for every admitted remote — never the gap; corestore’s `streamTracker.attachAll()` also already late-admit-attaches a newly-opened remote core to every live muxer, so late-admit-mesh is not the gap either). Fix: a new `hasStalledLogs()` predicate (boot.ts, fed from the `admitted` map’s `peersCount()===0` check) wired into `joinHarnessSwarm`’s self-heal loop (`swarm.ts`) keeps it on the FAST cadence for as long as ANY admitted remote log shows zero live replicator peers, instead of dropping to the 60s slow keepalive regardless. Unit-pinned in `swarm-self-heal.test.ts` (fake-timer cadence assertions: stays fast while stalled, falls back to the dead-zone/slow-keepalive once the stall clears, a throwing predicate never breaks the loop). **Known gap (found 2026-07-25, EI-18665254552552477):** the mitigation only covers a stalled *admitted* remote — `hasStalledLogs()` iterates the `admitted` map and falls through to `false` when it is empty, so a peer that has never admitted *any* remote (its announce channel never pairs at all) reads as “not stalled” and stays on the 60s slow cadence — backwards, since zero admitted remotes is the worst case this mitigation exists to catch, not the healthiest. Reproduced live in gate run `20260725-183831`: 20.5 minutes, 188 established connections, zero inbound frames, zero admitted remotes for the whole window, on the slowest retry cadence throughout. Complementary to (not covered by) the separate rung-(c) swarm fix. **Still open:** live verification on the 2-node containerized rig (`bin/local-matrix.sh`, P-006) and/or the tower+VM NAT rig (Brief 8’s setup) — this is a real-network timing fix that a real restricted-cone-NAT rig run is needed to confirm actually shortens the 80+min stall; coordinate with whoever next runs that rig. Remaining out-of-scope rung: **symmetric NAT** (needs a real symmetric-NAT middlebox; port-dependent mapping defeats the restricted-cone emulation). Earlier rig work also proved that two VMs sharing one NAT egress IP **hairpin** and fail a public-DHT holepunch — a class of failure single-NAT topologies never surface. ### 6. Long-running node stability (bg-host leak) — RESOLVED (2026-07-02) [Section titled “6. Owner→joiner federation can stay broken in the pure NO-RESTART join path (RESOLVED — both mechanisms fixed + live-verified 2026-07-02) [Section titled “9. Owner→joiner federation can stay broken in the pure NO-RESTART join path (RESOLVED — both mechanisms fixed + live-verified 2026-07-02)”](#9-ownerjoiner-federation-can-stay-broken-in-the-pure-no-restart-join-path-resolved--both-mechanisms-fixed--live-verified-2026-07-02) A live run (Brief 6 attempt-1, su-e7698: 2-frame, shared forceReFold `.deb`, real DHT) surfaced **owner(a)→joiner(b) content federation FAILING** in the plain join→write path with **no restart**: b’s `hive_members` roster stayed EMPTY for 270s+, so `decideMemberContentOp` dropped every owner op (b→a was fine). Code root-cause (su-0f0a4): `forceReFold` (`boot.ts`) fires **exactly once**, on the `rekey()`→pot-home rebind, then resets. If the owner’s `hive_members` op arrives at the joiner **after** that single re-fold (during drain), it is never re-applied — it stays dropped-in-the-home-window until a **restart or a later rekey**. This is consistent with Brief 5 (restart) PASSING (the restart re-folds) and means the earlier “proven live” runs (run33/34/35) may have included a restart/rekey rather than exercising the pure no-restart path. **Root cause (confirmed, su-2c799):** cross-process `opStateCache` staleness under `SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR`. `join-pot.ts` (MAIN process) commits the registry (`remote_hive:true` + `hive_slug`) and invalidates its OWN cache; but `rekey()` runs in the substrate SIDECAR process, whose warm `harness_registry` cache (2s TTL, kept hot by the sidecar’s constant reads) never saw that invalidation → it serves the STALE pre-join value → `joinerHiveHomeSlug` returns null → `resolveHiveHomeProjectionSlug` returns null → `next===prev(null)` → the rekey rebind block (boot.ts \~2599) SKIPS → `forceReFold` never fires → the member-slug projection binding latches → the owner’s `hive_members` rows drop forever → roster EMPTY. A restart cold-reads fresh at boot → binds correctly (why Brief 5 restart PASSED). Neither original candidate — it was a third mechanism (stale cross-process cache read at the resolve, not a re-fold-coverage or rebind-timing bug). **Status: FIX LANDED (su-2c799, WI-1378).** `resolveHiveHomeProjectionSlug` now calls `joinerHiveHomeSlug(ws, slug, { fresh: true })`, threaded through `loadHarnessRegistry({fresh})` → `readOperatorState({fresh})` to BYPASS the 2s cache on this one rare resolve path (hot-path callers keep the cache, so the seqscan perf win is preserved). A fresh PG read is guaranteed to see the committed write (join-pot awaits the `mutateRegistry` commit before the rekey RPC). **Second mechanism (WI-1544, the race bifurcation):** when the deterministic join-time binding resolved BEFORE the owner’s announce, the joiner’s pot-home projection conclusively rejected the owner core on the slug filter (origin=member-slug), membership chicken-and-egged, and A→B blacked out *permanently* (the rekey rescue was structurally unreachable — no binding transition). Fixed in `boot.ts`: `inJoinBootstrapWindow()` reclassifies a join-window `binding_invalid` as retryable/buffered instead of conclusive-reject, and the `scope_unresolved` buffer holds out-of-scope slug-filter frames while the pot-home projection slug is unresolved (WI-1544, resolved 2026-07-02; 41 dedicated tests in `boot.test.ts` + `announce-channel-multihive.test.ts`). **Live verification:** matrix run m1783013203 (2026-07-02) federated A→B on the FIRST poll across all 8 scenarios — no restart, no adaptive re-fold rescue needed. This limitation is closed. ### 10. Membership-lifecycle + residual trackers (P-011 verdicts, 2026-07-03) [Section titled “10. Membership-lifecycle + residual trackers (P-011 verdicts, 2026-07-03)”](#10-membership-lifecycle--residual-trackers-p-011-verdicts-2026-07-03) The post-min-bar backlog was given explicit verdicts under `shared-pot-p2p-release-readiness-2026-07-03` P-011 (full table: `shared-pot-release-testing/RELEASE-READINESS.md`). The standing ship-with-limitation rows, each with an accountable tracker: * **No un-revoke path (G8, WI-1855) — SHIP-WITH-LIMITATION, ratified.** Revocation is one-way; un-banning a member has no sanctioned flow. WI-1855’s acceptance criteria (a built un-revoke flow OR this owner-ratified permanent-limitation row) is satisfied by this row, hence its `resolved` tracker state — no code shipped for un-revoke itself, this is a documented-and-accepted gap, not a fix. ⚠️ **CORRECTED + RATIFIED (2026-07-09, WI-3566, closing the P-003 rest-lanes audit finding):** this row previously stated the sanctioned workaround (re-invite as a fresh device/epoch) “must NOT retro-grant cut epochs” — **verified FALSE against the actual implementation, and that old caveat is now removed as simply wrong.** `grantEpochKeysToMembers` (`pot-epoch-boundary-wiring.ts`) is a ratified v1 correctness call (D-009, 2026-06-19/2026-07-04): ANY newly-admitted member — including a re-invited fresh device for a previously-revoked identity — is granted wrapped keys for **every** epoch `[0..current]`, by design (pinned by `seed-past-epoch-key-guarantee.test.ts`; a current-epoch-only policy is explicitly a *deferred future forward-secrecy policy*, not implemented, and not currently planned work). **Ratified (WI-3566, superseding the earlier “owner design decision needed” framing): un-revoke-via-reinvite IS, and is meant to be, a full history restore** — the returning member gets every epoch key minted during their ban, including the K-cut boundary epoch that revoked them, identically to any brand-new member. There is no guard distinguishing “returning previously-revoked identity” from “genuinely new member” at grant time, and none is planned — this is the accepted v1 behavior, not a gap awaiting a fix. Treat un-revoke-via-reinvite as **equivalent to inviting a brand-new member with full history access** — NOT as a partial/forward-only restore. * **Membership teardown doesn’t federate (G24/G27, WI-1857) — SHIP-WITH-LIMITATION, ratified.** Dissolve publishes no membership tombstone (peers’ rows orphan out by TTL) and a leaver’s `hive_members` row persists on peers. Pinned by `lifecycle-membership-teardown.gap.integration.test.ts`; the read-plane mitigation (epoch K-cut) is live-proven, so this is a hygiene gap, not a security hole. Same as WI-1855: `resolved` reflects this ratified doc row, not a built fix. * **revoke() Hypercore session leak (G9, WI-1856) — FIXED 2026-07-05.** `openRemoteLog`’s `RemoteLog` now implements `close()` (`core.close?.()`), and `boot.ts`’s `revoke()` captures the `AdmittedLog` before deleting it from `admitted` and fire-and-forget closes it (deliberately not awaited — awaiting added multi-second live-replicator teardown latency that timed out an unrelated pinned test). Verified: `boot.test.ts` 43/43, `revocation-prior-row-semantics.test.ts` 1/1, `peer-log.test.ts` 4/4, a new pinning test added, `tsc --noEmit` clean on the 5 changed files (`peer-log.ts`/`read-merge.ts`/`boot.ts` + the two test files). * **Usage-events metering is machine-local (G2, WI-1858)** — the `contributor_usage_events` capture trigger is deliberately deferred to the GA migration (completeness-guard exemption until then). * **From-repo joiner incremental federation (WI-971) — RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-09 (p2p-rest-lanes-2026-07-09 P-005, WI-3542).** The outbox drain is never wired for joined/created pot harnesses (WI-259 was closed as its duplicate); the fix (join-pot.ts step “2c/2c′” — re-key the home-VIEW and every joined member onto the Pot-pubkey topic right after the registry view/identity materialize, instead of waiting for a process restart) was already unit-tested with mocked deps (`join-pot.test.ts`’s “2c′ home-view boot/rekey” block), but the earlier `resolved` state-flip carried no recorded completion evidence. New evidence: `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/join-hive-from-repo-incremental-federation.integration.test.ts` drives `joinHiveAsView` against a REAL, migrated Postgres (env-routed `getOrgPg`, the `owner-content-to-joiner-faithful.repro.integration.test.ts` pattern) with `mutateHarnessRegistry`/`loadHarnessRegistry` UNMOCKED, and a `rekeyHarness` stub that itself performs a real registry read at call time — proving (1) the home-view + member registry rows genuinely commit to Postgres, not an in-memory fake, and (2) the 2c′/2c rekey calls fire, in order (home view first, then every member), strictly AFTER that commit is visible — the exact ordering bug WI-971 closed. Green: `npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts packages/operator-core/lib/harness/join-hive-from-repo-incremental-federation.integration.test.ts` → 1 passed (1), 1292ms. **Scope note (fallback path, deliberate):** this proof is registry+ordering only — it stubs the from-repo `joinLink` (GitHub clone/attestation, unrelated to WI-971) and does not boot two REAL substrate peers through `joinHiveAsView` end-to-end to show a post-join content write federates incrementally with zero process restart. That remaining live-two-peer content-roundtrip proof is tracked separately — see the follow-up work item filed alongside this test (search `work_items` for “WI-971 live two-peer from-repo content roundtrip”). **CLOSED — live two-peer proof landed 2026-07-25 (WI-5775/WI-5628).** Two live `two-instance-hive-from-repo-smoke.sh` runs (plain, and with the gate’s exact `WITNESS_PROBE=1 PAPERCUSP_FLAG_PAPERCUSP_HIVE_REKEY=1` flags) against a real built `.deb` in sidecar-bundle fallback mode both report `OVERALL: PASS`: create/announce/discover/join/join-clone all PASS, and — the WI-971-specific proof — `federate-A→B`, `federate-B→A`, and `federate-A→B #2` (continuous, post-join) all PASS. `live-federation-gate.sh`’s `SKIP_FROMREPO` default stays `1` (a separate, standing decision — WI-5629 — not reopened by this fix), but its stale “expected WI-971 red” framing has been corrected: a from-repo RED is now a genuine regression. (The gate-flags run’s WITNESS sub-probe separately surfaced an unrelated AK-ban enforcement gap — tracked as WI-5783, not a WI-971 regression.) ### 11. Boot-window / silent-re-federation data-loss class for CDC-captured tables (WI-5441) — CONSCIOUSLY WAIVED for public release (2026-07-25, WI-5764) [Section titled “11. Boot-window / silent-re-federation data-loss class for CDC-captured tables (WI-5441) — CONSCIOUSLY WAIVED for public release (2026-07-25, WI-5764)”](#11-boot-window--silent-re-federation-data-loss-class-for-cdc-captured-tables-wi-5441--consciously-waived-for-public-release-2026-07-25-wi-5764) **Symptom (demonstrated live, 5+ independent repros across 2026-07-18/19):** a row written on the origin peer occasionally federates with **zero** corresponding `harness_shared.substrate_outbox` entry, ever — the write is silently and **permanently** non-federating, with no error, no stall-detect signal, and no reconciliation pass to catch it. First reproduced on `plan_item_assignments` (the generic `capture_substrate_outbox()` capture path, migs 359/446); the mechanism is not table-specific, so any table riding that generic capture function is exposed in principle — most consequentially `harness_shared.work_items` (features/issues), which rides the sibling `capture_work_items_outbox()` function (mig 375/423) and was flagged at filing time as the path where this class would be most damaging (the shared-pot editing surface). No work-items-family repro has been observed; this is a structural risk, not a demonstrated second instance. **What is CONFIRMED, after an exhaustive multi-session investigation (WI-5441 posts, 2026-07-18 22:03 → 2026-07-19 17:10, 5+ agents):** * The federation-capture trigger (`capture_substrate_outbox_trg`) is always attached and enabled well before the losing write in every repro — a “trigger not yet attached at boot” race was directly falsified by OID/timing forensics on 3 separate runs. * No online-guard, no `session_replication_role` override, no ON CONFLICT short-circuit, no swallowed exception, and no GC-deletion timing explains a bare local-origin INSERT losing its capture entry. * The clearest live-caught instance (real production content, plan `health-tab-v2-2026-07-12` items P-013–015, not the synthetic seed probe): a row’s `origin` flips `remote→local` with **byte-identical** federated content (no assignee/assigned\_ts/strategy/note change) and produces **no** outbox row — i.e. something **re-applies an already-materialized op through the projection’s `writeToPg`** with a provenance context that resolves `origin` to `'local'` on a write that is not actually a fresh local edit. The leading (unconfirmed) hypothesis is a periodic reconciliation/re-fold pass constructing `OpEnvelope`s directly from DB rows rather than from a peer-log op, without threading `provenance` — see WI-5441 post 52971 for the exact code seam to instrument (`writeToPg`’s `provenance?.origin ?? 'local'` fallback, `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/projections/ plan-item-assignments.ts`). * **Root-cause identification requires live rig instrumentation** (a debug capture trigger armed from before boot) — static code reading across every receive-side call site (own-log snapshot compaction, backfill-local-state, the epoch decrypt gate, `withHiveHomeApplyGuard`, `resolveOpProvenance`’s fallback) has been exhausted without a positive catch of the exact writer; see WI-5441 posts 52968/52971/52980 for what has been ruled out and why. **What WAS fixed 2026-07-25 (WI-5764, defensive hardening — NOT proven to be this class’s root cause):** a genuinely real, separate boot-ordering race was found and fixed in the **native `:5432` operator host** path (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts` + `host-bootstrap.ts`): `startRequestServers()` previously ran unconditionally immediately after the fire-and-forget `runBootstrap()` call, with no ordering guarantee against the still-running migration apply — so an HTTP write could in principle reach a table before a still-applying migration set had created its capture trigger. Fixed by gating `startRequestServers()` on a new boot-gate flag (`markMigrationsAppliedForRequestGate`/`awaitMigrationsAppliedForRequestGate`, `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/boot-gate.ts`) that flips the instant `applyPendingMigrationsAtBoot()` returns; a request-only host (`PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0`) or a timeout degrades open (log + serve anyway) so this can never wedge boot. **Caveat found while implementing this fix, worth recording explicitly:** the live-fed-gate / local-matrix rig that produced every WI-5441 repro above boots the **desktop/embedded-pg entrypoint** (`apps/operator/bin/serve.ts` → `startEmbeddedPostgresServer`), which `await`s its own migration-apply step to completion **before** `runBootstrap()` or `serve()` ever run — so that specific race does **not** explain the observed reds (consistent with WI-5441 post 52911’s own finding that the capture trigger already existed \~4 minutes before the losing write in that repro). The hono-host.ts fix is real, low-risk, and worth having (it protects the native `:3070`/`:3170` dev-box hosts, a different boot path with the same class of race), but it is **not** the fix for this section’s demonstrated defect — treat the two as separate, both real. **The waiver.** Given (a) the mechanism is narrowed but not pinned without a dedicated live-instrumentation session, (b) every prior attempt at that session was resource-constrained by the shared single-tenant rig, and (c) no second instance has been observed on the work-items family despite it being structurally exposed — **this class ships as a known, documented limitation for the public release**, not a release blocker, on the following basis: 1. It requires a specific, uncommon interleaving (a re-apply of already-correct content racing the capture path) — not a routine write path failure. 2. The loss is confined to metadata/assignment-shaped federated tables observed so far (`plan_item_assignments`); no core content (features/issues/plans/coord threads) loss has been demonstrated. 3. **The durable fix direction is known** (WI-5441 post 52911): a reconciliation pass that compares TABLE STATE across peers for CDC-captured tables (rows present on the publisher, absent/stale on the joiner) rather than trusting outbox history alone — this is a bigger, higher-risk change (a new periodic cross-peer state-diff mechanism) appropriately scoped as its own follow-up, not something to rush unattended against the release-critical gate rig. **Tracking.** WI-5441 stays **open, `blocked`, claim-held** with this waiver recorded — do not silently re-close it as resolved. Any future session with a free rig slot should pick up the live-instrumentation step exactly where post 52980 left off (a fresh rig with BOTH an INSERT and UPDATE debug trigger armed from before boot, per the first WI-5441 checkpoint). WI-5764 (this waiver + the defensive hono-host.ts fix) is the P-410 disposition for public release. *** ## Public-release checklist [Section titled “Public-release checklist”](#public-release-checklist) **Minimum bar to call cross-machine federation “public-release-ready”:** | Brief | Gate | Current status | | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **1** | Rig foundation (reusable lib, 3-frame, scenario drivers) | ✅ DONE + live-validated (run35) | | **2** | LIVE multi-member (3+) fanout | ✅ **OWNER-RATIFIED option B (2026-07-01, D-006 @ federation-release-hardening-relaunch-2026-07-01)** — min-bar = in-process multimember repro (green) + 2-node live briefs; true 3-machine fanout stays a documented known limitation gated on cap >2 servers + a 3rd distinct gh identity (scenario `deb-hetzner-brief2.sh` stays runnable) | | **3** | LIVE revocation + epoch K-cut | ✅ **DONE — LIVE PASS 2026-07-02** (su-f5d28, 2 Hetzner VMs, public DHT): baseline federated → owner ban accepted (revokedPubkeys) → post-ban content CUT OFF (\~90s negative assert) → pre-ban content stayed readable (not retroactive). # Federation rig — restart / recovery runbook (wedged smokes, stale ports, leaked VMs)

> How to recover the two-instance federation rig when a run wedges or leaves debris: reap ONLY dead runs (reap-orphans.sh) or one run (cleanup-run.sh) — never a broad pkill/rm (EI-1739); clear stale Xvfb / testnet-DHT / orphaned sidecars; free or self-discover wedged ports (the WI-754 self-heal); reset/relaunch the linux-test-vm VMs (vmctl); restart the scheduled live-federation-gate; and — when a peer is up but silently local-only (announces nothing, discovers nothing) — restore its MISSING gh auth, the most common dead-link cause after a VM reset (WI-757).

The **federation rig** = the `papercusp-desktop/bin/*federation*.sh` / `bin/two-instance-*.sh` smokes, their shared assert core `papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh`, and the `scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl` VM driver. Each run boots one or two **isolated** desktop/sidecar instances (own `$HOME` → own `~/.papercusp`, embedded-PG, corestore, ports) and asserts they federate. When a run crashes, times out, or is killed, it can leave debris — orphaned sidecars / embedded-PG / `hyperdht/testnet` nodes, a stale `Xvfb`, a held port, or a powered-on VM. This is the recovery runbook. Never broad-pkill / broad-rm — EI-1739 The box runs **many rigs concurrently** (the fleet + the scheduled gate). A `pkill -f papercusp-desktop`, `pkill -f <rig-name>`, or `rm -rf /tmp/<rig>.*` matches **every** run and crashes a sibling’s **live** run mid-flight (this is exactly the EI-1739 collision: a glob over all runs + a name-wide pkill deleted a sibling’s `$WORK` mid-`initdb` and killed its processes). Always use the **run-scoped** reapers below — they refuse anything that isn’t a single per-run `$WORK` dir, so they can never touch a live sibling. ## 1. Reap debris (the safe, default first move) [Section titled “1. Reap debris (the safe, default first move)”](#1-reap-debris-the-safe-default-first-move) 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop


# Reap ONLY dead runs (processes gone, older than the 5-min startup window).
# A live sibling always has referencing processes → never touched. Safe anytime,
# concurrently, by anyone.
bin/reap-orphans.sh                 # reap all dead runs
bin/reap-orphans.sh --dry-run       # show what WOULD be reaped, touch nothing


# Clean up exactly ONE known run's leftovers (you have its $WORK):
bin/cleanup-run.sh /tmp/pot-fromrepo-smoke.AbC123
```
 These wrap `fed_reap_orphans` / `fed_cleanup_run` in `federation-asserts.sh`. The rig’s `$WORK` prefixes are registered in `FED_RIG_TMP_PREFIXES` (e.g. `/tmp/pot-fromrepo-smoke.`, `/tmp/merge-smoke.`, `/tmp/vm-fed.`, `/tmp/deb-hzfed.`) — **add a new prefix there** if you add a rig, so the reapers keep seeing it. The reapers exclude the calling shell + its ancestors, so running them from inside an agent shell never false-flags or kills the caller. ## 2. Stale `Xvfb`, testnet-DHT, and orphaned sidecars [Section titled “2. Stale Xvfb, testnet-DHT, and orphaned sidecars”](#2-stale-xvfb-testnet-dht-and-orphaned-sidecars) The smokes run headless on a dedicated `Xvfb` display (never the user’s `:0` — see `fed_ensure_display` / `fed_fresh_display`) and spin a host `hyperdht/testnet` DHT (`fed_start_testnet_dht`). Both, plus the instance sidecars, are tracked in `FED_KILL_PIDS` and torn down by the run’s `EXIT` trap + `fed_cleanup_scoped`. After a hard kill (trap never fired) `reap-orphans.sh` (§1) catches the ones whose argv references the dead run’s `$WORK` (testnet nodes ride `$WORK` on argv exactly so the scoped reaper finds them). A **truly orphaned** `Xvfb` whose run dir is already gone is the one case the scoped reaper can’t attribute. Identify it by display number and kill **only that display** — never a bare `pkill -f Xvfb`: 
```sh
pgrep -af 'Xvfb :2(5[0-9]|99)'      # the smoke/gate display range (e.g. :99, :250, :252)
kill <pid>                          # the specific stale Xvfb, by pid
```
 ## 3. Wedged / mismatched ports [Section titled “3. Wedged / mismatched ports”](#3-wedged--mismatched-ports) Two port strategies are in play: * **Pre-assigned (robust):** the sidecar-bundle path + `deb-hetzner-federation.sh` pick a free port with `fed_pick_free_port`-style `ss` probing and pass it as `PAPERCUSP_HONO_PORT` / `PAPERCUSP_PG_PORT` — the instance binds exactly that. * **Dynamic + discovered:** the packaged `.deb`/Tauri path lets the instance pick its own ports; the rig **discovers** them. If a port is genuinely **held** by a dead run’s leftover, §1 frees it (killing the holder). To see what an instance is actually listening on, the rig now dumps it on failure (`fed_dump_instance_diag`: listening TCP ports + app-log tail). Manually: 
```sh
ss -tlnpH | sort -u        # all listeners + owning pid (own-user pids shown)
```
 ## 4. VMs (the `vmctl` linux-test-vm + the build VMs) [Section titled “4. VMs (the vmctl linux-test-vm + the build VMs)”](#4-vms-the-vmctl-linux-test-vm--the-build-vms) The `--vms` federation runs (`bin/vm-federation.sh`) drive disposable Ubuntu VMs via `scripts/linux-test-vm/vmctl`. A wedged VM: 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
./vmctl status fed-a            # VM up? app up? operator port? disk?
./vmctl reset  fed-a            # recreate a pristine overlay from golden
./vmctl down   fed-a           # graceful power-off (teardown)
./vmctl up     fed-a           # boot a fresh overlay
```
 `vm-federation.sh` resets + reinstalls per VM by default (the clean-boot acceptance run); pass `--no-reset` to reuse overlays while iterating, and `--keep-up` to leave the VMs running for debugging. For a wedged **Mac** VM parked at the OpenCore picker / holding SPICE ports, recover via **QMP, never pkill** — see [mac-vm-qmp-recovery](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mac-vm-qmp-recovery). General VM inventory + disk discipline: [build-system/vms](/internal/docs/build-system/vms). ## 5. The scheduled gate (`live-federation-gate.sh`) [Section titled “5. The scheduled gate (live-federation-gate.sh)”](#5-the-scheduled-gate-live-federation-gatesh) `papercusp-desktop/bin/live-federation-gate.sh` runs the smokes on a schedule on a quiet box and files an EI on any RED (the green-rig/red-binary guard, WI-261/P-013). It: * runs a **hermetic \~2s assert-core self-test first** (WI-754: `bin/lib/federation-asserts.selftest.sh` — proves the port-discovery logic before spending minutes on smokes; a fail exits `GATE: RED` with a clear message). Set `GATE_SKIP_SELFTEST=1` to skip it. * **SKIPs (not fails)** when 1-min load exceeds `LOAD_GATE` — the smokes get killed under load and false-RED below the kill threshold. Better to skip and retry next window than false-RED or pile onto a busy box. **`LOAD_GATE` is now core-aware (2026-07-03, P-013):** `max(15, 3*nproc/8)` — an absolute `15` never fired on the 128-core fleet box (it sat well below the box’s ordinary operating load), reproducing the exact “gate never runs” class P-013 exists to kill; a first core-aware cut at `nproc/4` *still* undershot the observed fleet-era floor (35-46). If a mid-run load spike pushes the 1-min load above the new `STORM_GATE` (default `nproc*0.6`) by the time the verdict is computed, a would-be FAIL is **downgraded to `SKIPPED-STORM`** (no EI filed) instead of a false-RED — the exact failure mode a load-94 fleet storm caused before this existed. * **Fresh-exit + staleness guard (2026-07-03, P-013):** a GREEN younger than `GATE_SUCCESS_TTL_H` (default 22h) makes the NEXT window’s run a no-op exit before the self-test even runs (hourly timer, \~daily actual smoke run). If no GREEN has landed in `GATE_STALE_DAYS` (default 3) — every window either load-skipped, storm-downgraded, all-legs-skipped, or failed — the gate files a **loud staleness EI** itself: silence must never look like green. Set `GATE_FORCE=1` to ignore the freshness TTL and force a run now (still storm-downgrade-protected if the box saturates mid-run). * **EI filing now requires a superuser bearer** (2026-07-03, WI-1841 follow-up to WI-1861): `?superuser=1` on the MCP URL alone is not sufficient — the handler also needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` matching `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` (`GATE_SUPERUSER_TOKEN_PATH` overrides the path). A missing/short token degrades gracefully to log-only, same as before; it is not fatal. * **Build provenance is stamped** (2026-07-03, WI-1861): each rebuild logs the working-tree `HEAD` + dirty-file count, so a “torn-tree build” red (the shared checkout was mid-edit by a fleet peer at build time — unreproducible at the next build, byte-identical blueprints) is diagnosable instead of a mystery. * **`log()` now writes to stderr, not stdout** (2026-07-03, load-bearing P-013 fix): the verdict logic reads a smoke leg’s PASS/FAIL via `$(...)` command substitution, and with `log` on stdout the captured string became `"log-line\nPASS|FAIL"`, so `[ "$RES" = FAIL ]` could never match — a genuine content-matrix FAIL was silently masked out of every verdict until this fix. journald still captures both streams, so nothing is lost. * **The from-repo leg’s known-red is WI-971, not WI-259** — WI-259 was closed as a duplicate of WI-971 (outbox drain never wired for joined/created pot harnesses); WI-280/WI-1666 are resolved. A content-matrix FAIL whose only `✗` lines match the WI-971 backfill/incr-B→A signature is downgraded to `PASS-971` (not a clean pass — WI-971 remains open) rather than a red. * **A new `local-matrix` leg** (P-002, no-op until `bin/local-matrix.sh` exists) runs the full containerized 8-scenario matrix on a weekly cadence (`MATRIX_TTL_H`, default 144h), and only on a window whose content-matrix smoke already passed. * **All-legs-skipped is NOT recorded as green** — if load-gate/staleness logic let a window through but every leg still SKIPPED (e.g. `SKIP_MATRIX=1 SKIP_FROMREPO=1`), the gate now exits `GATE: SKIPPED (no legs ran)` rather than silently counting as a pass. * **Run-dir retention (WI-3087, 2026-07-05):** each run’s `/tmp/live-fed-gate-*` dir (the unpacked `dpkg-deb -R` tree + the repacked gate `.deb`) used to be left behind forever — \~3.5GB per heavy run, 67 dirs / 111GB observed before the disk filled. The gate now keeps only the newest `GATE_KEEP_RUNS` (default 5) run dirs at the top of every invocation, and additionally removes its own `pkg/` tree right after a successful repack. Restart / re-run it manually on a quiet box: 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop
bin/reap-orphans.sh                                   # clear any prior debris first
LOAD_GATE=48 bin/live-federation-gate.sh              # raise only for a dedicated/idle host
GATE_NO_FILE=1 SKIP_FROMREPO=1 bin/live-federation-gate.sh   # log-only, skip the WI-971-RED leg
GATE_FORCE=1 bin/live-federation-gate.sh              # ignore the freshness TTL, force a run now
```
 It’s a routine — check / re-arm it via `routines:list` / `routines:set` (it does **not** push the live `:3070`; it builds + boots isolated instances). ## 6. Peer is up but silently local-only — missing gh auth (WI-757) [Section titled “6. Peer is up but silently local-only — missing gh auth (WI-757)”](#6-peer-is-up-but-silently-local-only--missing-gh-auth-wi-757) The single most common reason the live link is dead after a `vmctl reset` / re-image (§4): the peer has **no GitHub auth**, so it never federates — yet it boots, serves its API, and looks healthy. The federation **announce binds the device identity to a GitHub user** (`local-announce-identity.ts`): with no `gh` token, `resolveLocalAnnounceIdentity` throws and `boot.ts`’s swarm-join catch treats it as **“stay local-only — don’t federate.”** The peer then **announces nothing and discovers nothing**, silently — there is no loud signal; the only tell is `reachablePeers: 0` on an explicit announce. (This masquerades as a deep substrate/admission/cursor bug — check auth FIRST.) Symptoms: * `GET /api/discovery/pots` on the peer returns `count: 0`. * `POST /api/discovery/set-pot {visibility:"public"}` and `POST /api/harness/pots/from-repo` return `announced:false, reachablePeers:0, error:"local-announce-identity: gh not authenticated"`. * Cross-machine: the peer’s pots never appear on any other peer’s directory. Check it FIRST: 
```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-linux -p <sshPort> tester@127.0.0.1 'gh auth status'
# "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts" → this IS your dead link.
```
 Restore (reversible; **no operator restart needed** — `pot-directory-boot` lazily re-wires the directory on the next browse/announce): 
```sh
# from the HOST (gh-authed); pipe the token over ssh STDIN, never argv:
printf '%s' "$(gh auth token)" | \
  ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-linux -p <sshPort> tester@127.0.0.1 'gh auth login --with-token'
# then re-announce (or just browse) → announced:true, reachablePeers>0
```
 Use the identity the peer historically announced as (its `harness_shared.shared_presence.github_user_id`) — for fed-a that is `papercupai` (279242982); fed-b uses a different account. An operator-process restart **preserves** `~/.config/gh`; only a full **VM re-image** wipes it — so prefer a process restart over a reset, and re-auth after any reset. Coordinate a restart A restart to force a swarm re-peer must be coordinated with whoever owns the live federation/self-heal work (FED-2) — don’t restart a peer another agent is actively investigating. The durable fix (persist/restore auth across restart + a loud no-identity health signal) is tracked in WI-757. ### 6b. Loopback smoke gets 0 peer dials — ambient fleet DHT env leaking in (2026-07-03) [Section titled “6b. Loopback smoke gets 0 peer dials — ambient fleet DHT env leaking in (2026-07-03)”](#6b-loopback-smoke-gets-0-peer-dials--ambient-fleet-dht-env-leaking-in-2026-07-03) A different silently-local-only cause, specific to `fed_local_launch` / `fed_local_launch_sidecar` (`bin/lib/federation-asserts.sh`) launches on a **fleet shell**: fleet desktop sessions carry ambient `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST=<bridge-ip>` / `PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP=<bridge-ip:port>` for the tower↔VM rig, and a loopback smoke that inherits either one swarm-binds/bootstraps on the bridge instead of the loopback DHT the smoke actually spun up — so peers never dial each other (0 `peer_connected` fleet-wide, found 2026-07-03). Both launch primitives now **force-empty** `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST`/`PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` before `"$@"` — a caller that *wants* either passes it explicitly in the trailing `VAR=val` args, which win over the forced-empty default. If you’re troubleshooting a hand-rolled smoke that calls these primitives directly and it can’t see its peer, check the calling shell’s environment for `PAPERCUSP_DHT_HOST`/`PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP` before suspecting the substrate. ## 7. Driving the live fed VMs — `fed.sh` (port self-discovery, WI-754) [Section titled “7. Driving the live fed VMs — fed.sh (port self-discovery, WI-754)”](#7-driving-the-live-fed-vms--fedsh-port-self-discovery-wi-754) `papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh` is the **versioned** driver for the 2-machine fed-a / fed-b VMs — the reliable replacement for the ad-hoc `/tmp/fed.sh` that **hardcoded the VMs’ dynamic operator/PG ports**. Those ports are picked fresh on every operator restart and old listeners linger, so a hardcoded (or even “latest `[serve]` log line”) port goes stale and silently hits the wrong / a dead listener (EI-3409 / WI-559 burned \~30 min on exactly this). The versioned script **discovers the LIVE ports on each call**: it SSHes in (stable host-forward port), gathers candidate loopback ports, and picks the operator = the one answering `GET /api/desktop/preflight` with **2xx** and PG = the one that accepts a `harness_admin` psql — so it survives app/VM restarts with no edits. 
```sh
cd papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm
./fed.sh a ports                       # show the discovered operator/PG ports
./fed.sh a sql  "select count(*) from harness_features"
./fed.sh a api  GET /api/discovery/pots
./fed.sh a mcp  pot:report '{"pot":"…"}'
./fed.sh a ssh  'gh auth status'       # raw ssh (used by §6's gh-auth restore)
./fed.sh b rediscover                  # force a fresh probe (after a restart)
```
 `sql` uses the guest’s own `psql` if it’s on `PATH`, else the app’s bundled `sidecar/bin/psql`. Real client binaries have shipped with the app since 2026-07-07 — an install built before that date shipped a broken `pg_wrapper` shim instead, so on an older install run a fresh `vmctl install` before relying on `fed.sh a sql`. Ports are cached per-VM under `~/.papercusp/fed-rig-ports.<vm>` for `FED_PORT_TTL` (default 600s); `rediscover` (or deleting the cache) forces a fresh probe. SSH host-forward ports default to `2225` (a) / `2226` (b) — override with `FED_SSH_A` / `FED_SSH_B`. Cross-machine witness pots must be repo-bound For a live two-machine federation witness, do not create an arbitrary repo-less throwaway with `pot:create`. The cross-machine join path joins the owner’s per-member GitHub links (`joinHiveAsView` parses each member link and clones the member repo). A repo-less `pot:create` home has no member links for the peer to join, so the peer never subscribes to that pot’s topic and owner writes have no remote log to arrive on. Use `pot:create_from_repo` (or an existing repo-bound pot with a joined peer member) for B8/B10-style ban, dissolve, grant, and receipt witnesses. A valid witness setup is: owner box owns the pot, peer box has joined at least one repo-bound member, then drive the federation action. EI-3409 — workspace-scoped MCP writes Superuser MCP resolves `ctx.workspaceId='*'` while the HTTP routes/queue use `'default'`, so a pot created via `mcp` lands in the wrong workspace and the routes return `not_owner_swarm`. For a workspace-scoped WRITE tool (`pot:create` / `pot:takedown` / `pot:report` / `pot:moderation_*`), pass `"workspace":"default"` in the args — or set `FED_MCP_WS=default` and `fed.sh` injects it for you (opt-in; off by default because blanket injection breaks READ tools whose schema rejects an unknown `workspace` key). The durable fix (superuser ctx resolving the concrete workspace) is tracked on **EI-3409**. ## 8. Operator workspace-scoped HOME silently breaks BOTH the superuser token AND gh-auth (D-007) [Section titled “8. Operator workspace-scoped HOME silently breaks BOTH the superuser token AND gh-auth (D-007)”](#8-operator-workspace-scoped-home-silently-breaks-both-the-superuser-token-and-gh-auth-d-007) A peer can look healthy (API up, boots, serves requests) while `pot:membership_decide` fails `no_owner_identity` and `fed.sh <vm> mcp`/`api` fail `superuser_invalid_bearer` — **without any VM reset or gh-auth wipe (§6) having happened.** Root cause, isolated live on fed-a (2026-06-25, plan `shared-hive-public-release-2026-06-22` D-007): the VM’s operator process was launched with a **workspace-scoped `HOME`** (`/home/tester/.papercusp-workspaces/default`), not the login user’s real home (`/home/tester`). Two independent failures trace to the same single cause: 1. **`superuser_invalid_bearer`** — the operator reads its own superuser token from `$HOME/.papercusp/superuser-token` using **its own process `HOME`**, but `fed.sh`’s `api`/`mcp` verbs SSH in and read `~/.papercusp/superuser-token`, which expands against the **SSH login shell’s** `HOME` (`/home/tester`). When the two differ, the script reads the wrong file (or nothing) and the token never matches. 2. **`pot:membership_decide` → `no_owner_identity`** — `resolveLocalGithubIdentity` shells `gh auth token`, which reads `$HOME/.config/gh/hosts.yml` under the **operator’s** `HOME`. `gh auth login` run from an interactive SSH session authenticates the **login shell’s** `HOME` (`/home/tester/.config/gh`) — a different, workspace-UNSCOPED path — so the operator’s own `gh auth token` call sees “not authenticated” even though `ssh ... gh auth status` reports logged in. Diagnose it by comparing the two: 
```sh
# the operator process's ACTUAL HOME (what matters for both failures):
ssh ... "tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/\$(pgrep -f serve.mjs)/environ | sed -n 's/^HOME=//p'"
# the SSH login shell's HOME (what fed.sh's naive ~/... reads resolve against):
ssh ... 'echo $HOME'
```
 If they differ, that mismatch — not a dead peer, not a wiped gh-auth (§6) — is your cause. **Session fix that worked (2026-06-25, fed-a):** derive the token path from the operator’s *real* `HOME` via `/proc/<pid>/environ` instead of trusting the login shell’s `~`, and symlink the operator’s `.config/gh` to wherever the login shell’s `gh auth login` actually wrote it (`ln -s /home/tester/.config/gh /home/tester/.papercusp-workspaces/default/.config/gh`). Both are **session-local fixes, not code** — this doc’s own fed.sh copy still reads the plain `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` (verified 2026-07-26; no `/proc/<pid>/environ` derivation is committed), so **if you hit either symptom again, re-apply the same two workarounds** (or land the durable fix: patch `api`/`mcp` in `papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh` to resolve the token path off the operator’s own `HOME`, not the login shell’s). Product concern, not just a rig artifact D-007 flagged this as worth verifying beyond the rig: if the **shipped desktop sidecar** ever launches its operator with a workspace-scoped `HOME` that lacks its own `~/.config/gh`, real users would hit the identical `no_owner_identity` on hive admit — not just this test VM. Unconfirmed either way as of this writing; check the desktop launcher’s `HOME`/env wiring before assuming it can’t happen off the rig. ## 9. Fed-b substrate-boot saturation — a “clean restart” needs the safe reapers, not hand-killed PIDs (D-008/D-009, WI-779) [Section titled “9. Fed-b substrate-boot saturation — a “clean restart” needs the safe reapers, not hand-killed PIDs (D-008/D-009, WI-779)”](#9-fed-b-substrate-boot-saturation--a-clean-restart-needs-the-safe-reapers-not-hand-killed-pids-d-008d-009-wi-779) A joiner VM that has accumulated many ad-hoc test hives/harnesses across repeated rig sessions can hit `[hyperbee-substrate] (<ws>::<slug>) failed: boot timeout after 30000ms` for **every** harness on its next boot — swarm peering looks fine (`peer_connected` fires), but nothing ever merges, because the substrate that would carry the roster/content never finishes coming up. Root-caused live on fed-b (D-008): `boot-all.ts` fanned out an **unbounded `Promise.all`** across every harness, so a joiner with many members saturates a shared boot resource and **every** substrate — not just the newest ones — misses the 30s window (witnessed: 11 concurrent harnesses → all fail; 2 → boots in \~5.5s). Fixed durably (WI-779, D-009): a bounded-concurrency mapper (default 4, override via `PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY`) plus a test asserting peak in-flight ≤ the cap (`boot-all.test.ts`). The code fix means a **fresh** join no longer self-saturates. But a VM that is *already* sitting on a large pile of accumulated cross-workspace test harnesses (the state D-008 hit) still boots slowly and is worth cleaning up before the next witness run — and that clean-up is exactly the situation this runbook’s own §1/§4 danger box already warns about: * **Don’t** `ssh <vm> 'pkill -f serve.mjs'` / hand-`kill` PIDs found via a loose `pgrep` to force a “clean” fed-b. A hand-rolled kill-by-PID is fragile in precisely the way EI-1739 (§1) already documents for this rig: a stale or reused PID, a grep that also matches a concurrent sibling run’s process, or a kill that misses the embedded-PG/corestore child and leaves a lock behind — any of which either kills the wrong thing or leaves debris that makes the **next** boot slower still (compounding the exact saturation D-008 hit). * **Do** use the scoped tools this runbook already provides: `bin/reap-orphans.sh` (§1) to clear dead-run debris, or `vmctl reset fed-b` (§4) for a genuinely clean overlay when you want to shed the accumulated harness pile entirely — both are run-scoped and safe on a box running other live rigs. * If you only need fewer *concurrent boots*, not a clean VM, `PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY` (lower than the default 4) trades boot latency for headroom on an already-loaded joiner — cheaper than a reset when you just need one more witness run to fit inside the 30s window. ## Quick reference [Section titled “Quick reference”](#quick-reference) | symptom | do | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | drive a live fed VM (stale `/tmp/fed.sh` ports) | `scripts/linux-test-vm/fed.sh <a\|b> ports\|sql\|api\|mcp` (§7, WI-754) | | crashed/timed-out run left debris | `bin/reap-orphans.sh` (§1) | | one known run’s `$WORK` to clean | `bin/cleanup-run.sh <WORK>` (§1) | | “API never came up” / wrong port | now self-heals (WI-754, §3);
