Two smaller corollaries fall out of the same incident: * **“Republish to the same URL” is only executable for an artifact the account OWNS.** The `Artifact` update flow takes a `url` and requires ownership; a deleted or someone-else’s artifact cannot be targeted, so a plan that *prescribes* a same-URL republish can be unexecutable in principle, not just inconvenient. * **Check ownership with `Artifact { action:'list', scope:'all' }`, not `scope:'mine'`.** The default omits artifacts shared *with* the account, so a `scope:'mine'` miss cannot distinguish “not yours” from “not there”. Only the `scope:'all'` miss plus a `WebFetch` not-found settles it. ## Caveats on the cache [Section titled “Caveats on the cache”](#caveats-on-the-cache) * **It is a cache, not an archive.** It lives under the session directory and survives only as long as that directory does. Recovering from it is a rescue, not a retention strategy — the first thing to do with recovered content is put it somewhere permanent. * **The publishing agent’s directory is the one that has it.** On a fleet, that may not be you. `sessions:search` will tell you *which* agent published it (search for the URL); the file then lives under that agent’s `ownerId`. * **The file is rendered HTML**, i.e. post-publish output, not your source. Strip tags to recover the prose; structure (headings, tables) survives cleanly. ## Recovering the text [Section titled “Recovering the text”](#recovering-the-text) 
```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, html
F = "<the artifact-*.html path>"
s = open(F, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
# optional: narrow to one section, e.g. s[s.index('<section id="borrow">'):]
s = re.sub(r'<(h[1-6])[^>]*>', r'\n\n### ', s)
s = re.sub(r'</(h[1-6])>', '\n', s)
s = re.sub(r'<code[^>]*>|</code>', '`', s)
s = re.sub(r'<(li|p|dt|dd|div)[^>]*>|<br\s*/?>', '\n', s)
s = html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', s))
print(re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', s))
PY
```
 ⚠ Do **not** hunt inside these files with a regex like `'[^<>]\{0,120\}borrow[^<>]\{0,160\}'` — on a 250 KB single-line-ish HTML document that backtracks catastrophically and will blow past a two-minute tool timeout. Use fixed-string `grep -Fin <word>` to find the line numbers first, then extract by index. (Observed: the naive regex form had to be killed; `grep -Fin` answered in milliseconds.) ⚠ And do not kill it with `pkill -f '<the-filename>'` — your own shell’s argv contains that string, so the pattern matches the pkill command itself and terminates the very call you are running (exit 144). This is the same self-match trap the repo guide documents for `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f`; use `node scripts/proc-guard.mjs check <pattern>`, or bracket the first character.

# Recovering a dropped papercusp-su MCP client via the HTTP bridge

> When your harness MCP client disconnects (tools vanish, ToolSearch finds nothing) but the operator :3070 is healthy, replay MCP JSON-RPC directly via curl to /api/mcp and keep working — don't just idle waiting to reconnect.

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) A harness’s `papercusp-su` MCP **client connection** can drop mid-session and **not auto-reconnect**. Symptoms: every `mcp__papercusp-su__*` tool disappears, and `ToolSearch` for them returns *“No matching deferred tools found”*. A looping agent in this state will otherwise just idle (“MCP down, holding”) indefinitely — observed live 2026-06-20 for \~1.5h+ (WI-260). **A `/loop` (or other skill) reload is a suspected trigger.** In one session (su-707ed, 2026-06-20, EI-1740) the `mcp__papercusp-su__*` tools were present and in use, then vanished *immediately after the first `/loop` ran* (a large deferred-tools system-reminder appeared and the papercusp-su tools were absent from it). The harness rebuilds its tool registry on a skill reload and the MCP advertisement isn’t always restored. So **anticipate this specifically when you put yourself on a loop** — verify `coord:*` still works right after a `/loop`, and fall straight to the bridge if not. **Crucial check before you assume an outage — probe BOTH endpoints, not just `/api/health`.** `/api/health` alone is NOT sufficient: it answers off a trivial path and stays fast even when the operator’s event loop is saturated, so a 200 there does *not* prove `/api/mcp` “is still fully serving requests” (that claim was this doc’s own mistake until EI-19420557240747274, 2026-08-03 — corrected here). Run the pair: 
```bash
curl -s -m 4 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3070/api/health   # 200?
timeout 20 curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST 'http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1&client=probe&workspace=papercusp-workspace' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"1"}}}'
```
 Read the pair together: * **`/api/health` 200 AND `/api/mcp` answers fast (not a timeout)** → the drop is at the **harness MCP-client layer** (the streamable-HTTP/SSE connection died and was not re-established), NOT an operator outage. The bridge below **will work** — proceed. * **`/api/health` 200 but `/api/mcp` TIMES OUT** → the operator process is up but its **event loop is saturated** (a wedge, not a client drop). This is a different failure with a different fix: see [surviving-an-operator-wedge-mcp-severance](/agent-insights/surviving-an-operator-wedge-mcp-severance/). **The bridge below traverses the SAME wedged event loop as your MCP client did — it will hang too, not rescue you.** Don’t retry-storm it; back off per that runbook instead. * **Both fail / connection refused** → the process itself is down, not a wedge or a client drop; the bridge is irrelevant here too. ## The bridge [Section titled “The bridge”](#the-bridge) The `papercusp-su` MCP is plain **HTTP** (see `~/.claude.json` → `mcpServers` → `papercusp-su`): a URL `http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?...` plus a `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. You can replay MCP JSON-RPC over `curl` to that same authorized endpoint and call **any** tool (`coord:*`, `plans:*`, `work_items:*`, `memory:*`). Key details learned the hard way: * **Identity** comes from the `client` query param — use your `PAPERCUSP_SID` (`env | grep PAPERCUSP_SID`), e.g. `client=su-400d97b0-...`. Confirm with a `coord:whoami` call before any write so attribution is correct. * **Continuity gotcha:** `$PAPERCUSP_SID` can DIFFER from the su-id under which you already declared your lane / did work this session (observed 2026-06-20: env SID `su-3ece675c` vs the established identity `su-707ed` that owned the declared intent, claimed issues, and sent messages). If they differ, pass your **established** id as `client=` — not blindly `$PAPERCUSP_SID` — or you fork your own presence into two identities and peers see a stranger pick up your work. Both ids resolve via the bridge, so choose deliberately. * **EI-1753 — the flap that could happen DESPITE a correct `client=` — FIXED (EI-7066, 2026-07-03):** during operator blips / a reconnect the server-side identity resolution used to rank the per-CONNECTION `Mcp-Session-Id` transport id ABOVE the explicit `?client=`/`x-papercusp-client` SID, so a claude session that reconnected mid-life (a cold-loop RECYCLE respawn, a dropped MCP transport) silently swapped to a fresh per-connection identity — a claim/comment could land on the WRONG su-id even with the right `client=` passed. Fixed in `_mcp-handler.ts`’s superuser branch: precedence is now `x-papercusp-client` header > `?client=` > `Mcp-Session-Id` — an explicit per-launch SID (header or param) ALWAYS outranks the transport id; the transport id is used only when the caller supplied no SID at all. Covered by a dedicated regression suite: `describe('su identity precedence (EI-7066: explicit SID before Mcp-Session-Id)')` in `mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts` (unit) + `§12 per-session identity via Mcp-Session-Id` in `su-locks-http-mcp.integration.test.ts` (live, asserts “same `?client=`, different `Mcp-Session-Id` → SAME owner”). Still good practice to `coord:whoami`-confirm before a critical write if you have any doubt about which identity a given call resolved to — but this exact flap class no longer reproduces. * **Pass `workspace`** in the URL (e.g. `workspace=papercusp-workspace`). Omitting it under `superuser=1` fails with `request_rejected: scoped_superuser_workspace_unresolved`. * Responses are **SSE**: lines look like `data: {...json...}`. Grep `^data:` and strip the prefix. * Tool names use the **colon** form (`coord:whoami`, `plans:add-decision`), not the `mcp__papercusp-su__coord_whoami` harness alias. * The endpoint is effectively **stateless** per request (no `Mcp-Session-Id` needed): each POST is a self-contained `tools/call`. ### Reusable helper [Section titled “Reusable helper”](#reusable-helper) 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# psu_call.sh <tool-name> [json-args]
set -euo pipefail
URL='http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1&client='"$PAPERCUSP_SID"'&workspace=papercusp-workspace&profile='
TOK='<bearer from ~/.claude.json>'
TOOL="$1"; if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then ARGS="$2"; else ARGS='{}'; fi
payload=$(jq -nc --arg n "$TOOL" --argjson a "$ARGS" \
  '{jsonrpc:"2.0",id:1,method:"tools/call",params:{name:$n,arguments:$a}}')
curl -s -m 90 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -X POST "$URL" -d "$payload" \
  | grep '^data:' | sed 's/^data: //' \
  | jq -r 'if .result.content then (.result.content[].text) elif .error then ("ERROR: "+(.error|tojson)) else tojson end'
```
 Then e.g. `psu_call.sh "coord:declare-intent" '{"intent":"..."}'`, `psu_call.sh "plans:add-decision" "$ARGS"`. > Gotcha: `ARGS="${2:-{}}"` is a **bash brace-ambiguity trap** — it appends a literal `}` to your JSON. Use the explicit `if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]` form above. ### Caveat: an externally-launched session has NO minted `client` id [Section titled “Caveat: an externally-launched session has NO minted client id”](#caveat-an-externally-launched-session-has-no-minted-client-id) The helper above assumes `$PAPERCUSP_SID` is a real **minted** client identity. A Claude Code (or OMP/Codex) shell launched **outside** `psu` — i.e. *not* through `install-standalone-mcp.sh` — has no `PAPERCUSP_SID` and no minted `uiClientId`. In that state the bridge still authenticates (loopback + the bearer from `~/.papercusp/superuser-token`), but the tools split into two classes (observed 2026-06-20, EI-1740): * **Work without an identity:** `tools/list`, `memory:remember`, and read-only reads like `coord:handoffs` / `coord:feed`. Enough to recall context, persist a durable fact, and read the board. * **Gated on a `uiClientId`:** every tool that calls `resolveAgentIdentity` — `coord:whoami`, `coord:declare-intent`, `issues:*`, and `work_items:claim` / `:comment` / `:complete` / `:set_state`. They fail with: 
  ```plaintext
  handler_error: resolveAgentIdentity: superuser context is missing uiClientId
  — re-run install-standalone-mcp.sh to mint a ?client= id
  ```
 So an externally-launched session **cannot claim/close/comment on work items or declare a coord lane**, even via the bridge. Do NOT reflexively run `install-standalone-mcp.sh` to fix this mid-session: it **regenerates the superuser token and rewrites `~/.claude.json` + `~/.claude/settings.json`** (your *own* running session’s MCP config + hooks) — far too invasive to fire blind during an autonomous loop. Instead, deliver value through the ungated paths: land the actual **code fix** (the commit is the durable artifact), reference the `EI-NNNN` in-code and in the commit, and `memory:remember` the learning. The unclaimable-but-fixed item resolves when a peer or the issues-engine notices the fix; the small duplication risk is cheaper than a token/config rewrite at 4am. > **Superseded (fixed since discovery, EI-2127/EI-334):** the hard failure above no longer reproduces. `resolveAgentIdentity`’s superuser branch used to **throw** on a missing `uiClientId`; it now resolves a stable fallback id (`SUPERUSER_FALLBACK_CLIENT_ID = 'su-loopback'`, `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/identity.ts`) instead of throwing — and the JSON-HTTP transport layer (`libs/generic/tooldef-http/src/http-projection.ts`) already defaults a missing `uiClientId` to `'su-http-loopback'` before identity resolution even runs. So an externally-launched session hitting the bridge with **no** `?client=` now resolves to one of those fallback ids instead of failing — `coord:whoami`, `coord:declare-intent`, `issues:*`, and `work_items:claim`/`:comment`/`:complete`/ `:set_state` all work, just attributed to the shared fallback identity rather than a per-session one. The symptom, the `EI-NNNN` error text, and the workaround above are kept as a record of what the gap looked like and how to route around a **similar** future gap — don’t expect to hit this exact error anymore. ## When to use vs. wait [Section titled “When to use vs. wait”](#when-to-use-vs-wait) Don’t burn a loop idling on reconnection. If `/api/health` is green, switch to the bridge and keep making progress (post decisions, message peers, claim work). Re-`coord:declare-intent` through the bridge so peers see you’re alive — presence from the omp-hook is independent of the MCP client, so a dropped client leaves you looking “active” while doing nothing. ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * WI-260 — the underlying gap (no auto-recovery/detection of a dropped MCP client). * `agent-mcp-slow-but-health-fast-event-loop-saturation` — the *adjacent* case (MCP slow, health fast) caused by event-loop saturation; this doc is the harder case where the client is fully **disconnected**, not just slow.

# A red-test watchdog EI can be a RETIRED test, not a broken one

> Before chasing a red-test improvement EI's failure tail, confirm the file still exists and still runs — a test moved to _retired/ is excluded from the suite; the EI is stale, resolve fixed with run-history + retirement evidence.

A `red-test:<path>` improvement EI (`kind=bug`) carries a big **rendered-DOM failure tail** in its summary. That tail is a trap: it makes the failure look like a live component/fixture-contract bug to investigate — but the test may simply have been **retired**, not broken. Real example: **EI-10486** (`apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/MugTab.test.tsx`, “failed 26× in 6h”). A prior worker parked it: *“recurring major MugTab UI suite red with large rendered DOM drift. Requires broader component/fixture contract investigation.”* That investigation was wasted — the file had already been **retired** to `_retired/mug-kettle-rail-tabs/` under WI-4778 (“Papercup is the ONE persona”). The base vitest config excludes `**/_retired/**` (`libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts`), so it no longer runs. The `test_runs` history showed it had also stabilized to **green** (61 pass / 2 fail in 48h, last fail well before removal) before it was moved. Nothing to fix. ## The 60-second triage BEFORE reading the failure tail [Section titled “The 60-second triage BEFORE reading the failure tail”](#the-60-second-triage-before-reading-the-failure-tail) For any `red-test:<path>` EI, run these first: 1. **Does the file still exist at that exact path?** `test -f <path>` — if GONE, it was moved or deleted. Check `_retired/` (`find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -iname '<Base>*' -print`). `_retired/**` is suite-excluded, so a retired copy is never executed. 2. **What does the run history actually say?** Query `harness_shared.test_runs` for that `file_path` — the watchdog summary’s “latest run is still red” is a snapshot from EI-creation time and goes **stale**: 
   ```sql
   SELECT status, commit_sha, created_at FROM harness_shared.test_runs
   WHERE file_path = '<path>' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 15;
   ```
 All-recent-`pass` (or zero runs since a removal) ⇒ not currently failing. If the file is gone/retired **or** the latest runs are green, this is a **verified non-failure**: `improvements:resolve { id, outcome:'fixed', summary, testsRun }` citing the file-existence check + the run-history rows. **Do not** write a regression test — repo policy forbids tests for `_retired/` surfaces, and there is no live code path to guard. ## Why it re-dispatches [Section titled “Why it re-dispatches”](#why-it-re-dispatches) The EI stays `open` (assignee `improvement-runner`) until someone resolves it; the cadence keeps re-dispatching an open EI. Because the tracked path no longer produces runs, the watchdog won’t newly re-open it — but the **existing** open row must be closed by hand. Resolving it is the whole job. ## Note on `testing:prune-orphan-runs` [Section titled “Note on testing:prune-orphan-runs”](#note-on-testingprune-orphan-runs) It removes stale `test_runs` rows for known-non-signal paths (`_retired/`, `.papercusp/scratch`, `*.flakeproof.test.tsx`) and for files gone from a harness’s worktree. But a row with `harness_slug = NULL` (system-recorded gate runs) has **no worktree to existence-check**, so the tool leaves a plain `<Name>.test.tsx` orphan in place. That’s fine — with the file retired, no new runs are recorded and the flip history freezes; the only required action is resolving the EI.

# A red operator-vite build can DESTROY the live bundle — and only some failures do

> Vite empties outDir in a renderStart hook, so a LINK-time failure (missing named export) kills the running desktop while a resolve/syntax error leaves it fine. Builds are now staged into dist.next/ and swapped only on success.

## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) The desktop app dies. Every route returns: 
```plaintext
503  operator-vite is not built.
     Run `npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-vite run build`.
```
 …and running that command **fails**, so the advice is a loop. The app was working minutes earlier and nobody deleted anything. This took the owner’s desktop down **twice on 2026-07-12**. ## The mechanism (the part that is not obvious) [Section titled “The mechanism (the part that is not obvious)”](#the-mechanism-the-part-that-is-not-obvious) Vite empties `outDir` from a **`renderStart` (order: `'pre'`) hook** — `vite:prepare-out-dir`, i.e. *after* the module graph is built, *before* any chunk is written. So **whether a failed build destroys your bundle depends on which phase it dies in.** Measured on vite 8.0.16 (the version this app builds with), with a previous good bundle sitting in `dist/`: | failure mode | exit | previous `dist/` | | ------------------------------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------ | | unresolvable import | 1 | **SURVIVES** — dies before the empty | | syntax error | 1 | **SURVIVES** — dies before the empty | | **missing named export** (`MISSING_EXPORT`) | 1 | **DESTROYED** — dies after the empty | | killed / OOM mid-write | ≠0 | **DESTROYED** — half-written | This is why the bug survived so long: a casual repro (typo an import) shows `dist/` surviving and “proves” there is no bug. The destructive column is the **link-time** one — and that is exactly the class our browser shims produce. ## What actually triggered it (both times) [Section titled “What actually triggered it (both times)”](#what-actually-triggered-it-both-times) 1. A stray `pnpm install` hijacked `node_modules`; `@assistant-ui/store` lost its `tapClientResource` export → `MISSING_EXPORT` → dist eaten. 2. `agent-tools/coordination/log.ts` began importing `PgCoordLog` from `@papercusp/coordination/event-log`, which the SPA **aliases to a browser shim** (`src/shims/coordination-event-log-browser.ts`) that only exported `DEFAULT_COORD_WORKSPACE` → `MISSING_EXPORT` → dist eaten. Case 2 is a standing trap: **a shim is only ever linked by a real `vite build`.** Nothing type-checks an alias, so the entire unit suite stays green while the bundle is unbuildable. Add an import to a shimmed module and you can red the SPA build without a single failing test. ## What is in place now [Section titled “What is in place now”](#what-is-in-place-now) * **Builds are staged.** `bin/vite-build-singleflight` (the one seam every build goes through: the rebuild timer, `build-desktop-sidecar.sh`, `setup-release-checkout.sh`, and any hand-run `npm run build`) points vite at `dist.next/` via `PAPERCUSP_VITE_OUT_DIR` and **renames it over `dist/` only on exit 0** with an `index.html` present. A red build cannot touch the bundle that is serving — and `dist/` is never transiently empty *during* a build either, which also closes the EI-9836 window (`ls dist/assets` going 1513 → 0 → 1513 mid-build). * **Retain-regime builds are NOT staged** (`--watch`, or `PAPERCUSP_RETAIN_DIST_CHUNKS=1` — the desktop rebuild timer). Those run with `emptyOutDir:false`: they never empty `dist/`, so they are already crash-safe, and staging them would throw away the very old chunks an open webview is pinned to. * `dist-wipe-guard` is handed the **final** `dist/` (`PAPERCUSP_VITE_FINAL_OUT_DIR`), not the staging dir — the *swap* would yank a live watcher’s chunks just as an in-place empty would, so it must still refuse that case. * **The 503 tells the truth.** `apps/operator/lib/spa-build-status.ts` reads `.vite-build-failure.json` (dropped beside `dist/` by a failed build) and, if there is no bundle *because the last build failed*, says so — with the exit code, the timestamp, the log path and the error tail — instead of prescribing the command that just failed. * **Shim drift is caught in milliseconds.** `src/__tests__/browser-shims.test.ts` parses the shim aliases out of `vite.config.ts`, scans every SPA-reachable source for value imports through them, and fails if a shim is missing one. It would have caught case 2 before the build ever ran. ## If you hit this anyway [Section titled “If you hit this anyway”](#if-you-hit-this-anyway) 1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3270/` — 503 means no bundle. 2. Read `apps/operator-vite/.vite-build-failure.json` and the `.vite-build.log` it points at. The 503 body now contains both. 3. Fix the error, then `npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-vite run build`. `dist/` is restored by the swap; `:3270` goes green without restarting anything. ## The lesson worth carrying [Section titled “The lesson worth carrying”](#the-lesson-worth-carrying) “The build failed” and “the build destroyed the running app” are different events, and the second one is invisible in the exit code. Any tool that **empties a live directory before it knows it can refill it** has this bug — stage it and swap.

# Reflexive datatypes & tools — extend the platform from inside it

> How an agent declares a NEW entity type (a datatype) or a NEW tool at runtime and has the whole platform treat it as first-class. Datatypes — meta:define-datatype writes harness_shared.datatype_registry (dedup-only, D-010); a generic-kind datatype's work_item_kind is accepted by work_items:create AND its payload is validated against payload_schema (ajv), it's visible in list/search/plans, frontier-placeable via the pot-placement tag (opt-in), self-improvable by construction (P-010), and blueprint-dependable (dependencies.datatypes). Tools — meta:define-tool routes composed→live recipe / sandboxed|elevated→tools:scaffold PR rail; dynamic-tool-confinement is the adversarially-proven per-tool envelope (no fs-escape / denied-host net / cap escalation / cap minting). first-class migrations + the Comb-published shared tier + the runtime PEP wiring go through the reviewed PR rail (D-003) / the capability TCB (tier:'human', D-007).

## What [Section titled “What”](#what) Papercusp can be extended **from inside the running system**: an agent declares a new **datatype** (a named entity TYPE) or a new **tool** (a capability), and the platform treats it as first-class — no engineer, no redeploy. The point: a domain (an internal reference app was the first) models its own concepts *on* the self-improvement substrate instead of building a bespoke system beside it. Design anchors D-001..D-011 (the plan); the decisive ones are inlined below. ## Datatypes — the extension flow [Section titled “Datatypes — the extension flow”](#datatypes--the-extension-flow) `meta:define-datatype` (`agent-tools/datatypes/declare.ts`) writes one row to `harness_shared.datatype_registry` (migration 421) via `datatype-registry-store.ts`. Authority is **dedup-only** (D-010, the npm/crates model): a hard unique id (the kebab slug, the PK) + a soft semantic gate (`findSimilarDatatypes` — `title_tsv` lexical fused with the `embedding` cosine leg; `force:true` overrides). Declaration also requires/validates: * **A self-improvement surface (P-010, `datatype-self-improvement.ts`)** — `checkSelfImprovementForDeclare` REQUIRES `{ improvements[], scorecard[], gym{signals,rubric} }` for the authoritative tiers (generic-kind / first-class); a datatype is self-improvable *by construction*. Projection is exempt. * **A compilable `payload_schema`** — `isCompilableSchema` (ajv) rejects a malformed schema at declare time, so the create path never has to fail-open. Once a **generic-kind** datatype is declared, its `work_item_kind` is live everywhere with **zero bespoke plumbing**: * **Create + validate** — `work_items:create { kind, payload }` accepts the kind (`work_items/_create-core.ts` → `getGenericKindDatatype`) AND validates `payload` against the datatype’s `payload_schema` (`validateDatatypePayload`, ajv) → `invalid_payload` on a violation. This is the *validation* a datatype exists to provide (a malformed `bet` is rejected, not stored as a blob). * **Visibility** — `featureFamilyKindClause` (`work-items.ts`) makes the kind appear in list / count / search. * **Placement (OPT-IN)** — `frontierPlacementKindClause` (`datatype-frontier-placement.ts`) enrols the kind in the autonomous cup-placement frontier ONLY when the datatype carries the `pot-placement` tag. Visibility ≠ placement: a datatype is a data SHAPE; auto-spawning a worker per instance is deliberate. * **Blueprint dependency** — a blueprint’s `dependencies.datatypes` resolves against the registry: `depHostSetsFromCatalog(cat, listRegisteredDatatypeNames(sql, ws))` populates `availableDatatypes` (a `Set`, not an array), gated at harness creation (`agent-tools/harness/create.ts`). ### Tiers (D-002 / D-008) [Section titled “Tiers (D-002 / D-008)”](#tiers-d-002--d-008) `generic-kind` (default — a work\_item kind + validated payload, zero migration) · `first-class` (a native SQL-backed concept — its migration ships through the **PR rail**, NOT runtime) · `projection` (read-only, an EXTERNAL engine is the single writer, `authoritativeWriter:'engine:<name>'` — Papercusp holds a view, runs no gym over it). ## Tools — the extension flow (D-003: safety = confinement + review, not prohibition) [Section titled “Tools — the extension flow (D-003: safety = confinement + review, not prohibition)”](#tools--the-extension-flow-d-003-safety--confinement--review-not-prohibition) `meta:define-tool` (`agent-tools/tools/define.ts` → `define-tool-router.ts`) routes by tier: * **composed** → registers LIVE as a `code_recipe` (a DAG over EXISTING tools; mints no new capability), invoked via `recipes:run`. * **sandboxed-imperative | elevated** → NEVER registered at runtime; `tool-scaffold.ts` emits a reviewable `defineTool` skeleton (writes/runs/mints nothing — a `not_implemented` stub) for the PR rail (`tools:scaffold` → review + adversarial confinement proof → `platform:contribute`). `dynamic-tool-confinement.ts` is the **per-dynamic-tool envelope** (P-003 core, adversarially proven): `deriveDynamicToolEnvelope` holds ONLY the declared caps/paths/domains, NARROW-ONLY vs the host role, and can never hold the minting/escalation floor (`DYNAMIC_TOOL_FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY_GLOBS`: grant/revoke/envelope/set-tier/meta:define-\*/tools:scaffold/platform:contribute/secrets/processes:kill/cup:spawn). The runtime PEP wiring of this into dispatch is a **capability-TCB** edit (`capability-envelope/**`, `tier:'human'`, D-007) → reviewed PR rail, never an unattended auto-apply. ## Gotchas (these bite) [Section titled “Gotchas (these bite)”](#gotchas-these-bite) * **`payload_schema` is `Set`-vs-array etc. — types matter.** `DependencyHostSets.availableDatatypes` is a `Set<string>` the resolver `.has()`-checks; passing an array compiles-via-esbuild but fails tsc + crashes the resolver. Always `npx tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (esbuild ≠ typecheck). * **The minimal work-items test schema must carry `datatype_registry`.** The visibility + placement clauses reference `harness_shared.datatype_registry`; `test/_work-items-schema.ts` (`HARNESS_FEATURES_CONSOLIDATED_DDL`, used by `createFreshPgDb` tests) includes a minimal version so those tests don’t fail `relation ... does not exist`. `createOrgTestDb` tests apply the full migration 421. * **Don’t blind-build the gated parts.** first-class migration CODEGEN, the runtime confinement PEP wiring, and the **Comb-published shared tier** (a data-carrying Cupboard listing + the server moderation/distribution worker at `/admin/cupboard-moderation`) are PR-rail / cross-component by design — an operator-core-only build would be a non-functional stub. ## Verify [Section titled “Verify”](#verify) * Unit: `cd packages/operator-core && npx vitest run lib/datatype-registry-store.test.ts lib/datatype-self-improvement.test.ts lib/datatype-payload-validation.test.ts lib/define-tool-router.test.ts lib/tool-scaffold.test.ts lib/dynamic-tool-confinement.test.ts` * Integration (real PG): `npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts lib/datatype-registry.integration.test.ts lib/datatype-frontier-placement.integration.test.ts lib/datatype-instance-loop.integration.test.ts` * The end-to-end proof is `datatype-instance-loop.integration.test.ts` (declare → fetch-by-kind → payload validate → placeable). ## Live-verified end-to-end (2026-06-30, running operator) [Section titled “Live-verified end-to-end (2026-06-30, running operator)”](#live-verified-end-to-end-2026-06-30-running-operator) Exercised against the live operator via loopback MCP (scratch workspaces, cleaned up): * **Datatype loop:** `meta:define-datatype {tier:'generic-kind'}` → `work_items:create {kind}` with a VALID payload returns `ok:true` (the instance lands in `harness_features_consolidated` as a feature-family row); an INVALID payload is rejected `invalid_payload` with the ajv message. A generic-kind create requires an in-scope **harness** (by design — the feature table is harness-keyed). * **The `createWorkItem` re-check.** `work_items:create`’s gate validated the generic kind, but `createWorkItem` (a second entry point) re-checked `isWorkItemKind` and refused the insert — fixed (`work-items.ts` now re-checks the registry via `hasGenericKind`). * **Observability spans new datatypes (P-011).** `curation:state-of-pot` and an UNFILTERED `work_items:list` both surface a generic-kind instance. The **kind-FILTER** path was the gap: `work_items:list`/`work_items:search` locked `kind` to a `z.enum` of built-ins, so you could not filter the queue by a declared datatype — relaxed to a free string (built-in OR registered generic-kind); `familyOf()` already routes it to the feature family. Unknown kind simply lists empty. * **Tool loop:** `meta:define-tool {tier:'composed'}` registers a `code_recipe` LIVE; `recipes:run` then executes it (the system gains AND uses a tool from inside). `meta:define-tool {tier:'elevated'}` emits a review-gated scaffold file (NOT registered at runtime). * **Dogfood witness:** `platform:dogfood_verify {prUrl}` is read-only and wired — it returns the 5-stage round-trip assertion (prTracked / reviewed / merged / shipped / linked) with precise gaps. * **Gap on the outward PR path (WI-1293):** `platform:enable` on an install that already has a legacy shared harness returns `selfHive.status:'already_standing' detail:'legacy_shared_harness'` and does NOT stand up the dedicated `papercusp-platform-pot` member checkout, so `platform:contribute {kind:'pr'}` fails `self_hive_not_found`. Only blocks the owner-gated/cred-gated live fork→PR step; the internal loop + dogfood verifier are proven.

# Registering a repo-wide guard can be INERT — and probes must report it

> Why a guard registration can silently do nothing, how --print-affected now reports repo-wide guard tasks, and how whole-file scanners can flag their own fixtures.

Landing WI-37593 — whose entire subject was *“this guard is wired to nothing”* — my own fix reproduced the bug it was fixing. Four traps, each of which independently produces a **green that means “it stopped checking.”** ## 1. A registration is skipped SILENTLY when the host workspace lacks the script [Section titled “1. A registration is skipped SILENTLY when the host workspace lacks the script”](#1-a-registration-is-skipped-silently-when-the-host-workspace-lacks-the-script) `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` appends a registered guard with: 
```js
for (const guard of REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS) {
  const ws = wsByName.get(guard.workspace);
  if (!ws?.scripts?.[guard.script]) continue;   // <- silent skip
```
 `guard.workspace` is normally `@papercusp/operator-core`. A guard whose npm script is declared only in the **root** `package.json` therefore matches nothing and runs on **no path at all**. The entry looks right, reads right, and reviews clean. **Fix:** declare it in the host workspace too. The root scripts resolve `ROOT` from `import.meta.url`, so cwd is irrelevant: 
```json
"lint:workspace-deps-complete": "node ../../scripts/check-workspace-deps-complete.mjs"
```
 ## 2. `--print-affected` now reports guards too [Section titled “2. --print-affected now reports guards too”](#2---print-affected-now-reports-guards-too) The print-only probe now emits the original machine-readable workspace lines and a line for each repo-wide guard task attached by the same selection: 
```text
AFFECTED_WS  @papercusp/web
AFFECTED_GUARD  @papercusp/operator-core  lint:chunk-safe
```
 Unlike the old behavior, guard selection happens before the probe exits. Guard lines can therefore appear even when there are zero `AFFECTED_WS` lines, which is the intended fail-safe behavior for root-level changes such as `package.json`. The repo’s own detector names inert registrations outright — **run this after any registration**: 
```bash
npm run lint:guard-reachability
# ❌ 1 REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS registration(s) are INERT — the workspace declares no such script
```
 ## 3. “Nothing invokes it” is usually wrong — check CI before you claim it [Section titled “3. “Nothing invokes it” is usually wrong — check CI before you claim it”](#3-nothing-invokes-it-is-usually-wrong--check-ci-before-you-claim-it) WI-37593 asserted the guard was invoked by nothing, evidenced by a grep of `affected-tests.mjs`. That grep was correct and the conclusion was still too strong: `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs it, so `lint:guard-reachability` classifies it **`[ci]` = enforced**. The accurate, narrower finding is the one worth carrying: git-sync stamps every commit `[skip ci]`, so the `push`/`pull_request` triggers never fire (EI-18661485259809120), and green-checkpoint dispatches the workflow only **after** it fast-forwards `main`. Enforcement is therefore **remote and post-promotion** — the author gets zero local signal and the fleet’s blocking verdict never runs it. That is a real gap, and registering in `REPO_WIDE_INVARIANT_GUARDS` is what closes it. Caution `--census` prints only the PROBLEM categories (not-enforced / partially-covered / not-measured), never the enforced majority. A guard’s absence from it means “classified enforced”, **not** “unknown” — and not “the local path is covered”. It also writes via `console.error`, so `cmd --census 2>&1 > f` sends the report to your terminal and leaves you grepping an empty file. Use `> f 2>&1`. ## 4. A whole-file scanner eventually flags its own `selfTest()` fixtures [Section titled “4. A whole-file scanner eventually flags its own selfTest() fixtures”](#4-a-whole-file-scanner-eventually-flags-its-own-selftest-fixtures) `hook-repo-root-portability.test.ts` (the “no guard script hardcodes its repo root” ratchet) went red on `posttooluse-css-design-primitives-nudge.mjs` for `root = /repo`. That binding is inside `function selfTest()` — a synthetic tree handed to a pure helper, `isCandidateFile(root, '/repo/a.css')`. Fixture data cannot cause the fail-open the guard exists to prevent, so it was a false positive. **Do not “fix” the flagged file.** The detector is `ROOT_ISH = /(ROOT|REPO|WORKSPACE|CHECKOUT|TREE_?BASE)/i`, so every rename that keeps the meaning still trips it, and renaming to something non-root-ish makes the code less clear purely to satisfy a linter — dodging a detector, not satisfying it. The deciding evidence was the convention: 7 of the 8 sibling nudge scripts have `selfTest` blocks and none binds a fixture root. So the **detector** was fixed, not the peer’s script. Danger End the skipped block on a **column-0 `}`**, never by brace-counting. A brace inside a string literal miscounts, and the miscount is silent *in the dangerous direction*: an unbalanced count never re-enables scanning, so the guard quietly stops checking the entire rest of the file. Pair the change with a control asserting scanning **resumes** after the block (an offender before *and* after, with the fixture skipped) — that control is the canary for “it stopped checking.” ## The through-line [Section titled “The through-line”](#the-through-line) Every one of these fails toward a confident green. Before trusting a guard, ask what its green would look like if it were running on nothing — and pick a probe that can tell the difference. Same family as the documented traps that mining green-checkpoint’s `isolation:` lines returns the gate’s **own** test fixtures, and that a `tsc -p .` which typechecks zero files exits clean.

# Registration seams die silently when tests mock them

> A registerX()/getX() seam is only alive if some HOST actually calls registerX() at bootstrap — and nothing in CI checks that, because every unit test mocks or registers the seam itself. HostPlatform was dead on every production host for 9 days (agent:role / operator:scanner prompts/get threw) after the only registration call was deleted along with 'dead' instrumentation-node.ts. Fixing it then exposed a SECOND masked bug: import.meta.dirname is undefined under the operator host's tsx CJS transform. Verify seams on :3170, not in vitest.

## The mistake this prevents [Section titled “The mistake this prevents”](#the-mistake-this-prevents) `@papercusp/host-platform` shipped 05-20 with a deliberate design: `registerHostPlatform()` at host bootstrap, `getHostPlatform()` in consumers, **no silent fallback** — an unregistered host throws. The one production registration call lived in `apps/operator/instrumentation-node.ts` (a Next instrumentation hook). On 06-03, commit `5694e7d58` deleted that file as “dead scheduler code — its duties run via the embedded-pg boot runner + host-bootstrap, or are vestigial. Confirmed zero importers.” The registration was neither vestigial nor ported. From 06-03 to 06-12, **every** `prompts/get` for `agent:role` or `operator:scanner` on every host (green :3070, staging :3170, Tauri sidecar, stdio agent-mcp) returned `render_error: No HostPlatform registered`. Nothing noticed for 9 days: * `role.test.ts` mocks `@papercusp/host-platform` (deliberately, and well) — so the only test of the real resolver never exercises registration. * `tool-manifest.test.ts` drove real `node:fs` (pre-migration) — no seam. * No test anywhere asserts “the hosts register a platform at bootstrap”. The same deletion-commit pattern had already bitten once before: the endpoint-IPC server start ALSO lived only in instrumentation-node.ts and had to be ported to `host-bootstrap.ts` (see the long comment there). The registration call was the second side effect in that file, and it was missed. ## The rules [Section titled “The rules”](#the-rules) 1. **Deleting a “dead” entry file: enumerate its side effects, not its importers.** “Zero importers” proves nothing for a file whose job was to RUN things (registrations, server starts, watchers). Diff the file body against `host-bootstrap.ts` and port every effect, or state per-effect why it’s vestigial. 2. **A `registerX()/getX()` seam needs one test that fails when no host registers.** Unit tests mocking the seam keep the consumers green forever; the only honest check is at the host level (a bootstrap test, or a live probe). If you add such a seam, add the tripwire in the same PR. 3. **Verify on the running host, not in vitest.** The probe that found both bugs (bearer = any `kind='system'` row from `harness_shared.token_index`): 
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3170/api/mcp \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"prompts/get","params":{"name":"agent:role","arguments":{"role":"architect"}}}'
   ```
 Note: `~/.papercusp/superuser-token` does NOT resolve on this surface (`invalid_bearer`) — the prompts/resources paths resolve bearers via `token_index`, not the superuser bypass. ## The second bug a first bug can mask [Section titled “The second bug a first bug can mask”](#the-second-bug-a-first-bug-can-mask) With registration fixed, the same probe failed differently: `render_error: The "paths[0]" argument must be of type string`. `import.meta.dirname` is **undefined** when the operator host runs agent-mcp through tsx’s CJS transform (apps/operator has no `"type": "module"`), while under vitest (real ESM) it works — so tests pass and the host crashes. `import.meta.url` IS shimmed there. Portable helper: `packages/agent-mcp/src/prompts/module-dir.ts` (`dirname` → `fileURLToPath` fallback, null-safe). If you write `resolve(import.meta.dirname, …)` in code any operator host loads, use `moduleDir(import.meta)` instead — and remember the hosts run with **cwd `apps/operator`**, so cwd-relative fallbacks need a `../../` candidate too. Fixed in: host-architecture-2026-05-20-v2 P-001..P-003 (D-002 has the full phase-by-phase re-baseline).

# Deploys crash-loop :3070 on MODULE_NOT_FOUND — an in-place node_modules rebuild under the live operator

> ':3070 connection refused on all pages' in recurring ~1–35 min windows: a deploy's setup-release-checkout.sh refreshed node_modules with `rm -rf $dest; cp -al` IN PLACE while the live operator kept serving from it, so for the ~minute the root copy took the tree was deleted/half-populated → the 32 cluster workers respawned mid-copy, hit MODULE_NOT_FOUND (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, @papercusp/plugin-loader), exhausted the 160-respawn budget → 0 workers → connection refused, until the copy finished and it self-recovered. Root fix: atomic sibling-temp swap (two renames) so the live tree is only ever complete. Defense-in-depth: a workspace-resolution gate (step 3c, EI-2118) that aborts before restart if any workspace symlink is dangling, a boot-integrity preflight (fail fast + named), and a cluster boot-failure backstop (halt the respawn storm) so an inconsistent tree degrades to a fast, loud, self-correcting fail instead of an hour-long all-pages outage.

## The symptom [Section titled “The symptom”](#the-symptom) `:3070` (the operator that serves every page over SSE/sync) goes **“connection refused on all pages”** in recurring windows — the client shows **“Operator connection lost”** then reconnects (“Welcome back, User”), sometimes seconds apart, for anywhere from \~1 to \~35 minutes, then self-recovers. The operator journal during a window: 
```plaintext
[hono-host] fatal unhandledRejection — exiting: Error: Cannot find module
  '.../papercusp-release/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/types.js'  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
[cluster] worker N exited (code=1 signal=null); respawn budget exhausted (160) — NOT respawning
[cluster] SIGTERM — draining 32 worker(s) + exiting primary
```
 `NRestarts=0` at the systemd level can hide it — the storm is the **cluster primary respawning workers**, not systemd restarting the service. ## The mechanism (root cause) [Section titled “The mechanism (root cause)”](#the-mechanism-root-cause) `:3070` runs the `papercusp-release` checkout. A deploy shells `setup-release-checkout.sh`, whose step 3 historically refreshed node\_modules **in place**: 
```sh
[ -e "$dest" ] && rm -rf "$dest"      # deletes the LIVE root node_modules
cp -al "$nm" "$dest"                  # then slowly (~a minute, 100k+ files) re-hardlinks it
```
 This tree “never `npm install`s” — it **hardlink-copies** node\_modules from the integration tree. For the whole \~minute the root `cp -al` runs, the live operator’s node\_modules is **deleted or half-populated**. Any worker that (re)boots in that window — a `lag-self-restart`, a crash respawn, a deploy restart racing the copy — `require()`s a module that isn’t there yet → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → it exits → the primary respawns it → it crashes again → **the 160-respawn budget (workers×5 = 32×5) burns out → 0 live workers → connection refused on every page**. When the copy finishes the next restart boots clean and it self-recovers — which is why it looks transient and recurs on (dep-changing) deploys. `PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=32` maximizes the blast radius: one inconsistent tree crash-loops all 32 workers at once. ## The fix — four layers [Section titled “The fix — four layers”](#the-fix--four-layers) **1. Atomic node\_modules swap (root cause removal)** — `setup-release-checkout.sh` `sync_one_node_modules()`. Hardlink-copy into a **sibling** temp (`$dest.deploy-tmp.$$`, same depth so the workspace packages’ relative `../../packages/X` symlinks resolve identically), then swap with **two fast renames** (`mv dest old; mv tmp dest; rm old`). The live tree is only ever **complete**; the exposure shrinks from \~a minute to the microseconds between two `rename(2)`s. `set -e` aborts a failed `cp` *before* any swap, so a partial copy can never replace the live tree. **2. Workspace-resolution gate — step 3c (EI-2118)** — `setup-release-checkout.sh` step 3c. A related but distinct failure mode: the `need_node_modules()` heuristic compares entry **names** via `ls`+`diff`, which cannot detect a dangling symlink (it exists by name but the target is absent). Before EI-2118, a dangling `@papercusp/<pkg>` symlink in the release tree slipped through that check, the deploy skipped the re-copy, and the operator crash-looped on `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at the restart cutover (2026-06-20 `@papercusp/plugin-loader`). The fix: `unresolved_workspace_pkgs()` walks `@papercusp`/`@papercup` in both trees using `-e` (which **follows** symlinks), so a dangling link fails the test. `need_node_modules()` in `auto` mode now also calls it and forces a re-copy when any package is unresolved. After the copy, step 3c runs `unresolved_workspace_pkgs()` once more: if any package still doesn’t resolve, the script **exits 1 before any restart** — the old process keeps serving, zero downtime. **3. Boot-integrity preflight (fail fast + named)** — `boot-integrity-preflight.ts`, run as the **first import** of `hono-host.ts` via `boot-integrity-first.ts` (so it evaluates before the heavy import graph). It `require.resolve`s a manifest of load-bearing modules; on a broken/partial tree it logs one **named** diagnostic and exits `78` (distinct, `EX_CONFIG`) instead of a deep `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack. The module is **dependency-free** (only `node:module`) so it can’t be a victim of the inconsistency it checks. Manifest entries are **resolve-verified against a healthy tree** — naïve `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `mem0ai/package.json` FAIL even when installed (exports-map quirks), so the manifest uses the forms that actually resolve. **4. Cluster boot-failure backstop (no respawn storm)** — `cluster-fork.ts`, opt-in via `onUnbootable`. A worker that exits within `bootGraceMs` (10s) of fork never came up; if a **whole generation** fails that way and **none was ever healthy**, the build is unbootable → halt the respawn storm and call `onUnbootable` (→ exit the primary clean/fast/distinct so the supervisor/deploy rolls back) instead of burning all 160 respawns. A worker that crashes **after** surpassing the grace window is a normal runtime crash and still respawns — `onUnbootable` never fires once any worker has been healthy. Layers 1–2 prevent inconsistent trees from reaching the live operator (either by making the swap atomic or by aborting before cutover); layers 3–4 turn any *remaining* inconsistency (a botched rollback, a non-manifest module) into a fast, loud, self-correcting fail instead of an hour-long all-pages outage. ## Diagnosing / recovering a live incident [Section titled “Diagnosing / recovering a live incident”](#diagnosing--recovering-a-live-incident) * `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3070/api/health` → `000`/connection-refused = down; the journal grep above confirms the MODULE\_NOT\_FOUND crash-loop. * It usually **self-recovers** once the in-place copy finishes; if wedged, the documented recovery is `systemctl --user stop papercup-dev-api.service` then re-run the deploy (`PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1 npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute --no-drain`) or `npm ci` in `papercusp-release` to complete node\_modules. * Confirm `papercusp-release/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/types.js` and `@papercusp/plugin-loader` resolve (`cd papercusp-release && node -e "require.resolve('@papercusp/plugin-loader')"`). ## Related [Section titled “Related”](#related) * `cluster-workers-exhaust-inotify-watches.mdx` — a *different* 32-worker crash-loop (per-process inotify exhaustion); already fixed by gating watchers on `cluster.isPrimary`. * `deploy-pipeline-is-async-self-healing.mdx` — why `:3070` serves green `main`, not your staging edit.

# Renaming a first-party rubric races the cold-start seeder — always clear the placeholder row first

> A migration that renames a bundled rubric's on-disk directory MUST also delete a same-id owner='first-party-bundle' placeholder row, or the seeder can win the race and leave a spurious duplicate.

Filed live during the cup-lexicon rename (EI-8912 / WI-3618, 2026-07-10) while renaming `rubrics/hive-coordination-health/` → `rubrics/pot-coordination-health/`. ## The race [Section titled “The race”](#the-race) A first-party rubric is bundled as a self-describing directory (`rubrics/<id>/rubric.json` + `listing.json` + optional `METHOD.md`) but its LIVE identity is a row in `harness_shared.harness_plans` (a rubric **is** a plan row — see `packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts`). The cold-start seeder (`ensureFirstPartyRubricsSeeded`, wired into every `rubrics:list`/`get`/`search` read) is **no-clobber per-id**: it scans the bundled dirs on disk and seeds any `rubricId` that has **no** matching plan row yet, owner `FIRST_PARTY_RUBRIC_SEED_OWNER` (`'first-party-bundle'`). Renaming a rubric is therefore a two-sided move that must land atomically but usually can’t: 1. `git mv rubrics/<old-id>/ rubrics/<new-id>/` (+ the \~N producer-file string constants) — a plain tree commit, picked up by git-sync on its own schedule. 2. A DB migration that renames the **live** plan row `<old-id>` → `<new-id>`. Those two land as separate events. The moment (1) is live on disk but (2) hasn’t run yet, **any** background operator process’s lazy seed pass (a live dev/bg-host process, another agent’s session, a fresh boot) sees the new directory with no plan row under the new id yet — and seeds a **blank** row for it (`owner='first-party-bundle'`, today’s date, no real ratification history). When migration (2) then runs, you have TWO rows: the real historical one (still under the old id, about to be renamed) and a spurious first-party placeholder already squatting the new id. This isn’t a maybe — on any box with background workers running (which is every shared dev box), the window between “file rename commit lands” and “DB migration applies” is measured in minutes, and the seed pass fires on every rubric read. Assume it WILL happen. ## The fix — every rubric-rename migration must do this [Section titled “The fix — every rubric-rename migration must do this”](#the-fix--every-rubric-rename-migration-must-do-this) Before renaming the real row into the new id, unconditionally clear a same-id **placeholder** (never a real row — gate on `owner='first-party-bundle'` so you never clobber a genuinely-existing rubric that happens to already use that id): 
```sql
DO $$
BEGIN
  -- Clear a same-id placeholder the disk-scan seeder may have raced in ahead
  -- of us — never touch a real (non-seed-placeholder) row under the new id.
  DELETE FROM harness_shared.harness_plans
   WHERE plan_slug = '<new-id>'
     AND owner = 'first-party-bundle';


  -- sql-snippet-justified: a one-off seed-race REPAIR (guarded rename), not a read —
  -- no tool exposes an atomic exists/not-exists precondition on a plan row.
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE plan_slug = '<old-id>')
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE plan_slug = '<new-id>')
  THEN
    UPDATE harness_shared.harness_plans
       SET plan_slug = '<new-id>',
           template_data = jsonb_set(COALESCE(template_data, '{}'::jsonb), '{methodRef}', '"<new-id>"', true)
     WHERE plan_slug = '<old-id>';
  END IF;
END $$;
```
 This is idempotent and safe regardless of which order the two processes land in: if the seeder hasn’t raced yet, the `DELETE` is a no-op; if it has, the migration clears its placeholder before the real rename, so you never end up with two rows. Worked example: `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/531-rename-hive-coordination-health-rubric-to-pot.sql`. ## Since WI-3617: an invalid seeder-owned row self-heals (but the migration rule stands) [Section titled “Since WI-3617: an invalid seeder-owned row self-heals (but the migration rule stands)”](#since-wi-3617-an-invalid-seeder-owned-row-self-heals-but-the-migration-rule-stands) On 2026-07-17 a DB-recovery pass left the live `pot-coordination-health` row with `template_data = NULL` under `owner='first-party-bundle'` — invisible to every read (`planRowToRubric` nulls invalid rows) yet, under the raw-slug no-clobber check, permanently blocking its own re-seed. The seed decision core (`rubricsNeedingSeed`) now RECLAIMS a row that is both seeder-owned AND schema-invalid: it counts as needing seed and `proposeRubric` upserts the bundle content over it on the next rubrics read. A half-authored row under any real owner still blocks, invalid or not. This makes the wedge class self-healing, but a rename migration must STILL clear the placeholder first — a raced placeholder is usually *valid* (the seeder writes full bundle content), so the reclaim never fires for it, and its lack of ratification lineage is the reason it must not become the renamed row’s identity. Repair worked example (placeholder clear + tenant-scoped rename + content re-sync): `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/621-repair-pot-coordination-health-rubric-row.sql`. ## Why this lives here and not as a TS helper [Section titled “Why this lives here and not as a TS helper”](#why-this-lives-here-and-not-as-a-ts-helper) Migrations are plain, standalone `.sql` files applied by the migration runner — there’s no code path for them to call a shared TypeScript helper. The recurrence guard is this doc (discoverable via `docs:search` / `agent-insights-index`) plus the pointer left in `rubrics.ts` next to `FIRST_PARTY_RUBRIC_SEED_OWNER`, so anyone reading the seed code — not just anyone who happens to find the 531 migration first — learns about the race before authoring the next rubric rename. ## Checklist for the next rubric rename [Section titled “Checklist for the next rubric rename”](#checklist-for-the-next-rubric-rename) * [ ] Rename the on-disk dir + producer-file string constants in the same commit. * [ ] In the SAME migration that renames the DB row, DELETE a same-id `owner='first-party-bundle'` placeholder first (copy the snippet above). * [ ] Don’t forget `template_data->>'methodRef'` if the rubric has one — it’s a real stored field (unlike `rubricId`, which derives from `plan_slug`). * [ ] Verify no FK dependents before renaming `plan_slug` (it’s the PK); other tables reference it as a loose string and historical rows are meant to stay under the old id (an immutable log of what happened under that id).

# Rendering an operator-vite pane inside an apps/operator component

> The import direction between apps/operator and apps/operator-vite is one-way. When an operator-side shell must host a vite-side pane, invert the composition with a descriptor slot — plus the two things a moved left-rail pane silently loses.

You want to render a pane that lives in `apps/operator-vite/src` — a left-rail tab, an `/adv` panel, a voice surface — from a component that lives in `apps/operator`. The obvious import doesn’t work, and the reason isn’t visible at the import site. ## The constraint: the import direction is one-way [Section titled “The constraint: the import direction is one-way”](#the-constraint-the-import-direction-is-one-way) In `apps/operator-vite/vite.config.ts` the `@` alias resolves to `../operator` — **it points at a different app**: 
```ts
{ find: '@', replacement: operatorRoot },   // operatorRoot = apps/operator
```
 So: * `apps/operator-vite` → `apps/operator` — **fine**, that’s what `@/app/...` means from inside operator-vite. * `apps/operator` → `apps/operator-vite` — **impossible**. There is no alias pointing that way, and adding one would make the Next tree depend on the SPA shell that hosts it. This is the same trap [AGENT-ENV.md](/internal/docs/system/repo-conventions) records as the *cross-tree alias trap* (intra-app imports inside operator-vite must be relative, because `@/…` silently leaves the app). Here it bites from the other direction: the import you want simply cannot exist. The panes that trigger this are the ones importing operator-vite-local modules — `../adv/AgentsRunningPill`, `../voice-video/VideoGrid`, `@tanstack/react-router`. Moving the *file* into `apps/operator` doesn’t help: its imports come with it. ## The pattern: invert the composition with a descriptor slot [Section titled “The pattern: invert the composition with a descriptor slot”](#the-pattern-invert-the-composition-with-a-descriptor-slot) **The operator side exposes a slot. The operator-vite route fills it.** The operator component never learns what’s inside. This is the established convention, not a new invention: | Slot | Filled by | Introduced | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | | `QuickPanelPage({ headerSlot })` | `operator-vite/src/routes/quick-panel.tsx` | quick-panel-status-pills-2026-07-13 D-001 | | `OperatorChatSidebar({ faces })` → `ChromeShell({ chatFaces })` | `operator-vite/src/components/chat-faces/ChatFacesHost.tsx` | WI-5162 | A worked descriptor (`apps/operator/app/_components/op-chat-faces.ts`): 
```ts
export type OpChatFace = {
  id: string;                 // keys the ?opcv URL enum
  label: string;              // already lexicon-resolved by the provider
  tip: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
  render: () => ReactNode;    // a FUNCTION, not a node — see below
};
```
 Three things that made it work: 1. **`render` is a function, not a node.** A node prop would mount every pane eagerly. These sidebars are boot-critical and the panes open live `useSyncQuery`s, so an unpicked pane must not mount at all. Assert this in a test — `expect(render).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — it’s the kind of regression that costs boot latency silently. 2. **The host owns the state, the provider owns the identity.** URL state, pill chrome, lit/pressed state, the body swap: all host. The provider supplies only the id/label/icon/pane. Anything else and the two trees start negotiating. 3. **Guard id collisions when the id keys a URL enum.** `dedupeChatFaces` drops a face whose id shadows a built-in view (`chat`/`pot`/`inbox`) or an earlier face — otherwise `?opcv` goes ambiguous and two pills light at once. ## The gotcha: a moved left-rail pane loses two invisible inheritances [Section titled “The gotcha: a moved left-rail pane loses two invisible inheritances”](#the-gotcha-a-moved-left-rail-pane-loses-two-invisible-inheritances) The `pclsb-*` panes (`SwarmTab`, `VoiceTab`, …) were written assuming a `.pclsb` ancestor. Re-host them somewhere else and they render *almost* right — which is worse than obviously broken. They lose exactly two things: 1. **`--pclsb-current-accent`** — declared on `.pclsb` and overridden per `[data-tab="…"]`. Without it the pane’s accent falls back to the raw `#38bdf8` default. Note `swarm` and `voice` both resolve to `var(--accent)` (blue-frost) and **not** green — that’s WI-4789, an explicit owner correction (“the Fleet tab looks off”). Re-deriving the accent by eye silently reverts it. 2. **`.pclsb__body`’s scroll box** — `flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; padding: 4px 0 10px`. Without it the pane doesn’t scroll and grows its container. Re-supply both in a host wrapper and the panes need **zero** rewrite: 
```tsx
function ChatFacePane({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="pclsb-face-host">
      <style>{LEFT_SIDEBAR_CSS}</style>
      <style>{CHAT_FACE_PANE_CSS}</style>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}
```
 
```css
.pclsb-face-host {
  --pclsb-current-accent: var(--accent, #38bdf8); /* from .pclsb */
  flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto;         /* from .pclsb__body */
  padding: 4px 0 10px;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
}
```
 Re-injecting `LEFT_SIDEBAR_CSS` while the rail is *also* mounted is harmless — same rules, same cascade, and `<style>` dedupes nothing but costs nothing. ## Unrelated but adjacent: never put backticks in a CSS template literal [Section titled “Unrelated but adjacent: never put backticks in a CSS template literal”](#unrelated-but-adjacent-never-put-backticks-in-a-css-template-literal) The styles in this area live in tagged template literals (`OP_CHAT_SIDEBAR_CSS`, `LEFT_SIDEBAR_CSS`). Writing a markdown-style `` `code` `` span in a comment **inside** one terminates the literal: 
```plaintext
ERROR: Expected ";" but found "potLabel"
  Label widths by sidebar width, `potLabel:wordmark:fleetLabel`:
                                  ^
```
 The whole file fails to parse and `test:file` reports it as *unmatched* rather than failed. In WI-5162 this landed **after** the per-file suite had already gone green (the comment was a later edit), so only `npm run test:affected` caught it — a reminder that a green from before your last edit is not a green. ## Testing the seam [Section titled “Testing the seam”](#testing-the-seam) * Test the **slot** on the operator side with stand-in descriptors — no operator-vite import needed, which is the point of the seam. * Test the **removal** on the vite side, and delete the `vi.mock` for the panes you moved out. In `LeftSidebar.test.tsx` the stubs for `SwarmTab`/`VoiceTab` were removed deliberately: a stub would let a regression that re-mounts them pass silently. * Assert the **stale deep-link**. A bookmarked `?lst=swarm` must fall back to the default tab, not wedge the rail on a tab that no longer exists (nuqs’ `parseAsStringLiteral` does this for free once the id leaves the list — but assert it, because the list is what changed). ## See also [Section titled “See also”](#see-also) * [repo-conventions](/internal/docs/system/repo-conventions) — the deployment model and why the SPA is the desktop’s content layer, not a separable app. * [agent-e2e](/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e) — verifying the result in the Tauri shell (§1.3 for your own isolated instance; never drive the owner’s window).

# Replay-consumer loops must not re-ledger battery spend

> runGovernedReplay already ledgers every battery dollar on frontier:replay-harness — a consumer loop (regret/transfer/ablation) that also records the returned totalCostUsd on its own governor loop double-counts it on the one visible spend number.

**The trap.** The frontier consumer loops (regret mining FB-07, transfer harness FB-08, shadow ablation FB-09) run student/counterfactual batteries through `runGovernedReplay` (`packages/operator-core/lib/replay/governed.ts`). That wrapper ALREADY calls `recordLearningSpend` with the battery’s `totalCostUsd` on loop `frontier:replay-harness` (accumulate:true, origin=‘replay’). The returned `ReplayBatteryResult.totalCostUsd` is there for *reporting* — if your loop also ledgers it on its own governor loop, the same dollar lands twice in `summarizeLearningSpend().totalSpentUsd` (D-004’s “one visible number”), and your loop’s lifetime budget exhausts at half its real allowance. **The rule.** A consumer loop ledgers on its own loop id ONLY the spend it generates *outside* the battery (the transfer harness: distillation LLM calls). Battery spend belongs to `frontier:replay-harness` — that loop’s owner-set budget is the chokepoint for ALL replay consumers, by design (FB-06). Surface battery cost in your tick report from `totalCostUsd`, don’t re-record it. **How FB-08 wires it** (`lib/transfer/tick.ts` testLeg + `replay-adapter.ts`): the tick’s `recordSpend` port is called for distillation refs only; the adapter routes batteries through `runGovernedReplay` and returns the cost purely for the log line. **Corollary for arming (P-001).** A consumer loop needs BOTH budgets set to actually run: its own loop (distillation/selection spend) AND `frontier:replay-harness` (battery spend) — plus both flags. An armed consumer with a dark/unbudgeted replay loop fails its tests with “governed replay refused (replay-dark)” — that’s the designed refusal, not a bug.

# Replication-liveness detector: live debugging, the per-join counter blind spot, and the pre-admission blind window

> Why the replication-liveness detector is SILENT — how to read the WI-1840 registry on a live sidecar (RPC, socket path, PG creds), and the two blind-spot classes behind a quiet detector: per-join swarm-connection counters that cannot see pre-existing sockets, and the pre-admission window where zero admitted logs means the sampler never runs at all (announce channel never pairs, no announce, no admission, no zombie/no_replicator/frozen axis). Includes the announce-channel stage-count funnel recipe and why connection churn shorter than the grace is NOT the cause.

Written 2026-07-04 (su-b5d1c, plan `shared-pot-p2p-release-readiness-2026-07-03` P-004 / WI-1840, WI-183 class). Two things live here: the **diagnostic recipe** for the replication-liveness detector on a live frame, and the **blind-spot class** its first live proof exposed. ## The one-line lesson [Section titled “The one-line lesson”](#the-one-line-lesson) **A detector’s own liveness must be live-proven.** WI-1840’s `connected_never_replicated` axis was 17/17 green in-process and completely silent on a live rig with a genuine stall in front of it (run `m1783120511`). In-process green ≠ live green applies to the watchdog, not just the watched. ## The blind-spot class: per-join counters on shared event emitters [Section titled “The blind-spot class: per-join counters on shared event emitters”](#the-blind-spot-class-per-join-counters-on-shared-event-emitters) `joinHarnessSwarm` (operator-core `lib/sync/hyperbee/swarm.ts`) hand-rolled a `liveConnectionCount` (`++` on `'connection'`, `--` on socket `close`). Two mechanisms make such a counter read 0 while a peer is demonstrably replicating: 1. **Shared-swarm dedup** — one Hyperswarm instance serves every topic and emits `'connection'` ONCE per peer socket. A join registered AFTER the socket exists never sees the event (the interface doc on `HyperswarmLike.connections` states exactly this). 2. **Rekey reset** — the pot first-join `rekey()` replaces the handle with a fresh join whose counter starts at 0; live sockets don’t re-emit. Result: the merge-pass sampler fed `swarmConnections: 0` → the axis treated the node as offline (never alarms, by design) → silence in exactly the zombie-connection scenario the axis exists for. **Fix (landed):** the handle getter prefers the swarm’s OWN live set — `swarm.connections.size` — with the counter only as a fallback for minimal test fakes. Generalize: when a shared emitter exposes authoritative live state, **read the state, don’t shadow it with event arithmetic**. Regression pins in `__tests__/swarm.test.ts` (“shared-swarm late join”) and the b8 matrix scenario (a red-SLA soak now asserts the detector line exists — a silent detector on a real stall self-announces as `DETECTOR REGRESSION`). ## Diagnostic recipe: read the live registry on a frame [Section titled “Diagnostic recipe: read the live registry on a frame”](#diagnostic-recipe-read-the-live-registry-on-a-frame) The registry lives in whichever process runs the merge loop — under `papercusp-substrate-sidecar` (default-ON on rig frames, WI-1994) that is the sidecar child, and its console output lands in `serve.log` prefixed `[substrate-sidecar]` / `[substrate-sidecar-err]`. 1. **Grep the fire line** (what the b8 scenario pins): 
   ```plaintext
   grep "replication-liveness" /home/pcusp/serve.log
   # [replication-liveness] replication_stalled (connected_never_replicated) harness=… swarm has N live connection(s) …
   ```
 2. **Read the registry** — JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-framed, over the sidecar’s unix socket (`/tmp/papercusp-substrate-<spawner-pid>.sock`); no auth: 
   ```plaintext
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"substrate:getReplicationLiveness","params":{},"id":1}
   ```
 Key fields per log: `verdict` (`live` / `never_connected` / `no_replicator` / `frozen` / `sampling_stale` — a FIRED connected-never latch derives `no_replicator`), `peersCount`, `msSinceSampled` (\~1s when the merge poll is healthy — a big value means the merge loop itself is dead), and **`lastSwarmConnections`** — the exact value the axis saw on the last sample. `null` = the sampler never passed one (axis disabled at the source); `0` while a peer is connected = the counter blind spot above. 3. **Durable escalation** — EIs land in `harness_shared.engineer_issues` (`psql 'postgresql://harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:39532/papercusp'` on a rig frame; note the id column is `issue_id`, not `id`). One open EI per (harness, log, kind); rows federate to peers once replication heals. 4. **Admin HTTP route** (`/api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status`) is trust-gated: bare loopback curl gets 403 `unverified-loopback`. Bearer the frame’s superuser token (`/home/pcusp/.papercusp/superuser-token`, the `rig_ban_member` pattern in `deb-hetzner-rig.sh`). The RPC socket needs none. ## Grace/churn semantics (why the axis is quiet when it should be) [Section titled “Grace/churn semantics (why the axis is quiet when it should be)”](#gracechurn-semantics-why-the-axis-is-quiet-when-it-should-be) * Fire requires `swarmConnections > 0` samples accumulating ≥ 3min (`DEFAULT_LIVENESS_GRACE_MS`) on a log with **zero replicator attach this process lifetime**. Zombie connections churn (\~10s lives), so swarm=0 resets the window only after 60s sustained (`SWARM_CHURN_TOLERANCE_MS`). * Edge-triggered once per latch; recovery (a real replicator attach) re-arms. * The axis never fires when the substrate/swarm never came up (`swarmConnections` undefined) — genuinely-offline peers must not page. Related: the WI-183 stale-DHT-announce zombie-window mechanism (root cause the detector exists to catch) is written up on WI-183 / ledger row 13 of `shared-pot-release-testing/RELEASE-READINESS.md`. ## The PRE-ADMISSION blind window — read this before blaming the grace [Section titled “The PRE-ADMISSION blind window — read this before blaming the grace”](#the-pre-admission-blind-window--read-this-before-blaming-the-grace) Added 2026-07-25 (su-055ae, EI-18662944242304583). **The single most likely way you will misdiagnose a silent detector.** `sampleReplicationLiveness` is called at `boot.ts:2404`, inside `for (const log of admitted.values())` (`boot.ts:2363`). So with **zero admitted remote logs the sampler is never invoked and all three axes are dead code** — not quiet, *never executed*. Admission requires an announce; an announce requires a paired announce channel. Everything above is therefore invisible from down here, and “wedged” and “healthy” emit the identical observable (silence). **Do not reason about the grace until you have confirmed the log was being sampled at all.** Gate run 20260725-183831 was first filed as a grace defect (“connections die at 13s, the grace is 15s, so the axis can never see them”). That is wrong twice over: 1. `connectedNeverReplSinceMs` (`replication-liveness.ts:203`) is a **per-LOG** window, not per-connection. It is armed on the first sample with `swarmConnections > 0` and *survives* connection churn — it resets only after `SWARM_CHURN_TOLERANCE_MS` (60s) of **sustained** swarm=0. Churn shorter than the grace does not hide anything; the churn tolerance exists precisely so it can’t. 2. The real cause was that **nothing was ever admitted for 20.5 minutes**. The detector fired correctly 15s after its first opportunity. Corollary for fixes: a new leg added to the zombie axis **cannot** catch a pre-admission failure, because it would live inside the loop that never runs. Detection for this window has to sit at the swarm layer — which is what `joinHarnessSwarm`’s escalation rung (c) now does (`DEFAULT_SUBSTRATE_UNPAIRED_ESCALATION_MS`, pinned by `swarm-unpaired-announce-escalation.test.ts`): live connections + N announce- channel open attempts + never once paired ⇒ loud signal + forced topic rejoin. ### Diagnostic recipe: count the announce-channel STAGES [Section titled “Diagnostic recipe: count the announce-channel STAGES”](#diagnostic-recipe-count-the-announce-channel-stages) This is what cracked it — stage counts separate “never reached” from “reached and failed” in one pass. On a frame’s `serve.log`: 
```bash
for p in "announce-debug] mux mux=" "announce-debug] create mux=" \
         "announce-debug] open topic=" "announce-debug] recv topic=" \
         "announce_admitted"; do
  printf '%s\tfirst=%s\t%s\n' "$(grep -c "$p" serve.log)" \
    "$(grep -o "^\[[0-9T:.Z-]*\].*$p" serve.log | head -1 | cut -c2-25)" "$p"
done
```
 Read it as a funnel — the stage where the count collapses to 0 is the fault: | stage | meaning | 20260725-183831 (frame a) | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | | `mux mux=` | peer connections observed | 188 | | `create mux=` | we created + `open()`d a channel | 91 | | `open topic=` | Protomux `onopen` — channel **PAIRED** | **0 until 23:07:16** | | `recv topic=` | any inbound frame | **0 until 23:07:16** | | `announce_admitted` | admission (detector becomes able to run) | **0 until 23:07:16** | 188 connections, 91 open attempts, and not one frame in either direction for 20.5 minutes = a dead data path behind sockets Hyperswarm reported as connected. `open topic=` collapsing while `create mux=` is healthy is the signature of this class. If instead `create mux=` is 0, look at `openAnnounceChannel`’s early return (a reader with neither `onAnnounce` nor `ourAnnounce` opens no channel at all). ⚠ A connection dying at a fixed, repeatable sub-grace interval (\~13.0s here, `precededByError: 'connection timed out'`) is a **consequence** of the dead data path, not the cause of the silence: no ACK ever returns, so UDX gives up (hyperdht sets the stream keepAlive to 5000ms — `hyperdht/index.js:21`). The exact give-up arithmetic is in libudx’s C, which is not vendored here. Don’t tune a grace against it.

# Repo-less pot data layer: member-repo resolution, per-pot outbox-drain, dead-executor reaper

> A kind:'pot' harness can be repo-LESS — its code lives in a MEMBER repo (e.g. papercusp's member is papercup). Three facets must resolve that correctly or the pot looks broken: (1) repo-backed surfaces (Docs/Tests) must read the member repo, not the empty pot dir; (2) the pot must arm its OWN cross-pot-outbox-drain on create or its substrate_outbox grows unbounded; (3) the DBOS routine scheduler must survive dead-executor dedup wedges (the reaper) or NOTHING fires — including the drain. All three were the root of papercusp looking half-broken on 2026-06-19.

## The shape [Section titled “The shape”](#the-shape) A `kind:'pot'` harness can be **repo-less**: it has no git working tree of its own; its code/docs/tests live in a **member** repo. Anything that resolves a harness to on-disk files or runs its automation must account for this, or the pot looks broken even though its data is intact. Three facets, all fixed 2026-06-19: > **Update (2026-06-20 — Option-B merge):** papercusp itself is no longer the running example of a repo-less pot. The operator-home pot and its dogfood repo (`papercup`) were merged into **ONE** registry entry, marked `self_repo: true` (`ProjectEntry.self_repo` in `harness-registry.ts`) — the home pot now IS its own checkout, not a repo-less state dir borrowing a separate member. `resolveHarnessContentPath` short-circuits for a `self_repo` hive: it returns the harness’s **own** `project.path` and never looks for a member, so a stray project that set `hive_slug` to the home pot can’t hijack its docs/tests/source reads. Everything below (facets #1-3) still applies in full to a genuinely repo-less pot (a fresh `pot:create` without `linkExisting`/`requiresRepo`) — papercusp is just no longer that example. ## 1. Repo-backed surfaces resolve the MEMBER repo [Section titled “1. Repo-backed surfaces resolve the MEMBER repo”](#1-repo-backed-surfaces-resolve-the-member-repo) Docs and Tests read a harness’s on-disk repo. For a repo-less pot the registry `project.path` is the (near-empty) pot state dir → blank tabs. **Fix:** `resolveHarnessContentPath(reg, slug)` in `packages/operator-core/lib/harness-registry.ts` returns, for a `kind:'pot'` harness, its **member repo’s** path — UNLESS the pot itself is `self_repo` (the Option-B merge case above), in which case it returns the pot’s own `project.path` directly and skips the member lookup entirely. For a normal repo harness (not a pot at all) it likewise falls straight through to `project.path`. Applied at every repo-backed resolver: * docs MCP tools — `agent-tools/docs/{outline,search,get}.ts` * docs HTTP endpoint — `harness/docs/harness-repo.ts` `resolveHarnessRepoRoot` (feeds `buildMergedDocs` / the Docs tab) * testing endpoints — `endpoint-route/routes/harness/testing.ts` `resolveCtx` (Tests tab + `/file-status`, `/health-strip`, `/domain-detail`) Result: papercusp’s Docs (426 pages) + Tests (36 domains) now match papercup. The fallback is exact for non-pot harnesses, so this is additive. ## 2. A pot arms its OWN cross-pot-outbox-drain on create [Section titled “2.
