The report distinguishes an operational `rotation_strand` (a previously-authenticated spawn whose key was rotated out from under it — must be re-spawned) from an `unverified` first-seen/malformed/escalation attempt, because a rotation and a forged-URL attack both surface as `invalid_signature` on the next verify. To tell them apart the process remembers the spawns it has successfully verified (`verifiedSpawns`, capped at 4000), so a later signature failure for one of them is definitively a strand, not an attack. The route can also **opt into active remediation** (`RotateSpawnSigningKeyOptions`, WI-3194): stop/relaunch eligible nursery spawns whose verified URL was just invalidated, capped at `ROTATION_REMEDIATION_CAP` (25). Direct unit callers keep the historical rotate-only behavior; the orchestrator re-spawns anything the remediation didn’t cover. ### Read the verification audit log [Section titled “Read the verification audit log”](#read-the-verification-audit-log) 
```bash
TOKEN=$(cat ~/.papercusp/superuser-token)
curl "http://localhost:3070/api/admin/spawn-signing/failures?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
 Query params: `limit` (max 1000, default 100), `since` (ISO timestamp), `reason` (filter). Returns `{ rows, summary: { byReason, window } }`. A non-zero rate of `invalid_signature` outside explicit test runs is a real signal. Correlate `claimed_spawn` with orchestrator spawn IDs to identify the culprit. ## When to stop and ask [Section titled “When to stop and ask”](#when-to-stop-and-ask) You should stop and ask before doing any of these: * The component you want to wrap doesn’t fit one of the four shipped plugin shapes (subprocess single-tool, HTTP+optional-secret, subprocess multi-tool, HTTP+required-secret-with-schema). Don’t invent a fifth shape; the function-as-truth design doc lists which patterns are blessed. * You want to extend the manifest contract with a new field. Each existing field corresponds to a dispatcher behavior; adding one is an architecture decision, not a cleanup. * You hit one of the known open issues and need to work around it. The workaround usually masks a real bug — better to surface it and get the framework fix. * The handler signature you’d want isn’t `(input, ctx) => ToolResult`. The framework can’t accommodate exotic shapes. If you want a callback-based contract, a multi-response stream, or anything else non-request/response, it doesn’t belong here. * You’re tempted to delete a route a UI surface still fetches from. **Always grep for UI callers first.** The legacy Next app-router routes are gone — `apps/operator/app/api` is now an empty leftover directory with no `route.ts` files anywhere under `apps/operator`; everything is now a `defineTool` route under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes`, served at `/api/plugins/<plugin>/<tool>`. The migration is complete, but the rule stands for any route you’re about to remove: switch UI URLs in the same PR, and delete only when zero callers remain. ## Per-tool migration checklist [Section titled “Per-tool migration checklist”](#per-tool-migration-checklist) When you’re moving an existing route to the endpoint system, run through this list. Each step is mandatory; skip any and you ship a broken tool: 1. Grep for UI callers of the legacy route. Decide replace-with-redirect or full-delete. 2. If new PG schema, write the SQL file in `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/` and apply it manually. 3. Write the typed function with no transport awareness. 4. Write the manifest entry. JSON Schema directly. No `zodToJsonSchema`. 5. `curl` the HTTP transport. Verify status code + body shape. 6. `curl` the MCP transport. Verify the same. 7. `psql` the telemetry row. Verify `status='ok'` and `app.workspace_id` was set. 8. Quota smoke test: fire perChunk+1 → second is 429. 9. Role gate smoke test: wrong role → 403. 10. `curl /api/plugins/host/refresh`. Confirm error count unchanged. 11. Delete the legacy route in the same commit (only if step 1 said zero UI callers). 12. Submodule commit first if you touched `libs/papercusp/`, then bump the parent’s submodule pointer in a second commit. ## Per-turn commit discipline [Section titled “Per-turn commit discipline”](#per-turn-commit-discipline) When you’re working across the operator app and the `libs/papercusp/` submodule: * Commit the submodule first. * Bump the parent’s submodule pointer in a second commit. Otherwise the parent commit references a submodule SHA that isn’t pushed and the next agent sees a broken checkout. This is observed-from-experience guidance; multiple agents have shipped half-broken trees by inverting the order.

# Overview

> One function, three transports — what the endpoint system is and why we built it this way.

## The one-line version [Section titled “The one-line version”](#the-one-line-version) You write **one typed function**. The framework projects it onto: * An **HTTP route** at `/api/plugins/<plugin>/<tool>` (or `/api/agent-tools/<tool>` for built-ins) * An **MCP `tools/call` entry** under `<plugin>.<tool>` (or `<scope>:<verb>` for built-ins) * An **in-process call** any TypeScript caller can `await` directly You declare exposure, role allowlist, capabilities, and quotas in a manifest. The framework handles auth gating, role enforcement, quota windows, telemetry persistence, streaming progress, and per-spawn URL context — none of which you write per tool. ## Why “endpoint system” not “MCP migration” [Section titled “Why “endpoint system” not “MCP migration””](#why-endpoint-system-not-mcp-migration) The first instinct was to call this an MCP migration. That framing is wrong. **The function is the source of truth.** HTTP and MCP are projections of it. Once a function is decoupled from any specific transport, all three callers — your dashboard, an AI agent over MCP, another module in the same Node process — get it for free, with the same auth/role/quota/telemetry behavior. The hard part isn’t writing the MCP wrapper. The hard part is pulling a function out of its current transport-coupled form so that the wrapper *can be* generated. The “MCP-callable” part is the smallest-and-easiest consequence of that decoupling. ## What this gets you [Section titled “What this gets you”](#what-this-gets-you) * **No duplicated route+handler code.** A new feature is one typed function plus six lines of manifest. Both the dashboard and the agent get it. * **Single test surface.** You test the function. Both transports inherit correct behavior because they both go through the same dispatcher. * **Uniform observability.** Every invocation lands in `harness_shared.tool_invocations` with role, window key, status, duration, output size — regardless of transport. You can answer “which agents called which tools when” without per-route instrumentation. * **Uniform gating.** Role allowlist, capability check, and per-window quota all enforce in the same dispatcher. Adding a new sensitive tool means setting `roles: ["operator"]` + `rolesQuota: { operator: { perRun: 5 } }` and you’re done. * **Stream-or-not, no rewrite.** A function that calls `ctx.progress(pct, msg)` automatically gets MCP `notifications/progress` events on the MCP transport and SSE events on the HTTP transport. No transport-specific wiring. * **Token-efficient by default.** A function returns structured `data`; the dispatcher serializes it in the most compact format the data’s shape allows (TOON for arrays, lossless JSON otherwise) — agents read ≈ −20–35% fewer tokens on list results with no change to how they call. Declaring `result: <schema>` unlocks CSV + MCP `outputSchema` advertisement. See [Transports → Result formats](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/transports). ## What this is not [Section titled “What this is not”](#what-this-is-not) * Not a replacement for SSE chat, WebSocket voice, or anything else that holds a long-lived bidirectional connection. Those stay on dedicated routes; the endpoint system is for request → response (with optional streamed progress). * Not a way to expose your dashboard to the public internet. The trust model is **loopback bind + HMAC-signed per-spawn URL params** (see [Spawn-URL signing](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/spawn-signing)), suitable for local dev + Tauri desktop. Off-loopback exposure needs a real principal/auth layer in front, since same-UID code can still read the signing key from PG. * Not a generic RPC framework. The contract is narrow on purpose: `(input, ctx) => ToolResult`. Trying to make it accommodate exotic shapes (callbacks, multi-response, file uploads >5MB) defeats the point of having one function as truth. ## The route projection — `defineTool` also defines plumbing [Section titled “The route projection — defineTool also defines plumbing”](#the-route-projection--definetool-also-defines-plumbing) Not every endpoint is an agent tool. The browser, the desktop shell, an orchestrator, a webhook — they call **routes**: HTTP plumbing that must *not* appear in the agent tool catalog. `defineTool` produces those too. `defineTool` accepts a **route-shaped** input — discriminated by the `method` field — and returns a `RouteDefinition` instead of a `ToolDefinition`: 
```ts
defineTool({
  method: 'GET',
  path: '/desktop/version',
  auth: 'public',                    // or a PrincipalRequirements gate
  input: z.object({ verbose: z.coerce.boolean().optional() }), // optional
  handler(req, ctx) {                // Web-standard Request in, Response out
    return Response.json({ version: '…' });
  },
});
```
 A route runs through the same cross-cutting machinery — auth, input validation, timeout, telemetry, uniform errors — but it is **not** projected onto the MCP catalog. `tools/list` never sees it; an agent cannot call it. That guarantee is what keeps plumbing out of the agent surface. Two route-level knobs tune that machinery. A route defaults to a **30s wall-clock timeout** — a wedged handler aborts; pass `timeoutSec: null` to disable the watchdog for long-lived SSE/streaming routes whose handler legitimately outlives any fixed budget. Telemetry defaults to `sampleRate: 1` (record every call); lower it (`0..1`) for high-frequency polled routes, or set `0` to never record. Route files import `defineTool` directly — the former `defineRoute` alias was **removed** when the primitives were unified (Phase E6, `endpoint-unification-2026-05-21`). A route is *declared* with `defineTool` and *mounted* host-side by `registerRoute` (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/`). ### Paired-phone routes — `auth: { kind: ['device'] }` + `cors` [Section titled “Paired-phone routes — auth: { kind: \['device'\] } + cors”](#paired-phone-routes--auth--kind-device---cors) A route reachable from the paired phone declares the device-JWT auth gate and opts into cross-origin reachability — there is no implicit folding: 
```ts
defineTool({
  method: 'POST', path: '/device/heartbeat',
  auth: { kind: ['device'] },        // gate on the device-JWT principal
  cors: true,                        // CORS allowlist (paired-device + tauri + localhost)
  handler(req, ctx) { /* ctx.principal is the device */ },
});
```
 `cors: true` mounts the shared CORS middleware (OPTIONS preflight + headers); `auth: { kind: ['device'] }` makes the route-stack reject anything that doesn’t resolve to a device principal. Paired-phone routes live under `/api/device/*`. Built-in tools are reachable from the phone for free — the device JWT is a bearer token, and the `/api/agent-tools/*` catch-all resolves it like any other. ## Two channels at a glance [Section titled “Two channels at a glance”](#two-channels-at-a-glance) A tool handler has two outbound channels available, projected uniformly across transports: | Channel | API | Wire | Replay on reconnect | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | | **Events** | `ctx.emit('name', payload)`, `ctx.progress(pct, msg)` | typed SSE events / MCP notifications | Ring buffer (T2.2), bounded by `replayBufferSize` | | **State** | `ctx.askUser(spec)`, `ctx.publishState(snapshot)` | `state-snapshot` SSE on `/api/operator/state-snapshot` | Current snapshot only — replay does not re-prompt | Cards (`ctx.askUser`) and tool state (`ctx.publishState`) live on the state channel because they’re not append-only — a reconnecting client wants the latest answered/unanswered card state, not history of every snapshot. The two installs have different conditions: `ctx.askUser` is installed whenever the call has a `workspaceId + runId` (always present for HTTP-projected calls), but `ctx.publishState` is installed only when the tool *also* declares a `state` schema. A tool with no `state` schema gets `ctx.publishState === undefined` even on an HTTP-projected call — publish snapshots from a state-shaped tool, and use `ctx.emit` otherwise. See [ctx.askUser](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/ask-user) and [state-shaped tools](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/state-tools). ## How it’s packaged [Section titled “How it’s packaged”](#how-its-packaged) The endpoint system started life inside `@papercusp/agent-mcp`. It has since been **carved into a host-agnostic engine plus thin adapters** (plan `papercusp-tooldef-extraction-2026-05-29`), so the same dispatcher can be used outside Papercusp: | Package | Role | | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **`@papercusp/tooldef`** | The engine — `defineTool`, the registry, the dispatch pipeline, the state/card/replay channels, OpenAPI assembly, core types. **Zero host-coupled deps**: no PG / Next / `@restart`. Its only `@papercusp/*` deps are three host-agnostic `libs/generic/` libs (`chat-protocol`, `result-encoding`, `rules`). Validator-agnostic ([Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev)); every host-specific rule is injected (table below). | | **`@papercusp/tooldef-http`** | The HTTP transport adapter (`handleHttpToolRequest` / `…Streaming`). Resolves a request → tool, builds the ctx from `X-Papercusp-*` headers, dispatches. Depends only on the engine + `@papercusp/sse`. | | **`@papercusp/ipc-endpoint-server`** | The IPC (unix-socket) transport adapter. IPC exposure is **opt-in per tool** via `expose: { ipc: true }` in `defineTool` — unlike HTTP + MCP, which project automatically. | | **`@papercusp/tooldef-mcp`** | The MCP transport bridge primitives — generic `mcp-handler` `extra` extractors (`bearerFromExtra` / `urlFromExtra` / `headersFromExtra`) plus a projected-dispatch→MCP-result mapper (extracted under P-031). The host-specific auth + spawn-context assembly stays in the host route layer. | | **`@papercusp/agent-mcp`** | The **Papercusp host adapter** — supplies the injected deps (PG-backed quota/telemetry, the role config, quota-window policy, capability→tier table, gate-bypass mapping) and re-exports the engine + HTTP surface so existing import sites are untouched. The **generic MCP-bridge glue** now lives in `@papercusp/tooldef-mcp`; only the host-specific spawn-context auth and HMAC spawn *verification* stay in the operator route layer (`packages/operator-core/lib/spawn-signing.ts`, wired in the transport `_mcp-handler`). | Everything Papercusp-specific is a **host-injected seam** with a generic engine default: | Concern | Seam | Engine default | | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | | Roles | augment the `RoleRegistry` interface → shapes `AgentRole` | `string` (any role) | | Quota window + ceiling | `DispatchProjectedDeps.computeQuotaWindow(ctx, roleQuota)` | run-scoped / `perRun` | | Capability → tier | `setCapabilityTierResolver` (read via `tierFor`) | `'low'` | | Gate bypass (privileged callers) | `ctx.gateBypass { role?, capability?, quota? }` | absent ⇒ all gates enforce | | Schema validation | `args` / `state` / card `dataSchema` typed `StandardSchemaV1`; `standardValidate` | any Standard Schema validator | | Schema → JSON Schema | `setJsonSchemaAdapter` (read via `toJsonSchema`) | Zod 4 `toJSONSchema` | | Quota / telemetry I/O | `DispatchProjectedDeps.readQuotaState` / `recordInvocation` | no-ops | | Transaction handle | `ToolContext<Tx = any>` | `any` | The engine is provably standalone — see `libs/generic/tooldef/examples/standalone-inprocess.ts` (registers + dispatches a tool importing **only** `@papercusp/tooldef`). It is also mirrored to a standalone `Papercusp/tooldef` repo for external consumers. ## Where to read next [Section titled “Where to read next”](#where-to-read-next) * [Function-as-truth](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/function-as-truth) — the architectural spine: why the function comes first * [Writing a tool](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/writing-a-tool) — the recipe for built-ins and plugins, end to end * [Transports](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/transports) — how MCP, HTTP, IPC, and in-process callers all reach the same function * [Voice modality](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/voice-modality) — how tools surface in the ElevenLabs Conv AI integration and how cards collapse to `fallbackText` on voice * [ctx.askUser](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/ask-user) — interactive prompts mid-run; the state channel; `askUserLocal` client-only variant * [State-shaped tools](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/state-tools) — `ctx.publishState`; when to publish snapshots instead of streaming events * [Gating](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/gating) — auth, capabilities, roles, quotas — what blocks what when * [Spawn-URL signing](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/spawn-signing) — HMAC verification of the seven per-spawn URL params; what it defends against and what it doesn’t * [Telemetry](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/telemetry) — `tool_invocations` schema and how to read it * [Operations](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/operations) — host refresh, hot reload, common failure modes * [Superuser mode](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/superuser-mode) — `?superuser=1` loopback escape hatch for dev/admin scripts * [Tool catalog](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/tool-catalog) — every projected tool snapshot (live source: `/settings/plugins/tools`) * [Reference](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/reference) — manifest schema, error codes, file map * [Agents → Prompt assembly](/internal/docs/agents/prompt-assembly) — adjacent layer: how a role’s system prompt is built from persona, tools catalog (powered by `defineTool({ guidance })`), and role playbook

# Reference

> Manifest schema, error codes, file map, capability conventions. Lookup material.

## Manifest schema (plugin tool entry) [Section titled “Manifest schema (plugin tool entry)”](#manifest-schema-plugin-tool-entry) 
```jsonc
{
  // Required
  "name":        "do_thing",                   // Identifier within the plugin
  "description": "One-sentence description.",  // Shown in tools/list to agents
  "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "..." },  // JSON Schema — use Zod 4's z.toJSONSchema, never zodToJsonSchema


  // Strongly recommended
  "capabilities": ["http:fetch:example.com"],  // Descriptive on plugins, enforced on built-ins
  "roles":        ["worker", "architect"],     // Role allowlist — empty/missing means "no role gate"
  "rolesQuota":   { "worker": { "perChunk": 1 } },  // Per-window quota; reads usually don't need this
  "timeoutSec":   60,                          // Default 60 if omitted


  // Streaming + state
  "events": {                                  // Typed event vocabulary; surfaced on tools/list
    "delta":     { "type": "string" },         // z.string() → raw text on the SSE wire
    "tool_call": { "type": "object", "..." }   // any object → JSON-encoded
  },
  "replayBufferSize":  100,                    // Ring-buffer size for Last-Event-ID resume. Default 0 = no replay.
  "idleTimeoutSec":    120,                    // Abort if no event emitted for N seconds. Default unset.
  "state":             { /* JSON-Schema for ctx.publishState payload */ },  // Declares state-shaped tool (auto opt-out of replay buffer; auto-streamable)
  "modality":          ["text", "voice"],      // Surface filter for prompt-assembly catalog. Default (absent) = ["text", "voice"] — visible in both catalogs.
  "guidance": {                                // Rendered into prompt-assembly tools catalog
    "when":      "User asks to <X>; pair with <Y> for the chained-list case.",
    "notWhen":   "Not for <Z> — use <other_tool> instead.",
    "chaining":  "After <prerequisite_tool>; before <successor_tool>."
  },


  // Optional — exposure overrides
  "expose": {
    "http": {
      "path":    "/api/plugins/my-plugin/do_thing",  // Default: /api/plugins/<short-name>/<tool.name>
      "methods": ["POST"]                            // Default: ["POST"]
    },
    "mcp": {
      "name":         "my-plugin.do_thing",          // Default: <short-name>.<tool.name>
      "streaming":    true,                          // Explicit streamability opt-in. Also implied by declared events or state.
      "largeOutput":  true                           // Hint that output may be written to scratch dir
    },
    "slash": {                                       // Slash-command projection via MCP prompts. DEFAULT ON for
      "name":        "do-thing",                     //   every MCP-exposed tool; `false` opts out entirely.
      "description": "Run the thing.",               //   See transports → "Slash exposure".
      "args":        ["target"]                      //   Restrict which scalar inputs become prompt arguments.
    }
  }
}
```
 If `expose.*` is omitted entirely, the framework picks defaults for both. If you want only one transport, declare only that one. (`expose.slash` defaults ON whenever the tool is MCP-exposed — it is a catalog projection, not a transport; see [Transports → Slash exposure](/internal/docs/endpoint-system/transports#slash-exposure--the-tool-catalog-as-slash-commands).) Built-in `defineTool` calls accept the same fields as TS/Zod (`state: z.object({...})`, `events: { delta: z.string(), ... }`, etc.). The `RoleToolDefinitionInput` shape is the canonical authority — see `libs/generic/tooldef/src/types.ts`. ## Error codes [Section titled “Error codes”](#error-codes) | Code | HTTP | Meaning | | ------------------------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | `unauthorized` | 401 | Built-in tool, no bearer / invalid bearer | | `role_not_allowed` | 403 | Plugin tool, role not in allowlist | | `missing_capability` | 403 | Built-in tool, principal missing required capability | | `quota_exceeded` | 429 | Window count ≥ limit | | `invalid_input` | 400 | Function threw a typed input-validation error | | `timeout` | 504 | AbortController fired before function returned | | `unknown_tool` | 404 | No projection registered at this path/name | | `method_not_allowed` | 405 | HTTP method not in `expose.http.methods` | | `handler_error` | 500 | Function threw an unhandled error | | `invalid_request_context` | 400 | MCP call missing required URL spawn params | | `invalid_bearer` | 401 | (MCP) Bearer didn’t resolve to a principal | For MCP transport, errors return `{ result: { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'code: message' }], isError: true } }` rather than HTTP status codes. The codes are the same. ## Capability conventions [Section titled “Capability conventions”](#capability-conventions) Capability strings should namespace by intent. Existing patterns: * `tools:<plugin>:<verb>` — ownership marker for plugin-contributed tools (`tools:repomix:pack`, `tools:web:fetch_clean`) * `compute:exec:<bin>` — subprocess execution (`compute:exec:repomix`, `compute:exec:npx`); enforces `ctx.spawn(bin, ...)` to a basename match * `http:fetch:<host>` — outbound HTTP fetch to a specific host (`http:fetch:r.jina.ai`, `http:fetch:api.firecrawl.dev`) * `secrets:read:<NAME>` — explicit secret access (`secrets:read:FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`) * `<scope>:read` / `<scope>:write` — built-in tool capabilities (`audit:read`, `tasks:write`) * `events:emit:<name>` / `events:listen:<name>` — pub-sub event bus Don’t consolidate capabilities into a single `secrets:*` or `compute:*` namespace. Granular grants exist so a future principal/auth model can selectively allow `secrets:read:FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` without granting access to all secrets. ## Role names [Section titled “Role names”](#role-names) Agents pass one of these as the `?role=` URL param: | Role | Quota window | Typical use | | ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | `worker` | `chunk:<id>` | Implements one feature per chunk | | `validator` | `run:<id>` | Tests the worker’s output | | `scoper` | `run:<id>` | Generates feature plans + validation contracts | | `architect` | `run:<id>` | Routes work, owns the loop | | `reviewer` | `run:<id>` | Code review pass | | `debugger` | `run:<id>` | Debugs failing validations | | `operator` | `run:<id>` | UI-mode reads/writes | | `documenter` | `run:<id>` | Doc generation | | `curator` | `run:<id>` | Curates artifacts | The framework doesn’t care if you invent a new role — `tool.roles[]` is a string list, not a typed enum at runtime. But sticking to the established set keeps quotas comparable across runs. ## Window keys [Section titled “Window keys”](#window-keys) `window_key` (and the quota ceiling) in `tool_invocations` is computed by the host-injected `DispatchProjectedDeps.computeQuotaWindow(ctx, roleQuota)` (plan P-011). The engine default (`defaultComputeQuotaWindow` in `libs/generic/tooldef/src/dispatch-types.ts`) is run-scoped / `perRun`; Papercusp’s policy (`papercuspComputeQuotaWindow` in `packages/agent-mcp/src/quota-policy.ts`, wired via `PROJECTED_DEPS`) is: * `worker` → `chunk:<chunkId>` (cap `perChunk`) if `ctx.chunkId` set, else null (no window, no quota) * power-user session → `power-user:<uiClientId>` (cap `perRun`) — keyed on the stable auth session, not the per-request run * anyone else → `run:<runId>` (cap `perRun`) if `ctx.runId` set, else null Null window means no quota check (and no telemetry insert path that requires the key). In practice every real call has both `?run=` and either a worker chunk or a run-scoped role, so windows are always set. ## File map [Section titled “File map”](#file-map) > The engine was extracted into **`@papercusp/tooldef`** (plan `papercusp-tooldef-extraction-2026-05-29`); the HTTP adapter into **`@papercusp/tooldef-http`**; IPC is **`@papercusp/ipc-endpoint-server`**. `@papercusp/agent-mcp` is the Papercusp host adapter (supplies the injected deps + re-exports the engine surface).
