Acceptance criteria”](#8-acceptance-criteria) * All 4 verbs implemented and individually green via authenticated curl * All 4 verbs idempotent on `actionId` replay (cache-is-authoritative documented) * All requests rejected with 401 if no/invalid bearer token * All requests rejected with 403 if body claims a harness identity not bound to the bearer token * `parent_slug` and `from_slug` always derived from the bearer token, never from body * `papercusp install papercup-org@0.1.1` materializes 7 working harness dirs each with a `harness_token` * Builtin `afterDone` hook fires for any harness with `parent_slug` set, including non-papercup-org harnesses * At least one non-papercup-org template has `spawnable: true` and is reachable via `GET /api/marketplace/spawnable` * `papercup-org` template re-bundled with NO per-dept afterDone scripts * Every prompt includes the “About Papercusp” preamble + neighbor view (with `spawned_count` + aggregate) + Tier 3 capabilities * Tier 3 capability is verified to actually work end-to-end (agent can inspect) * Coding-harness prompt-build includes own bounded inbox; auto-ack only on DONE/NEXT\_\* decisions * `send_message` requires `reason` ≥10 chars; placeholder regex matches log a quality flag * `scaffold_harness` enforces slug uniqueness with 409 * `scaffold_harness` 5-minute timeout enforced * `spinup_project` recursion is transactional (all-or-nothing across schemas) * Migration script handles broken registry rows: skip + log * Smoke A passes twice from clean state * Smoke B passes twice from clean state — no code in either path references “papercup-org” by name * Smoke C passes twice — neighbor view + cross-harness messaging + auto-ack scoping verified * Smoke D passes twice — auth model holds against forgery attempts * No regressions in `sheets` standalone coding-harness flow * Estimates updated to actuals; deltas analyzed ## 9. Documentation deliverables”](#9-documentation-deliverables) Part of the work, not afterthoughts. \~1d total, folded into the relevant steps: * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/harness-spawning.mdx` — what `scaffold_harness` does, how `parent_slug` works, completion reporting * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/spawnable-templates.mdx` — what makes a template spawnable, the `spawnable` manifest field, recognized `kind` values, how to publish * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/spawning-harnesses.mdx` — how to author a harness whose director can spawn children * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/cross-harness-coordination.mdx` — how `send_message` works, tiered visibility model, inspect-on-demand capabilities, conventions for `reason` strings * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/auth-and-identity.mdx` *(new)* — per-harness token model, identity binding, what’s derived vs body-controlled, threat model + non-goals (rotation), recovery procedure if compromised * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/scaffold-failure-recovery.mdx` *(new)* — runbook for partial scaffold failures (timeout, init failed, register failed), how to clean up + retry * `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/spec/marketplace-versioning.mdx` *(new)* — append-only-at-same-major.minor rule, when to bump patch * Update `apps/operator/content/internal-docs/implementation/status.mdx` with rows for “Harness spawning (standard substrate feature)” and “Cross-harness coordination (auth-bound + tiered visibility + send\_message bus).“ ## 10. # Run.sh → TS orchestrator port (handoff)

> TypeScript port of the bash autonomous-harness orchestrator. State as of 2026-04-27.

The ported run-loop is now RETIRED (2026-06-06) This is a **historical handoff doc**. The TS run-loop this port produced (`main-loop.ts`, `bin/run.ts`, `pre-loop.ts`, the checkpoints/snapshots/dispatches cluster) was retired and archived to `libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/` (plan `archive-legacy-orchestrator-deadcode-2026-06-06`; git tag `legacy-orchestrator-run-loop-retired-2026-06-06`) — superseded by the **DBOS durable pipeline** (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`). Parts of the port were deliberately kept LIVE rather than moved: `invoke.ts`, `lanes.ts`, the worker chunk-loop (`worker-chunk-loop.ts` / `chunk-loop-driver.ts`), `cost-cap.ts`, and `decision-parse.ts` all remain in the `@papercusp/orchestrator` package (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/`) and are **consumed** by the DBOS pipeline via `@papercusp/orchestrator` imports (e.g. `parseDecision`, `parseDecisionFor`, `DECISION_VERBS` in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`). They do **not** live inside the `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/` directory. The `papercusp-orchestrate` bin and the `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR` fall-through described below no longer exist. Note also that `bash run.sh` itself was deleted entirely (2026-05-30): the TS path became the canonical, only main-loop driver well before this retirement, and `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=0` is now a warning-only no-op, **not** a working bash fallback. The body below — describing `run.sh` as the live fall-through target and the flag as opt-in — is historical and no longer accurate. ## Why this exists [Section titled “Why this exists”](#why-this-exists) The autonomous-harness orchestrator was historically a 2,122-line bash script (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/run.sh`). The desktop app needs to drop the bash prereq for Windows users (Git for Windows is currently required to run the loop). A TypeScript port of `run.sh` achieves that without losing Claude Max subscription support — the port keeps the agent CLI (`omp -p` by default, `claude -p` opt-in) as a child-process spawn rather than switching to the SDK. Hard constraint for handoff Do **not** swap the agent CLI (`omp -p` or `claude -p`) for `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. Both CLIs handle Claude Max auth via the user’s Claude Code session (omp via Meridian’s SDK-bridge, claude directly); the SDK route requires API keys and breaks Max users. The whole point of the port is to drop bash, not the CLI layer. ## Where it lives [Section titled “Where it lives”](#where-it-lives) New package `@papercusp/orchestrator` at `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/` (in the `papercupai/papercusp` submodule). Feature-flagged via `PAPERCUSP_USE_TS_ORCHESTRATOR=1` — currently opt-in. The CLI entry `bin/run.ts` handles the flag and falls through to bash for any decision branch the TS port doesn’t yet cover. ## Stage table [Section titled “Stage table”](#stage-table) | Stage | Status | Tests | Notes | | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 0. # Pi (oh-my-pi) integration

> Two-track integration — pi as worker-role CLI (Option

[`oh-my-pi`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) (binary `omp`) is a 3.5k★ open-source AI coding agent for the terminal — strong tool harness (read / bash / edit / write / grep / find / lsp / python / browser / subagents / hooks / plugins), `--mode=rpc/json` structured output, multi-model fuzzy matching, session resume, and a TUI. It complements Papercusp at a different layer: **pi has strong in-loop autonomy; Papercusp has strong mission orchestration**. Together: pi as the worker, Papercusp as the conductor. This page covers two integration tracks. ## Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI [Section titled “Track A — Pi as the worker-role CLI”](#track-a--pi-as-the-worker-role-cli) The smallest valuable integration. Papercusp’s per-role config already supports overrides; add `cliBin` to the schema so individual roles can specify a non-default CLI. 
```json
// config.json (in any harness)
{
  "primaryRole": "orchestrator",
  "roles": {
    "worker": { "cliBin": "pi", "model": "opus" },
    "validator": { "cliBin": "claude" },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```
 **What lands:** pi runs the worker pipeline (where tool breadth matters); claude stays on plan / validate / orchestrate (where structured-decision reliability matters). Each invocation is `pi -p --no-session --append-system-prompt=<file>` so the fresh-context contract holds. **Effort:** \~½ day. The bash run.sh’s `invoke()` and the TS orchestrator’s `invoke.ts` both already shell out to a configurable CLI binary; this is wiring per-role config through to that spawn. **Output parsing.** Pi’s `--mode=json` emits a JSONL event stream with the same shape papercusp already parses for claude (session header, then events). Empirically verified: first event is `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"…","cwd":"…"}` followed by tool/message events. The adapter to map pi’s event names to papercusp’s audit schema is \~30 lines, not a deal-breaker. **Auth.** Pi inherits the sidecar’s environment, including `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Users logged into Claude Code see no auth prompt when papercusp invokes pi — the same Claude Max subscription that drives `claude -p` drives `pi -p`. Other providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, …) flow the same way via their respective env vars. ### Cost-mixing example [Section titled “Cost-mixing example”](#cost-mixing-example) The interesting payoff is fine-grained cost control across roles. Pi’s four model slots ([see §16.4 in the spec](/spec/cli-pluggability/#two-layer-pluggability-a-worked-example)) let a single config dial each role independently: 
```json
// config.json — opinionated mid-budget setup
{
  "roles": {
    "scoper":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "planner":      { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--plan=opus"] },
    "worker":       { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=sonnet", "--smol=haiku"] },
    "validator":    { "cliBin": "pi", "extraArgs": ["--model=gemini-2-flash"] },
    "orchestrator": { "cliBin": "claude" }
  }
}
```
 Reasoning: opus on the rare planning calls, sonnet on hot-path worker calls (with haiku for tool-plan subtasks via pi’s `--smol`), gemini flash on cheap validator passes, claude on the orchestrator for stable decision-verb output. Pairs naturally with papercusp’s [hard-stop budget enforcement](/spec/state/#53-hard-stop-budget-enforcement) — the substrate enforces the hard cap; this config tunes the per-call cost. See [§16 CLI pluggability](/internal/docs/spec/cli-pluggability) for the substrate concept this builds on. ## Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane [Section titled “Track B — Embedded pi TUI as a peer pane”](#track-b--embedded-pi-tui-as-a-peer-pane) A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard that hosts an interactive `omp` process inside the desktop app. The autonomous loop continues in the background; the human can drop into pi mid-mission for surgical override. ### Goal [Section titled “Goal”](#goal) Surface an interactive pi TUI inside the Papercusp Desktop harness UI alongside the existing `vscode` / `git` / `brainstorm` panels. (Phase 3b adds a “open in pi” button per feature that scopes pi to that feature’s worktree.) ### Design decisions [Section titled “Design decisions”](#design-decisions) 1. **PTY runs in the Node sidecar for the web/cloud path; the desktop build uses a Tauri-native pty.** The original decision was sidecar-only `node-pty` (the same sidecar code runs in desktop and cloud modes, and a Rust-side PTY would fork the codebase). That still holds for the web/cloud case. **For the native desktop build this was revised** (plan `desktop-ipc-transport-completion-2026-05-20`): inside the Tauri webview, `PiPanel` detects `isTauriNative()` and skips HTTP/WS/SSE entirely — it forks the pty in the Tauri Rust process via `openNativeSession()` and streams over Tauri IPC end-to-end, consulting `POST /pty/resolve` only to build harness-aware args/cwd/env without spawning. The Node-sidecar `node-pty` path (HTTP control plane + WS/SSE data channel) remains the transport for the web/cloud case. 2. **I/O transport: WebSocket preferred, SSE + POST fallback.** A full-duplex WebSocket transport shipped: `PiPanel.tsx` connects via `ptyWsUrlForId()` and attaches xterm’s `AttachAddon` (binary frames, no base64), backed by the `packages/operator-core/lib/pty-ws.ts` WS server. It falls back to SSE output + POST input only when the WS server is unreachable (proxy doesn’t pass upgrades, `PAPERCUSP_PTY_WS=0`, etc.). The HTTP control plane (`POST /spawn`, `/kill`, …) is identical either way — only the data channel differs. SSE was the original v1 transport (Next.js’s standalone server didn’t natively support raw WS-upgrade on arbitrary routes); WS is now primary and SSE is the compatibility path. 3. **`pi` is a user-installed prerequisite, not bundled.** Matches the existing `claude` pattern. The desktop preflight UI already surfaces missing-prereq state — extend with a `pi` check. 4. **No session persistence in v1.** Pi has `--no-session` for ephemeral runs; persistent resume across pane reopen is v2 polish. 5. **Slot into the existing `MainPanel` union.** `HarnessDashboard.tsx` lists every embedded-tool tab (`brainstorm`, `proposals`, `git`, `dashboard`, `vscode`, `insights`, etc.) — adding `'pi'` follows the established pattern. The `vscode` tab (which embeds `code-server` in an iframe) is the direct precedent: same shape, different embedded tool. ### Rejected alternatives [Section titled “Rejected alternatives”](#rejected-alternatives) * **Rust-side PTY (`portable-pty` crate)** — originally rejected (forks desktop/cloud paths, more native build pain on Windows, couples a UI feature to the platform shell). This was **effectively revised for the native desktop transport**: the desktop build now does fork the pty Rust-side (see design decision #1). The web/cloud path keeps the sidecar `node-pty`, so the “forks the codebase” concern is contained to the desktop transport seam rather than the whole stack. * **SSH/wetty-style HTTP terminal services** — another process, another auth surface, another port. The `node-pty + xterm.js + SSE` stack runs entirely inside the existing sidecar. ### Pi command surface used by Track B [Section titled “Pi command surface used by Track B”](#pi-command-surface-used-by-track-b) The pane spawns one of: * `omp` — pi’s interactive default mode. Best for general use. * `omp shell` — pi’s “interactive shell console” subcommand. Slightly different surface; useful for shell-flavored workflows. Useful flags to pass: * `--no-pty` — disable pi’s *internal* PTY-based bash execution. We already have a PTY (the one we bridge to xterm.js); pi nesting another inside it can confuse signal handling and resize semantics. Set this in the embedded pane. * `--session-dir=$STATE_DIR/.pi-sessions/` (or env `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) — point pi’s session store at the harness state dir so sessions are scoped to the harness, not the user’s home. Falls back to `~/.omp/agent` if unset. * `--append-system-prompt=<file>` — for Phase 3b feature-scoped opens, inject the feature’s spec/lineage as additional system prompt. * `--export=<session-file>` — Phase 3d candidate. After a session ends, exporting it to HTML and storing under the harness audit dir makes the in-pane work part of the durable record. ### Phasing [Section titled “Phasing”](#phasing) **Phase 3a — MVP terminal pane (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped. A new `pi` tab in the harness dashboard. Click → opens xterm.js connected to a fresh `pi` process in the harness’s project directory. Keystrokes in, output out. Close tab → kill pi. **Phase 3b — peer pane layout + feature-scoped launch (\~1 day).** ✅ shipped (tab-scoped, not split-pane). Each feature’s `FeaturePeekPanel` gets an “open in pi” button → pi spawns in `<stateDir>/worktrees/<fid>` (falls back to project root if no worktree). The pty is deliberately **not** killed when the client disconnects: the SSE stream’s `onClose` keeps the handle alive (PiPanel unmounts on every dashboard tab switch), and PiPanel’s own unmount cleanup explicitly skips the kill so a remount can resume the same session via `resumePtyId`. Genuinely-abandoned handles are reaped by the 5-minute idle reaper in `pty-bridge`, not by a disconnect kill. The plan called for a split-pane layout; we shipped tab-pattern instead (matches the existing `vscode` tab; no layout-shift, full pane width). True split-pane is a future affordance if needed. **Phase 3c — desktop polish (\~½ day).** ✅ shipped. `pi` added to preflight checks (PATH + well-known-paths probe). Install-hint UI surfaces missing-pi with `brew install can1357/oh-my-pi/oh-my-pi`. README documents pi as an optional prereq. Pi missing does NOT block the app from booting — only the pi tab degrades. **Phase 3d — partially shipped.** * **Feature-scoped system-prompt injection** ✅ shipped. When the user clicks “open in pi” on a feature, the spawn endpoint reads `harness_features` for that `(slug, featureId)` (columns `feature_id`, `title`, `summary`, `status`), formats them as markdown via the shared kickoff factory, writes the brief to a fresh `mkdtemp` dir under `/dev/shm` (tmpdir fallback) named `<feature-id>.md`, and adds `--append-system-prompt=<path>` to the omp args. The temp dir is scheduled for removal after 30s. Pi launches already aware of the feature it’s working on. Falls back silently when the feature lookup fails — no error surface, just no injection. * **Per-harness session persistence** ✅ shipped via `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<stateDir>/pi-sessions/`. Each harness has its own pi history under its state dir; sessions persist across pane reopens automatically. Future polish: explicit “resume last session” button using `omp -c` / `omp -r <id>`. * **Audit export** ✅ shipped. `attachAuditExport()` registers an `onExit` hook that runs `exportPiSessions()`, which finds the session jsonls created during the pty’s lifetime and shells out to `omp --export <sessionFile>` per session, storing the resulting HTML under `<stateDir>/audit/pi-sessions/`. Two GET endpoints serve the exports — `GET /pi-sessions/audit` (lists them) and `GET /pi-sessions/audit/:filename` (serves one HTML, basename-validated against path traversal) — and PiPanel’s “past sessions” chip + popover lists and links them. * **Pi extension** ✅ shipped and wired into spawns. The spawn endpoint resolves `global-plugins/pi/extension.ts` and, when it exists, pushes `-e <path>` onto the omp args (the `-e <path>` extension flag — not `--plugin-dir`). The extension registers `papercusp_status`, `papercusp_list_features`, `papercusp_lineage`, `papercusp_audit`, `papercusp_proposals`, `papercusp_decisions`, and `papercusp_issues` (underscore-namespaced). `GET /pty/tools` enumerates them (returning `extensionAvailable: false` with an empty list when the extension isn’t present). The extension reads papercusp state through the existing API (so no extra trust boundary). * **Subagent cross-pollination** — deferred. `omp agents unpack` ships curated subagent personas. Wrap each as a papercusp plugin so they appear in the marketplace catalog. Cross-pollinate the ecosystems. * **Multi-pane** — shipped via the dockview `PiTerminalsDock.tsx` (see the file tables below). Multiple concurrent pi panes scoped to different features, capped per the process-wide, host-scaled pty cap in §Risks. ### File-level changes (Phase 3a + 3b + 3c) [Section titled “File-level changes (Phase 3a + 3b + 3c)”](#file-level-changes-phase-3a--3b--3c) #### New files [Section titled “New files”](#new-files) | Path | Purpose | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/pty/index.ts` | Router mounted at `/api/harness/:slug/pty/*` (+ `/pi-sessions/audit/*`). ```plaintext
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/spawn
  body: { command?, args?, laneId?, cols?, rows?,
          env?, resumePtyId? }
  → { id, command, args, cwd, pid }   // (+ prewarmed:true if adopted
                                       //  from the pool, resumed:true
                                       //  if resumePtyId matched a live pty)
  cwd is derived from laneId (the lane's worktree if it exists, else the
  project root) — there is no ctxPrompt or cwd field in the body.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/resolve
  Same body shape; returns { command, args, cwd, env } WITHOUT spawning.
  Used by the Tauri-native path to build harness-aware args.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/prewarm
  Reserves a warm omp (same body shape) so /spawn can adopt it and hide
  omp's ~1.2s startup. → { reserved: true } (or reused:true).


GET /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/stream    (text/event-stream — SSE fallback)
  ← event: data\ndata: <base64-bytes>\n\n
  ← event: exit\ndata: {"code": 0}\n\n
  On connect, replays the full byte history into the new subscriber.


POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/input    { data: <base64-bytes> }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/resize   { cols, rows }
POST /api/harness/:slug/pty/:id/kill


GET /api/harness/:slug/pty/tools          enumerates the pi extension's tools
GET /api/harness/:slug/pi-sessions/audit  lists exported session HTML
GET /api/harness/:slug/pi-sessions/audit/:filename  serves one export
```
 On the WS path the data channel is binary frames of raw pty bytes (no base64). On the SSE fallback, bytes are base64-encoded over JSON to keep the stream uniform regardless of encoding (xterm.js handles arbitrary byte streams; pi may emit non-UTF-8 in edge cases like binary file contents). Idle PTYs (no input, no consumer marking activity) auto-kill after 5 minutes. **Auth split.** Only the read/stream routes are `auth: 'public'` (`/:id/stream`, the two `/pi-sessions/audit` routes, and `/pty/tools`). The mutating routes — `spawn`, `resolve`, `prewarm`, `input`, `resize`, `kill` — are `auth: 'loopback'`. **Reconnect / replay.** The server keeps two replay sources per handle: an `xterm-headless` mirror fed every byte (bounded screen-state serialization, \~tens of KB, VS Code’s approach — used for WS reconnect), and a 1 MB raw-byte ring (full-history replay, used by the SSE path). A dashboard tab switch therefore resumes the same pty with prior output intact rather than starting fresh. **Cross-agent wake routing.** Each managed pty is tagged with its owner SID (`PAPERCUSP_SID` from the spawn env) so the await-event wake executor can route a wake turn into the correct session. `findPtyByPid` carries a recycled-pid guard (EI-151): a recorded pid recycled by the OS to a *different* owner’s live pty is not treated as a match. ### Critical files to read first [Section titled “Critical files to read first”](#critical-files-to-read-first) | File | Why | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `apps/operator/app/harness/PiTerminalsDock.tsx` + `PiPanel.tsx` | The current pi-pane surface — dockview multi-pane container + the xterm/SSE panel. (Supersedes the original `HarnessDashboard.tsx` `MainPanel`-union integration.) | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts` | Hono route-table assembly. The pty router registers the same way the harness/plugins routers do. | | `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` | Sidecar spawn — confirms env passes through (`PATH`, etc.) which pi needs. | | `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/desktop/preflight.ts` | Pattern for prereq checks. The `pi` check mirrors the `claude` check (plus well-known-path probing). | | `papercusp-desktop/web/index.html` | `renderHint()` switch — the pi case. | ### Verification [Section titled “Verification”](#verification) **Phase 3a:** 1. Launch the desktop shell: `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` (the only supported run path; it boots the operator sidecar + webview). 2. In the Tauri window, open a harness (`/harness/<some-slug>`). 3. Click the new pi tab. 4. Pi prompt appears; type `pwd` + Enter; output shows the harness’s project directory. 5. Type `exit`; pane shows “(pi exited 0)” and the spawn lifecycle cleans up (verify `pgrep -af omp` returns nothing). 6. Resize the window; xterm-fit addon resizes; pi sees the new width (`tput cols`). **Phase 3b:** 7. Two-pane layout works: dashboard left, pi right; resizable divider; both visible. 8. On a feature row, “Open in pi” puts pi inside that feature’s worktree directory (verify with `pwd`). 9. Pi’s first prompt includes the feature spec + lineage (visible when asked “what are you working on?”). **Phase 3c:** 10. `pi` shows as `missing` in the bootstrap UI when uninstalled; install hint card appears with a brew/install command. 11. Once installed, `pi` flips to `ok` on next preflight tick; pi tab works. 12. README quick-start mentions pi as optional. **Cross-cutting:** * No native-binary load errors at sidecar boot on macOS, Linux, Windows. * The desktop bundle still ships within size budget (no inadvertent +100MB from xterm assets). * No stray pty processes survive sidecar shutdown. ### Risks [Section titled “Risks”](#risks) | Risk | Mitigation | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `node-pty` native binding fails under Next.js `output: 'standalone'` (Next traces deps and may miss the `.node` file). | Verify on day 1. If `next.config.js` `outputFileTracingIncludes` doesn’t capture `node_modules/node-pty/build/Release/*.node`, add an explicit include. Fallback: ship pty-bridge as a separate child process the Next handler shells out to. | | `node-pty` Windows ConPTY initialization fails on older Win10. | Document min Windows version (10 1809+) in README. Surface a clear inline error in the pane. | | Pi binary not on `PATH` despite being installed (Mac homebrew + Tauri-Cocoa launches without a login shell). | Probe `/usr/local/bin/omp`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/omp`, `~/.cargo/bin/omp` in addition to `which`. Fall back to user-configurable `pi.binPath` in `config.json`. | | Concurrent pi panes spawn many processes / use lots of memory. | A **process-wide, host-scaled** cap, not a fixed per-harness number: `livePtyCap()` = `min(host-scaled backstop, fleet maxSimultaneousAgents)`, where the backstop = `min(2× the resource-profile agent budget, ceiling 16)`. Spawning past the cap throws `pty cap reached (n/cap)`; the pane surfaces it inline. On a small box this floors low (a 4-core laptop’s backstop is \~2–4); on a typical box it sits well above 4. | | Pi’s nested PTY (its `bash` tool) conflicts with the outer xterm.js PTY — terminal corruption or signal loss. | Spawn with `--no-pty`. Pi degrades gracefully (loses interactive bash but keeps every other tool). | | Auth state drifts: user logged into Claude Code in their normal shell, but the desktop app launches without that env. | Surface `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` presence in the preflight UI; document the GUI-app-no-login-shell gotcha in the README. | ## What is explicitly NOT in scope [Section titled “What is explicitly NOT in scope”](#what-is-explicitly-not-in-scope) * Replacing the `vscode` tab — pi sits alongside it, not instead of it. * Web (non-desktop) deployment of the pi pane — works the same way (sidecar is identical), but rollout is separate. (The original “not in scope” list also named the pi plugin and session-persistence/resume; both shipped under Phase 3d — see the phasing notes above.)

# Plugin + marketplace pipeline — state as of 2026-05-11

> One-page reference for the TS plugin/template/snapshot/marketplace system as it stands today. Where the code is, what's covered by tests, what's deferred, and where to look first.

Dated snapshot — paths and the marketplace surface have moved Preserved as the 2026-05-11 milestone. Reading it today, note: * The operator is now **`apps/operator/`** and its `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**; `apps/operator/lib/*` (e.g. `plugin-host-runtime.ts`, `plugin-grants.ts`) now lives under **`packages/operator-core/lib/`**. The Next route paths in the tables below are stale. * Migrations **`051`** and **`052`** were folded into **`000-baseline.sql`** and archived (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/archive/`); they are no longer live numbered migrations. `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants` is defined in the baseline. * The `localhost:3057` / `papercuspai.com` marketplace-api was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`, CF Workers + Hono + D1). * The “use git worktrees for non-main work” hard rule is **reversed** under the current model: the shared tree stays on `staging` and you do **not** branch/worktree — concurrency is serialized by the `locks:*` + `coord:*` systems. See the repo `CLAUDE.md` “Branch discipline” section. ## TL;DR [Section titled “TL;DR”](#tldr) Three publishable kinds (`plugin`, `template`, `snapshot`) share one marketplace pipeline. Operator at `localhost:3055` serves the install/discover surface; marketplace-api at `localhost:3057` is the registry. Plugins run in-process under a two-tier capability check (manifest ∩ user-granted). Tests cover every helper and DB-backed function shipped in this session. *As of today:* the `snapshot` publishable kind was **retired** (see the snapshot note below); the `:3057`/`papercuspai.com` registry was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard**; plugins also load as **WASM** or **daemon** runtimes, not only in-process JS. ## Source layout [Section titled “Source layout”](#source-layout) | What | Where | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Plugin SDK (types, capability strings, manifest schema) | `packages/plugin-sdk/` | | Plugin loader (manifest validate, capability check, reaction rules, action registry, audit) | `packages/plugin-loader/` | | Plugin host runtime in operator | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` | | Per-(plugin, harness) grants | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-grants.ts` + `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants` in `000-baseline.sql` | | Audit log (PG writer) | `apps/operator/lib/plugin-audit-writer.ts` | | Marketplace API routes | `apps/operator/app/api/{marketplace,plugins,templates,snapshots,harness/[slug]/save-as-template}/` | | Marketplace UI components | `libs/marketplace-public-ui/src/` (shared with public site) | | Operator-side marketplace pages | `apps/operator/app/marketplace/{,templates,plugins,snapshots}/` | | Operator-side installed pages | `apps/operator/app/installed/{harnesses,plugins,snapshots,templates}/` | | Marketplace registry server | `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/` (separate repo `papercupai/papercusp-registry`) | | CLI (`papercusp install`, `plugin enable/disable/lint/init/doctor`, `snapshot {fork,publish}`) | `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/` | | Snapshot capture / restore | `libs/papercusp-export-state/src/` — **RETIRED**, moved to `_retired/snapshot-system/papercusp-export-state` (see snapshot note below) | ## What runs end-to-end today [Section titled “What runs end-to-end today”](#what-runs-end-to-end-today) ### Plugin lifecycle [Section titled “Plugin lifecycle”](#plugin-lifecycle) 1. **Install** — *(superseded)* The original `POST /api/marketplace/install-plugin` path that shelled out to `papercusp install <slug>@<version>` (atomic staging-dir tarball download/extract/validate) is **dead**. Install now goes through **`POST /api/cupboard/install-plugin`** (revive-cupboard-distribution D-003/P2), which **git-clones** the Cupboard listing’s GitHub repo (resolved from `listingId`, or a direct `githubUrl`) and runs the capability-gate + install-consent path. The route header itself describes the old `:3057`/CLI tarball install as dead. 2. **Enable** — `POST /api/plugins/enable { slug, harnesses[], disable? }` adds to `enabled-plugins.json` for each harness and writes the boot-time silent grant backfill. `enabled-plugins.json` stays the on-disk source of truth (the CLI is its only writer), but it is now **mirrored into `harness_shared.plugin_enables`** (`plugin-enables-pg.ts`) so read paths use one cross-harness PG query instead of fanning over the filesystem; an FS watcher (`harness-fs-watcher.ts`) re-mirrors on direct CLI/file edits. 3. **Consent** — `/installed/plugins/<slug>/permissions` renders a harnesses × capabilities grid; toggling `POST /api/plugins/grants { plugin, version, harness, capabilities, action }` mutates `harness_shared.plugin_capability_grants`. Two-tier check: every `hasCapability(ctx, cap)` ANDs manifest with the granted set. 4. **Run** — The typed `PluginHooks` shape is now a **frozen back-compat surface** (plugin-system-pot-port D-003); the host fires it by direct iteration. Members: `onLoad`, `onUnload`, `onHarnessCreated`, `beforeMissionStart`, `afterDone`, `onFeaturePassed`, `onProposalAccepted`, `onPostOrchestrator`, `onPostWorker`, `onPostValidator`, `contributeOperatorSuggestions`, `getStateForReload`, `restoreFromReload`. The WordPress-style **HookBus** (`addAction`/`addFilter`, plus topic strings like `mission.start` / `task.passed` / `feature.completed` / `proposal.accepted`) was **retired and deleted** from loader/SDK/host (P-006/D-003) — those topics no longer exist as fire targets. The live extension surface is capability-scoped **event-reaction rules** (see the extension axes below). 5. **Action invocation** — `POST /api/plugins/[...path]` proxies through `ctx.actions.register(...)`’d handlers. Every invocation produces an audit row via `PgAuditWriter` (fail-closed — action fails if audit write fails). 6. **Update** — `GET /api/plugins/updates` diffs installed vs catalog; `/installed/plugins` shows “Update → vX.Y.Z” with new-cap re-consent prompt before bumping. 7. **Uninstall** — `POST /api/plugins/uninstall { slug }` removes the global plugin dir + disables from every harness it was enabled in. ### Plugin runtime model + extension axes [Section titled “Plugin runtime model + extension axes”](#plugin-runtime-model--extension-axes) *(Added post-snapshot — the runtime surface grew well beyond the action registry described above.)* Each plugin instance gets a per-(plugin, harness) `ctx` carrying: * `ctx.actions` — the action registry (`register(...)`’d handlers behind `/api/plugins/[...path]`). * `ctx.spawn` — capability-gated `compute:exec` with a frozen PATH (`makePluginSpawn`). * `ctx.kv` — plugin-private, quota’d K/V backed by `harness_shared.plugin_kv` (quota from `manifest.kvQuota`; left `undefined` in test/no-PG contexts, so plugins must tolerate absence). * `ctx.oauth.token(field)` — acquires a fresh access token, resolving the backing provider from the plugin’s manifest `oauth[]` entries. * `ctx.recordResource(...)` — writes a record to the provision WAL (for in-process plugins that create external resources from a hook handler rather than a setup script). The **primary** extension surface is no longer the typed lifecycle hooks — it is two manifest-declared axes the host wires at load: * **Tool axis** (main consumer): `manifest.tools[]` entries are projected as agent tools `<plugin>.<verb>` over both HTTP and MCP (`registerPluginTools`). * **Event-reaction axis**: `manifest.reactions[]` rules — when a trigger `on` settles, the rule fires one of the plugin’s **own** tools through normal capability-scoped dispatch. Each `on` trigger requires an `events:listen:<on>` capability (`registerPluginReactionRules`). Plugin-emitted events (the WASM event sink, `plugins:fire_event`) feed the same reaction registry as synthetic events. The **RoutineDefinition** and **RoleDefinition** manifest axes were **retired** in the pot port (`collectRoutines`/`collectRoles` deleted, zero callers). The manifest `roles` field stays schema-tolerated as inert data (so existing plugins that declare it still load); routines authors are pointed at blueprint triggers / event-reaction schedules. ### Template lifecycle [Section titled “Template lifecycle”](#template-lifecycle) 1. **Save** — “Save template” button on harness dashboard → `POST /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template { slug, version, description?, author? }` forks the recipe (SPEC.md, AGENTS.md, `.papercusp/config.json`, `.papercusp/validation-contract.md` + plugin recommendations from `enabled-plugins.json`) into `~/.papercusp/templates/<slug>/<version>/`. 2. **Publish** — `POST /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish` tars + signs + uploads to marketplace-api. 3. **Install** — `POST /api/marketplace/install { slug, projectName, targetPath? }` scaffolds a new project. **Slug-collision recovery (PR #5)**: returns `{ code: 'project_name_taken', suggestedName: '<base>-2' }` on conflict; UI auto-offers via `confirm()`. Partial-init cleanup wipes half-scaffolded dirs on `papercusp init` failure. ### Snapshot lifecycle [Section titled “Snapshot lifecycle”](#snapshot-lifecycle) Publishable-snapshot system RETIRED The publishable-snapshot / snapshot-**export** pipeline below was **retired** (retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09, shipped). `libs/papercusp-export-state` moved to `_retired/snapshot-system/papercusp-export-state`; `@papercusp/export-state`, the `snapshots:*` tools, all `/api/snapshots/*` publish routes, and the Cupboard `kind=snapshot` were retired (migration 199 drops `snapshot_index`). The fork route `instantiate.ts` — the **only** non-test caller of `copyGrantsToNewHarness` — now lives under `_retired/`. The reproducible replacement is the **InstanceSpec** system (`packages/operator-core/lib/instance-spec/`). The surviving `/api/harness/:slug/snapshots` route is a **different** feature — per-harness iteration snapshots (FS rollback of `.papercusp/snapshots/<ts>-iter-<n>/`), not publishable snapshots. *Historical (pre-retirement) flow:* 1. **Capture** — `POST /api/snapshots/create` writes a tarball under `<harness>/.papercusp/snapshots/`. 2. **Publish** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/publish` uploads to marketplace. 3. **Fork** — `POST /api/snapshots/<id>/instantiate` (or `papercusp snapshot fork`) creates a new harness with schema rename. **Grants carry over (PR #2)**: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` copies every `(plugin, version, capability)` grant on the source harness to the new fork via `INSERT … SELECT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. 4. **Republish** — *pending*. PR-B paused per `@plugin`’s reply on coord, awaiting v1 plan greenlight (Batch G+1 bumps `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2). ## Hard rules in this code (don’t break) [Section titled “Hard rules in this code (don’t break)”](#hard-rules-in-this-code-dont-break) * **No TS deletion** anywhere in `apps/operator/` or `libs/papercusp/`. Set by `shared.jsonl` 2026-05-10T05:50. * **Rust port is opt-in** via `?backend=rust`; default routes always go to TS. * **Paperclip stomps** `apps/operator/app/harness/*` periodically. `pgrep -af paperclip` before editing harness UI; race-and-recommit if it stomps you. * **Schema ownership**: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` is `@plugin`’s territory going forward (per their handoff on coord 2026-05-11T15:30). Transitional additions get a `kind: contract` post first. * **Use git worktrees** for any non-main feature work — never branch-switch the canonical `papercup/` checkout while other agents may be writing. ## Test coverage [Section titled “Test coverage”](#test-coverage) Plugin-loader tests (vitest, `packages/plugin-loader/`): * 91 cases covering manifest validation, capability matching (incl. two-tier), action registry, semver, audit, api-factory, tools. *(Snapshot-era count; the suite has since grown and the HookBus tests were removed with the HookBus — new specs include the daemon/WASM runtimes, reaction rules, and `plugin doctor`.)* Operator unit tests (vitest, `apps/operator/`): * 67 cases on pure helpers from PRs #2-#5: `isNewerVersion`, `computeCapChange`, `suggestNextFreeName`, `SLUG_RE`, `SEMVER_RE`, `explainCapability`, `tierBadgeColor`. Operator integration tests (vitest + testcontainers PG, `apps/operator/test/`): * 25 cases covering every public function in `lib/plugin-grants.ts`: `copyGrantsToNewHarness` (8), `grantCapabilities/revokeCapabilities/getGrantsForPluginInHarness` (11), `backfillGrantsFromEnabledPluginsAndLegacyFile` (6). Total: **183 tests** specifically on the plugin/marketplace surface. ## What’s deferred / out of scope [Section titled “What’s deferred / out of scope”](#whats-deferred--out-of-scope) Documented in `/docs/spec/plugin-runtime-roadmap` (Batch F deferrals — **all shipped**): * Typed `ctx.kv` with quotas — **shipped** (`plugin-kv.ts`, backed by `harness_shared.plugin_kv`, per-plugin quotas wired from `manifest.kvQuota`). * Hot-reload state preservation — **shipped** (`getStateForReload`/`restoreFromReload` SDK hooks, gated on `manifest.hotReload.preserveState`, backed by `harness_shared.plugin_reload_state`). * `papercusp plugin doctor` (declared-vs-used capability static analysis) — **shipped** (`plugin-doctor.ts`, wired into the CLI `case 'doctor'` → `cmdPluginDoctor`). ```plaintext
GET   /api/marketplace/catalog                  — proxies marketplace-api with hide-filter
POST  /api/marketplace/install                  — template install (slug-collision aware)
POST  /api/cupboard/install-plugin              — plugin install: git-clone the listing's GitHub repo (replaces the dead marketplace/install-plugin tarball path)
DELETE /api/marketplace/uninstall               — template uninstall
GET   /api/plugins/global                       — installed plugins
GET   /api/plugins/manifest?slug=<id>           — declared capabilities for consent UI
GET   /api/plugins/updates                      — installed-vs-catalog diff with capChange
GET   /api/plugins/grants?plugin=&version=&harness=
POST  /api/plugins/grants                       — toggle a (plugin, harness, cap) grant
POST  /api/plugins/enable                       — enable/disable a plugin in harness(es)
POST  /api/plugins/uninstall
# /api/snapshots/* (create, publish, instantiate, retract) — RETIRED; the
#   publishable-snapshot system moved to _retired/snapshot-system. Replacement:
#   the InstanceSpec system (packages/operator-core/lib/instance-spec/).
#   The surviving /api/harness/:slug/snapshots is a DIFFERENT feature
#   (per-harness iteration snapshots / FS rollback).
POST  /api/harness/<slug>/save-as-template
POST  /api/templates/<slug>/<version>/publish
```
 ## First places to look [Section titled “First places to look”](#first-places-to-look) * New plugin author: `/docs/spec/plugin-quickstart` — five-command flow from blank dir to published plugin. * Plugin runtime contract: `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts` — capability strings + lifecycle hook signatures. * Capability semantics: `packages/plugin-loader/src/capabilities.ts` — wildcard matching, two-tier AND. * Manifest schema: `packages/plugin-sdk/papercusp-plugin.schema.json` — `additionalProperties: false`. * Lifecycle wire-up: `apps/operator/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts` — fire-points + audit + grants integration. * Marketplace registry: `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — catalog, signing, retraction, SBOM.

It’s preserved as a dated milestone log; **the file paths and a few component names below are stale** after later refactors. The big renames to keep in mind when reading: * `apps/papercup/**` and `apps/papercusp/**` → the operator now lives at **`apps/operator/`**; its Next.js `app/api/**` routes were ported to **Hono routers under `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/**`**. * The operator-side process-level lifecycle host moved to **`packages/operator-core/lib/plugin-host-runtime.ts`**. The React-render layer named below (`lib/plugin-runtime.ts`, `lib/PluginTabs.tsx`, `lib/PluginReactTab.tsx`) did **not** move — it still lives under **`apps/operator/lib/`**. * The `run.sh` → TS orchestrator port shipped and its ported run-loop was later **retired** (see [orchestrator-port](/internal/docs/implementation/orchestrator-port)); the live pipeline is the DBOS runner in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`. * The `papercuspai.com` marketplace described in the “After all of the above” table was superseded by the in-app **Cupboard** (`apps/operator-public`). The reference runtime lives in this monorepo (`Papercusp/papercup`). # Performance — rules every agent must follow

> Render, bundle, network, layout, and measurement guidelines distilled from the apps that feel fastest, plus concrete anti-patterns from real audits of this codebase. Apply to all new code.

> **Webapp retired (2026-05-14).** Any `localhost:3055` or `localhost:3070` URL on this page is only reachable while the **Tauri dev shell** is running. Start it with `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`. Stack note — Next.js has been removed This page was written when the operator app was a **Next.js App Router** project, and several rules below were framed around RSC / Server Components / Next-specific tooling. **That framework is gone.** The operator is now a **Vite SPA on TanStack Router** (`apps/operator-vite`, dev server on `:3055`) fronting a **Hono host** (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`, `:3070`). There is no `next` dependency, no RSC, no Server Components, and `'use client'` is an inert vestige. The `next/*` import surface (`next/image`, `next/dynamic`, `next/link`, `next/navigation`) is satisfied by TanStack-Router-backed shims under `apps/operator/lib/router-compat/{dynamic,link,navigation}.tsx`. RSC-only advice (“ship zero JS”, “push `'use client'` to the leaf”) does **not** apply to a SPA — read those rules as historical context. The *measured* perf wins (parallelize fs/PG, request-scoped read caches, virtualize/memoize lists, animate only transform/opacity) still hold; only the **named cause** “Next.js dev mode” and any Next-specific tool are stale. See `apps/operator/docs/plans/finish-next-removal-2026-06-01.md` and `apps/operator/docs/plans/operator-vite-migration-2026-05-20.md`. Read this BEFORE making any changes **Every agent must read this page before changing code in this repo.** “It works” isn’t the same as “it’s fast.” This page captures (a) practices from apps users consider best-in-class — Linear, Notion, Vercel, Figma, Discord, Stripe — and (b) **real anti-patterns we’ve shipped** that have caused production slowdowns. The “What not to do” section near the bottom is **load-bearing**: it lists specific traps with measured impact and the correct alternative. If a pattern in your change matches one of those traps, change the approach before continuing. ## What “fast” actually means here [Section titled “What “fast” actually means here”](#what-fast-actually-means-here) The targets are stricter than the typical web app baseline: | Metric | Target | Why | | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | Time to interactive (TTI) on the harness page | < 1.5 s on a warm cache | Operators sit on this page all day | | Frame rate during list updates / animation | 60fps minimum, 120fps when transform-only | Anything below 60 feels sluggish | | Re-renders per keystroke in a 50-row form | ≤ 1 per field | Anything more is a re-render storm | | Bundle delta per new feature | < 10 KB gzip / route | Death-by-a-thousand-cuts kills warm-cache TTI | | Web Vitals (LCP / INP / CLS) | “Good” (2.5s / 200ms / 0.1) | Google’s standard; passes user perception threshold | You can verify the first three locally with React DevTools’ Profiler. The last two need Lighthouse or Web Vitals in production. ## Lessons from the apps that feel fastest [Section titled “Lessons from the apps that feel fastest”](#lessons-from-the-apps-that-feel-fastest) | App | What they do | What you can copy | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Linear** | Local-first sync — every action mutates the local store first, then syncs to the server in the background. Zero “loading…” spinners on normal operations. Fine-grained subscriptions: components only re-render when *their slice* of state changes. | Use `useSyncQuery` (`libs/generic/sync`) the way it’s already wired — it’s **transport-agnostic**, so local-first/optimistic behavior is what you get on the Zero/WebSocket transport, with REST fallback on polling/SSE. Optimistic UI for every mutation that runs on WS. Don’t subscribe to whole tables when one row is enough. | | **Notion** | Block-level memoization in the editor — every block is a `React.memo` with a stable identity, and they avoid re-rendering ancestors when a block changes. Service worker for offline. View Transitions API for sidebar nav. | Memoize list items by stable key. Use `React.memo` + `areEqual` on FeatureList row, IssuesList row, ProposalsPanel item. | | **Vercel** | Server Components by default; `'use client'` only at leaves. Streaming SSR with Suspense boundaries around slow data. Edge-runtime for routes that don’t need Node. | *(RSC/SSR pattern — not applicable: the operator is a Vite SPA with no Server Components.)* What still transfers: keep route chunks lean and code-split heavy pieces, and wrap slow client data-fetching in `<Suspense>` with `React.lazy`. | | **Figma** | UI is React (chrome only). The canvas is custom Rust→WebAssembly. They explicitly *don’t* try to make React fast enough for the design surface — they use the right tool for the right surface. | When you have a hot rendering loop (canvas, graph), don’t reach for React. Drop down to imperative DOM / canvas / WebGL. | | **Discord** | Virtualized chat list. Workers for syntax highlighting and search indexing. Replaced setState chains with Flux to avoid double-renders. | Virtualize any list > 50 rows (`@tanstack/react-virtual` already in deps). Move CPU-heavy work off the main thread (Web Workers). | | **Stripe** | Inline critical CSS. Defer all non-critical JS. `preconnect` to API hosts. Prerender hot paths. | Eager-load (don’t lazy/defer) above-the-fold images and set explicit dimensions. `<link rel="preconnect">` for cross-origin APIs (Anthropic, Cloudflare, etc.) in `apps/operator-vite/index.html`. | | **Airtable** | Virtualized grid. WebWorker for formula compute. Optimistic UI everywhere. | Same patterns. We already use `RichGrid` virtualization — keep it. | | **GitHub** | Turbo (HTML over the wire) for many surfaces, replacing SPA. View Transitions for navigation. Aggressive HTTP caching. | *(The operator is deliberately a SPA — the “prefer SSR + native nav” half doesn’t apply here.)* What transfers: aggressive HTTP caching on the Hono API, and the View Transitions / WAAPI approach for cross-route animation (see `RouteTransitionProvider`’s jump-gate warp). | ## Hard rules — must follow [Section titled “Hard rules — must follow”](#hard-rules--must-follow) These are non-negotiable. CI / review will reject violations. ### 1. (Historical — RSC no longer applies) Keep the JS you ship small [Section titled “1. (Historical — RSC no longer applies) Keep the JS you ship small”](#1-historical--rsc-no-longer-applies-keep-the-js-you-ship-small) > **Stale on this stack.** This rule assumed Next.js App Router Server Components. The operator is now a Vite SPA on TanStack Router — **everything ships to the browser; there are no Server Components and `'use client'` is a no-op.** The rule below is kept for context and for the parts that still generalize. The SPA-era takeaway: there is no free server-only tier, so be deliberate about what each route’s chunk pulls in. Code-split heavy, not-immediately-needed pieces (see rule 14 with the `dynamic` shim), keep route bundles under the per-feature delta target, and don’t hoist a one-route dependency into the shared chunk. Original (Next-era) guidance, for reference only: 
```tsx
// (Next.js App Router — no longer the stack)
// Wrong — every server-rendered child of /reports also ships to the browser
'use client';
export default function ReportsPage() { ... }


// Right — only the chart is client-rendered; the surrounding page stays server-only
export default function ReportsPage() {
  return (
    <Layout>
      <ReportSummary />            {/* RSC */}
      <ReportChart data={data} />  {/* this one has 'use client' */}
    </Layout>
  );
}
```
 ### 2. Virtualize any scrollable list of more than \~50 items [Section titled “2. Virtualize any scrollable list of more than \~50 items”](#2-virtualize-any-scrollable-list-of-more-than-50-items) Rendering 1000 DOM nodes for a list the user only sees 20 of is wasted work. Use [`@tanstack/react-virtual`](https://tanstack.com/virtual) (already a dependency). `RichGrid` already handles this for the feature/issues lists; copy that pattern for any new long list. **Anti-pattern**: rendering all rows and relying on `overflow: auto` to “hide” the off-screen ones. The DOM is still there, paint cost is still there. ### 3. Memoize list-row components by stable key [Section titled “3. Memoize list-row components by stable key”](#3-memoize-list-row-components-by-stable-key) Every row in a virtualized list should be `React.memo`-wrapped with an `areEqual` that compares the row data identity (not deep equality). The parent shouldn’t re-render the row when something elsewhere in the list changes. 
```tsx
const FeatureRow = React.memo(function FeatureRow({ row }: { row: Feature }) {
  return <div>...</div>;
}, (prev, next) => prev.row === next.row);
```
 Pair with **stable identity** in the data layer — on the Zero/WebSocket transport `useSyncQuery` returns the same object reference for unchanged rows. If you map the data into new objects on every render, memoization is useless. ### 4. Animate only `transform` and `opacity` (and `filter` sparingly) [Section titled “4. Animate only transform and opacity (and filter sparingly)”](#4-animate-only-transform-and-opacity-and-filter-sparingly) These are GPU-composited; the browser handles them off the main thread. Animating `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `padding`, `margin`, `font-size`, or any size-affecting property forces layout + paint on every frame and torches your frame rate. 
```tsx
// Wrong — animates layout
<div style={{ transition: 'width 200ms', width: open ? 320 : 0 }} />


// Right — animates the GPU-composited transform
<div style={{ transition: 'transform 200ms', transform: open ? 'translateX(0)' : 'translateX(-100%)' }} />
```
 If you absolutely need to animate size, use `motion`’s `layout` prop, which uses FLIP under the hood (compute the start/end rects, animate the *transform* between them — not the size). ### 5. Never animate inside a `useEffect` that depends on a frequently-changing value [Section titled “5. Never animate inside a useEffect that depends on a frequently-changing value”](#5-never-animate-inside-a-useeffect-that-depends-on-a-frequently-changing-value) Animation effects with unstable deps trigger re-render storms. If you find yourself writing `useEffect(() => { setTimeout(...) }, [openCount])`, you’re about to fire one timeout per render. Use `motion`’s declarative API (`animate` prop) instead. ### 6. Keep server-only code out of the browser bundle [Section titled “6. Keep server-only code out of the browser bundle”](#6-keep-server-only-code-out-of-the-browser-bundle) > **Reframed for the SPA.** The old wording (“`'use client'` files cannot import server-only code”) was a Next.js RSC boundary rule. `'use client'` no longer means anything, and `app/api/` is gone — server endpoints live in the Hono host (`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts` + `lib/endpoint-route/`). The underlying hazard is still real on the SPA. Everything in the operator-vite client tree gets bundled and shipped to the browser. Don’t import Postgres clients, credential loaders, `node:fs`, or other host-only modules into a component or a file the client tree reaches — it bloats the bundle and can leak secrets. Keep client/server-only types and functions in separate files and cross the boundary via the Hono API (`fetch`/`useSyncQuery`), not a direct import. ### 7. Don’t add a dependency you’ll only use once [Section titled “7. Don’t add a dependency you’ll only use once”](#7-dont-add-a-dependency-youll-only-use-once) A 50 KB lib for a single gradient effect is not a fair trade. Inspect the route’s chunk with a Vite/rollup bundle visualizer (e.g. `rollup-plugin-visualizer` against the operator-vite build) before adding any dep over \~5 KB gzip and prove it’s worth the cost. (The old `ANALYZE=true npm run build` / `@next/bundle-analyzer` flow is gone with Next — `@next/bundle-analyzer` is not installed, and `apps/operator`’s `build` script just runs the operator-docs Starlight build then the operator-vite Vite build.) If the team has a stalwart utility (e.g. `@formkit/auto-animate` / `motion` for animations, `lucide-react` for icons), use it instead of pulling a parallel one. ### 8. Always test under “Slow 4G” + “4× CPU throttle” in DevTools [Section titled “8. Always test under “Slow 4G” + “4× CPU throttle” in DevTools”](#8-always-test-under-slow-4g--4-cpu-throttle-in-devtools) What feels fine on your M3 Pro is unusable on a $300 Chromebook. The harness page is an internal tool — most of the audience is on developer hardware — but the muscle memory matters because it surfaces real perf regressions you’d otherwise miss. ## Soft rules — should follow [Section titled “Soft rules — should follow”](#soft-rules--should-follow) ### 9. `React.memo`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` — only when measured to help [Section titled “9. React.memo, useMemo, useCallback — only when measured to help”](#9-reactmemo-usememo-usecallback--only-when-measured-to-help) Premature memoization adds maintenance cost and rarely helps. The exceptions: * Components in a virtualized list (always memo). * Components that pass props down a deep tree (memo + stable refs). * Computations > 1 ms (useMemo). Profile first. For everything else, React’s reconciler is fast enough. Don’t `useCallback` every event handler “just in case.” ### 10. Use `useDeferredValue` and `useTransition` for slow updates [Section titled “10. Use useDeferredValue and useTransition for slow updates”](#10-use-usedeferredvalue-and-usetransition-for-slow-updates) If a search input filters a 500-row table, the typing should feel snappy and the filtering can lag a few ms. Wrap the filter in `useDeferredValue(query)`; the input updates immediately, the table updates when there’s an idle frame. ### 11. Co-locate slow data fetches with `<Suspense>` boundaries [Section titled “11. Co-locate slow data fetches with \<Suspense> boundaries”](#11-co-locate-slow-data-fetches-with-suspense-boundaries) A page that needs both a fast and a slow data source should stream — the fast part renders, the slow part shows a skeleton. Don’t block the whole page on the slowest fetch. 
```tsx
<Page>
  <FastHeader />
  <Suspense fallback={<SlowChartSkeleton />}>
    <SlowChart />
  </Suspense>
</Page>
```
 ### 12. Use the `next/image` shim (`@/lib/router-compat`) for any non-icon image, and always set explicit dimensions [Section titled “12. Use the next/image shim (@/lib/router-compat) for any non-icon image, and always set explicit dimensions”](#12-use-the-nextimage-shim-librouter-compat-for-any-non-icon-image-and-always-set-explicit-dimensions) The `next/image` import resolves to the router-compat shim (`apps/operator/lib/router-compat`), not Next’s optimizer — there is no Next image server in the SPA. Whichever `<img>`/`<Image>` you use, **set explicit `width`/`height` (or an aspect-ratio box) and `loading="lazy"` for below-the-fold images.** A bare `<img>` with no reserved box is a guaranteed CLS regression. ### 13. Move heavy CPU work to a Web Worker [Section titled “13. Move heavy CPU work to a Web Worker”](#13-move-heavy-cpu-work-to-a-web-worker) Anything > 50 ms of synchronous JS work blocks user input. Examples that should be in a worker, not the main thread: * Markdown / code highlighting (we currently do this on main thread — known TODO) * JSON-Schema → form converter for huge schemas * Search index building * CSV / large-payload parsing The pattern: `new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`. ### 14. Lazy-load above-the-fold-but-not-critical features [Section titled “14. Lazy-load above-the-fold-but-not-critical features”](#14-lazy-load-above-the-fold-but-not-critical-features) Plugin tabs in Config aren’t visible until the user clicks Config. Tutorial dock isn’t visible until invoked. Use the `dynamic` shim (`@/lib/router-compat/dynamic`) — or plain `React.lazy` + `<Suspense>` — for these: 
```tsx
const ProposalsPanel = dynamic(() => import('./ProposalsPanel'), { ssr: false });
```
 (The `ssr: false` option is a no-op vestige on the SPA — there is no SSR — but the shim accepts it so call sites don’t have to change.) Reduces the initial chunk for the harness route; the lazy chunk loads when needed. ### 15. Prefer CSS `contain` and `content-visibility` for off-screen work [Section titled “15. Prefer CSS contain and content-visibility for off-screen work”](#15-prefer-css-contain-and-content-visibility-for-off-screen-work) Tabs that are open but not visible (because their `data-state="inactive"`) still cost layout/paint. Tell the browser to skip them: 
```css
.h-tab-content[data-state="inactive"] {
  content-visibility: auto;          /* skip rendering when off-screen */
  contain-intrinsic-size: 800px 600px; /* reserve space so scroll position doesn't jump */
}
```
 ## Animation rules [Section titled “Animation rules”](#animation-rules) Adopting the [animation strategy](#) (see also `lib/forms` style guide for forms): | Need | Use | Reach for it because | | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Modal / popover / dropdown / tab open/close | **CSS keyframes on Radix `data-state`** | Native compositor; zero JS cost. The `--ease-out` / `--ease-in` / `--dur-fast` / `--dur-normal` / `--dur-slow` tokens in `globals.css` are the standard. | | List item add / remove / reorder | **`@formkit/auto-animate`** | One-line `useAutoAnimate`. WAAPI direct; zero React re-renders. | | Counter tweens, choreography, drag, layout | **`motion`** | WAAPI-backed since v10. `<motion.div>`, `AnimatePresence`, `LayoutGroup`. | | Cross-route page transitions | **plain TanStack `<Link>`** (+ the Web Animations API for the two jump-gate links) | `next-transition-router` was removed as pure overhead when the app moved to TanStack Router. Ordinary navigation is now a plain TSR `<Link>` (instant, no transition machine); `RouteTransitionProvider` only plays a WAAPI transform/opacity “warp” on the two `jump-gate` anchors (`/` and `/adv`). The route progress bar is driven by `@bprogress/react`, not `next-transition-router`. | | **Don’t use** | GSAP, Theatre, react-spring, popmotion | Either overkill, abandoned, or duplicates of what we already have. | **Reduced-motion is mandatory**: 
```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  }
}
```
 For motion-driven JS animations, wrap the dashboard tree in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`. ## Network / data rules [Section titled “Network / data rules”](#network--data-rules) ### 16. Use the local cache before the network [Section titled “16. Use the local cache before the network”](#16-use-the-local-cache-before-the-network) `useSyncQuery` (`libs/generic/sync`) is a **transport-agnostic** data hook — it works in any transport mode. On the **Zero/WebSocket** transport it gives us local-first, optimistic reads from the replica; on **polling/SSE** transports it falls back to REST. Don’t bypass it with a raw `fetch` for data the active transport already serves. Spinners on data we already have locally are a UX bug. Mutations follow the same split: `useSyncMutate(path, restFallback)` runs **optimistically through the Zero client only on the WebSocket transport** (instant local apply, then server reconcile/rollback); on polling/SSE — where there is no Zero client — it calls your `restFallback`. Pass a stable `restFallback` so the same call site is REST-correct today and becomes optimistic for free once a WS provider is mounted. (Note: no `@rocicorp/zero` dependency is declared in any `package.json` — Zero is one configured transport, not a hard dependency of the hook.) ### 17. Pre-fetch the next likely route [Section titled “17. Pre-fetch the next likely route”](#17-pre-fetch-the-next-likely-route) If clicking the harness picker is going to navigate to a different harness, use a TanStack `<Link>` (via the router-compat shim) so its chunk can be preloaded before the click. TanStack Router preloads on intent (hover/touch) when configured; keep navigation as `<Link>` elements rather than imperative `router.push` / `navigate()`, which don’t get the same preload behavior. ### 18. Cache server responses appropriately [Section titled “18. Cache server responses appropriately”](#18-cache-server-responses-appropriately) `Cache-Control: max-age=...` on idempotent GET endpoints. SWR semantics where appropriate. Zero takes care of most of this for harness data; keep it consistent for new endpoints. ### 19. `preconnect` to cross-origin API hosts [Section titled “19. preconnect to cross-origin API hosts”](#19-preconnect-to-cross-origin-api-hosts) For Anthropic, Cloudflare, Chatwoot, etc., add `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.anthropic.com">` in the SPA’s root HTML (`apps/operator-vite/index.html` `<head>`, or the root layout component). Buys you 100–300 ms on the first request. ## Layout / paint rules [Section titled “Layout / paint rules”](#layout--paint-rules) ### 20. Avoid layout thrash (read → write → read in the same frame) [Section titled “20. Avoid layout thrash (read → write → read in the same frame)”](#20-avoid-layout-thrash-read--write--read-in-the-same-frame) Reading geometry (`offsetWidth`, `getBoundingClientRect`) after writing styles forces synchronous layout. Batch reads first, then writes. 
```tsx
// Wrong — alternates read and write, forces layout each iteration
items.forEach(el => {
  const w = el.offsetWidth;       // read
  el.style.width = `${w * 2}px`;  // write (forces layout next read)
});


// Right
const widths = items.map(el => el.offsetWidth);  // batch reads
items.forEach((el, i) => el.style.width = `${widths[i] * 2}px`);  // batch writes
```
 ### 21. Use `transform: translate3d(0,0,0)` to promote heavy elements to their own layer [Section titled “21. Use transform: translate3d(0,0,0) to promote heavy elements to their own layer”](#21-use-transform-translate3d000-to-promote-heavy-elements-to-their-own-layer) Only for confirmed-hot elements (a moving canvas, a live-updating chart). Don’t sprinkle it everywhere — too many compositor layers tank GPU memory. ### 22. Avoid box-shadows on scrolling elements [Section titled “22. Avoid box-shadows on scrolling elements”](#22-avoid-box-shadows-on-scrolling-elements) Box-shadow forces re-paint on every scroll frame. If you need a shadow on a sticky header, animate via `transform: translateZ(0)` + a static shadow, or use `filter: drop-shadow` which is sometimes composited. ## Measurement — how to know if you broke it [Section titled “Measurement — how to know if you broke it”](#measurement--how-to-know-if-you-broke-it) ### 23. Use React DevTools Profiler before claiming “it’s fast” [Section titled “23. Use React DevTools Profiler before claiming “it’s fast””](#23-use-react-devtools-profiler-before-claiming-its-fast) Record an interaction. Look at: * Number of components rendered * Total render time per commit * Wasted renders (rendered but result was unchanged) Target: < 5 ms per commit on the warm path. If it’s > 16 ms, you’re below 60fps. ### 24. Run Lighthouse on the harness page weekly [Section titled “24. Run Lighthouse on the harness page weekly”](#24-run-lighthouse-on-the-harness-page-weekly) Targets: * Performance score ≥ 90 * LCP < 2.5 s * INP < 200 ms * CLS < 0.1 * TBT < 300 ms If any drops, fix it before merging the next feature. ### 25. Use the Performance tab for animation issues [Section titled “25. Use the Performance tab for animation issues”](#25-use-the-performance-tab-for-animation-issues) When an animation feels janky: 1. Open Performance tab in Chrome DevTools. 2. Record the interaction. 3. Look at the Frames row. Anything not green (i.e. frames > 16 ms) is dropped. 4. Check the Main row for tasks > 50 ms (long tasks block input). 5. Check the GPU row to confirm transforms/opacity are composited. ### 26. Bundle analyzer before merging a dep [Section titled “26. Bundle analyzer before merging a dep”](#26-bundle-analyzer-before-merging-a-dep) Run a Vite/rollup bundle visualizer (e.g. `rollup-plugin-visualizer`) against the operator-vite build and look at the route’s chunk for unexpected size. Anything > 100 KB on a single route is suspect. (The old `ANALYZE=true npm run build` / `@next/bundle-analyzer` path is gone — `@next/bundle-analyzer` is not installed and the build is no longer a Next build.) ## Anti-patterns we’ve fallen into before — frontend [Section titled “Anti-patterns we’ve fallen into before — frontend”](#anti-patterns-weve-fallen-into-before--frontend) These are real frontend regressions we’ve shipped and reverted: 1. **Spinning loaders for data we already have locally** — fixed for IssuesList in 2026-05-02 (now shows “No issues” instead of spinner). If you find another, kill the spinner. 2. **Using `setState` in a tight loop instead of batching** — caused chat panel scroll jank. Pattern: collect updates, set once. 3. **Importing the entire `lodash` for one helper** — pulled in 70 KB gzip. Use `lodash-es` per-function, or just write the helper inline (most “lodash helpers” are 3 lines). 4. **Animating `height`/`width` on a panel slide** — caused dropped frames. Switched to `transform: translateY`. 5. **Not memoizing RichGrid rows** — caused 200ms commits when status changed in any row. Added `React.memo`. 6. **Fetching the same plugin manifest from 12 components** — Zero deduplicates this for us; trust the cache. ## What NOT to do — server-side / data layer [Section titled “What NOT to do — server-side / data layer”](#what-not-to-do--server-side--data-layer) The 2026-05-03 perf audit found these patterns *had been shipped* and were causing the dashboard’s TTFB to be \~19 seconds on localhost. Each one is now in the “do not repeat” list: ### A1. Don’t `await` filesystem operations in a serial `for` loop [Section titled “A1. Don’t await filesystem operations in a serial for loop”](#a1-dont-await-filesystem-operations-in-a-serial-for-loop) If you read N files sequentially, the per-call latency multiplies: in the audited environment \~150ms per `fs.readFile` × 68 files = 10 seconds **just from the loop shape**, where the same code parallelized was \~14ms. (The audit measured this under the old Next.js dev server, whose HMR file-tracking instrumentation wrapped every fs call; that named cause is **stale** — dev now runs the Vite SPA on `:3055` plus a tsx/Hono host on `:3070`, with no Next dev server wrapping fs. The parallelize-the-reads advice still stands regardless of the runtime.) 
```ts
// ❌ Wrong — measured 10.9s for 68 files (serial loop shape)
for (const h of harnesses) {
  const raw = await fs.readFile(join(dir, h, 'config.json'), 'utf8');
  out[h] = JSON.parse(raw);
}


// ✅ Right — same files, ~single-call latency (10×+ speedup)
const results = await Promise.all(harnesses.map(async (h) => {
  const raw = await fs.readFile(join(dir, h, 'config.json'), 'utf8');
  return [h, JSON.parse(raw)] as const;
}));
const out = Object.fromEntries(results);
```
 **Why this matters even in production**: it’s still wasteful, just less catastrophically so. Always parallelize independent fs reads. ### A2. Don’t open one Postgres pool per slug in a serial loop [Section titled “A2. Don’t open one Postgres pool per slug in a serial loop”](#a2-dont-open-one-postgres-pool-per-slug-in-a-serial-loop) `getHarnessPg(slug)` opens a postgres-js pool with `max=1` per harness. With \~70 registered projects, calling `getHarnessPg(p.slug)` in a loop opens 70 sequential connections × \~80ms each = **5+ seconds per request**. Found at `harness.get('/projects')` — used to fire every 30s via autoloop AND every dashboard load. 
```ts
// ❌ Wrong — sequential pool opens
for (const p of projects) {
  const sql = getHarnessPg(p.slug);
  const row = await sql`SELECT 1 FROM ...`;
}


// ✅ Right — Promise.all parallelizes the pool warmup, OR
//          better yet: single admin-pool query that fans across schemas
const results = await Promise.all(projects.map(p => {
  const sql = getHarnessPg(p.slug);
  return sql`SELECT 1 FROM ...`;
}));
```
 **Best**: use the cross-harness `harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated` view (one admin pool, one query) instead of N per-harness pool opens. See [memory: harness\_features cross-harness view](#). ### A3. Don’t introduce a heavy and a lite endpoint and have hot paths use the heavy one [Section titled “A3. Don’t introduce a heavy and a lite endpoint and have hot paths use the heavy one”](#a3-dont-introduce-a-heavy-and-a-lite-endpoint-and-have-hot-paths-use-the-heavy-one) `/api/harness/projects` does N×PG-pool-open enrichment per project; `/api/harness/projects/lite` returns the same shape minus the enrichment. Audit found **5+ seconds per call**, hit on every harness page load (including SSR) and every 30-second autoloop tick. A `/lite` endpoint is a smell signal: anywhere a callsite uses the heavy version “just in case,” it likely doesn’t need the enrichment. Default to lite, justify each upgrade. ### A4. Don’t shell out to `psql` / `pg_dump` from runtime code [Section titled “A4. Don’t shell out to psql / pg\_dump from runtime code”](#a4-dont-shell-out-to-psql--pg_dump-from-runtime-code) Replaced with `postgres-js` + `@electric-sql/pglite-tools` in 2026-05-03 (commits `a979073`, `0915a96`, `599755d`). **If you find yourself wanting `spawn('psql', ...)`**, you almost certainly want postgres-js’s `sql.unsafe(text)` for SQL apply or `sql\`COPY … TO STDOUT\`.readable()`for COPY. (Historical note: the lint guard and the one allowlisted`pg-dump.ts`dev-fallback exception lived in the`@papercusp/export-state`package —`libs/papercusp-export-state`no longer exists; that package has been retired to`\_retired/snapshot-system/papercusp-export-state/\`, so the cited guard path is dead.) ### A5. Don’t put module-init side effects on a hot, re-evaluated path [Section titled “A5. Don’t put module-init side effects on a hot, re-evaluated path”](#a5-dont-put-module-init-side-effects-on-a-hot-re-evaluated-path) > **Artifact moved.** The original offender was a Next.js catch-all route, `apps/operator/app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts`, with `mountPluginApiRoutes(plugins).then(log)` at module top level — re-evaluated per request by Next dev, producing `[plugin-mount]` log spam. That route is **gone** (`apps/operator/app/api/` is empty), and `mountPluginApiRoutes().then(...)` now lives in the one-time boot script `apps/operator/bin/host-bootstrap.ts` (the Hono host), so the “re-evaluated per request” premise no longer applies. The lesson generalizes: keep boot-time side effects (route mounting, pool warmup, log statements) in a script that runs **once at process start**, not at module top level on a path that can be re-imported/re-evaluated. If a `.then(log)` runs on every request, you’ve put init work somewhere hot. Guard it behind a “first call” papercup or hoist it into the host bootstrap. ### A6. Don’t use `<details>` to gate “lazy” rendering [Section titled “A6. Don’t use \<details> to gate “lazy” rendering”](#a6-dont-use-details-to-gate-lazy-rendering) Native `<details>` keeps its children **mounted in the DOM regardless of `open`**; the browser only toggles visibility. A `<details>`-wrapped 21-row × 100-`<option>` table costs the same as an always-open one. Use the `LazyDetails` component (`apps/operator/app/_components/LazyDetails.tsx`) which actually defers child mount until first toggle-open. 
```tsx
// ❌ Wrong — children render even when collapsed
<details>
  <summary>Per-role voices</summary>
  <RoleVoicesTable {...} />  {/* mounts immediately */}
</details>


// ✅ Right — children mount only after first open
<LazyDetails summary="Per-role voices">
  <RoleVoicesTable {...} />
</LazyDetails>
```
 ### A7. Don’t poll on a 500ms cadence “for safety” [Section titled “A7. Don’t poll on a 500ms cadence “for safety””](#a7-dont-poll-on-a-500ms-cadence-for-safety) Polling cadences should match the data’s actual change rate. A 500ms poll for system-voice-list arrival (changes once per page lifetime) is wasted CPU at best, render storm at worst. Cap at 5 attempts then stop. For ongoing polling (action log, scoper-result), use 4s while-something-active / 30s otherwise. ### A8. Don’t push the same id twice into a render-key list [Section titled “A8. Don’t push the same id twice into a render-key list”](#a8-dont-push-the-same-id-twice-into-a-render-key-list) 
```tsx
cs.push({ id: 'replan', ... });   // unified non-destructive replan
// ...
cs.push({ id: 'replan', ... });   // legacy destructive variant — DUPLICATE
```
 This **freezes the dashboard**: React’s “two children with same key” Console Error fires Next.js’s error overlay, which fires Fast Refresh full-reload, which re-renders → same error → infinite loop. Real incident on 2026-05-03; took the dashboard offline. Always grep for `id: 'YOUR_ID'` and `key="YOUR_KEY"` before adding to a registered-list pattern. ### A9. Don’t dynamic-import inside a hot loop [Section titled “A9. Don’t dynamic-import inside a hot loop”](#a9-dont-dynamic-import-inside-a-hot-loop) 
```ts
for (const p of projects) {
  const fs = await import('node:fs/promises').then(m => m);  // wrong — per-iteration
  await fs.readFile(...);
}
```
