Making it a plugin would mean “harness with no plugins = empty UI” which breaks the first-run experience and the “core works without plugins” guarantee. 2. **`summary` should stay CORE.** Every harness benefits from “what got done”; the implementation is template-agnostic (read features+goals from state, render a timeline). Pulling it into a plugin would force every template author to either reimplement it or depend on the same plugin (a tax on adoption). 3. **`pi` should be a PLUGIN, not core.** Pi/omp is one specific external tool; not all harnesses use it. Treating it as core would tie papercusp to one external tool. **The dashboard nuance**: the dashboard *chrome* (tab strip, panel layout, action surfaces) stays core. The dashboard’s *primary panel* (feature queue for coding ≠ briefing pipeline for research-org) is contributed by the active template via a `defaultDashboardPanel` UI contribution. Templates ship their own dashboard panel; the chrome stays core. ## 14.6 Migration plan — porting tabs to plugins [Section titled “14.6 Migration plan — porting tabs to plugins”](#146-migration-plan--porting-tabs-to-plugins) The migration is straightforward because each tab is already an isolated React component in `apps/papercusp/app/harness/`. Each plugin extraction is: 1. Move the component file into `libs/papercusp-marketplace/seeds/papercupai/<plugin-name>/src/` 2. Wrap it in a `Plugin` export with appropriate per-id capabilities 3. Replace the inline `activePanel === 'X'` render with a `dashboardTabs` contribution 4. Publish via the seed-publish pipeline (service token model) 5. Add to `papercup-coding`’s `recommends:` so existing users get it on install Per-tab effort estimate (post-Phase-P2): | Tab → Plugin | Lines | Capabilities | Est | Status | | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------------- | | `vscode` → `@papercupai/vscode-server` | \~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:vscode` + config `code_server_url` | 30 min | **Retired 2026-07-07** | | `docs` → `@papercupai/fumadocs` | \~10 (iframe) | `ui:harness-tab:docs` + config `docs_url` | 30 min | P7 | | `pi` → `@papercupai/pi-companion` | \~150 (PiPanel) | `ui:harness-tab:pi` + typed-services for child-process needs | 1.5h | P7 | | `proposals` → `@papercupai/scope-proposals` | substrate-protocol change | New: plugin authorization to mutate harness-canonical state | DEFERRED to v1.5 | See note | **Why proposals is deferred to v1.5**: proposals isn’t a UI panel extraction. The blocker is **the write side** — today `apply_proposal_to_spec` is substrate code mutating substrate-canonical state (SPEC.md, the goals tree). For proposals to live in a plugin, the substrate has to authorize a plugin to mutate harness-canonical state, which is a real authorization-model question (not “let plugins call substrate functions” — those exist via the DI proxy — but “let plugins overwrite the harness contract”). Designing that authorization model is its own milestone; until then, proposals stays core. Total v1 migration effort (vscode + docs + pi): \~2.5h of straightforward refactoring once the action + tab plugin primitives are in place. The migration is **non-breaking** because: * Each tab keeps its component code, just relocates * The dashboard chrome already has a generic `dashboardTabs` slot * Plugins are loaded at substrate boot; existing harnesses see them on next `papercusp run` * Templates that haven’t been republished still work (they just don’t get the new tabs until users explicitly install the plugins) ## 14.7 Implementation roadmap [Section titled “14.7 Implementation roadmap”](#147-implementation-roadmap) Order matters; later items depend on earlier. **Status — 2026-04-27**: P1 → P8 shipped + operator dashboards for `audit.action_executions` (drill-down + webhooks) and plugin grants (`granted-capabilities.json` + `extended-grants.json` with revoke). **Seven** in-tree reference plugins (`@papercupai/{vscode-server, cloudflare-pages,pi-coding,fumadocs,slack-notifier,postgres-manager, notion-export}`) published to the local marketplace; full publish → catalog → install → enable → lockfile round-trip verified end-to-end with the service-token CI flow. Drill-down drawer has **Detail** + **History** tabs + a **Retry** button (re-invokes via the substrate CLI, mirrors the result back into `audit.action_executions`) + a **diagnose→remediate** affordance that surfaces a “revoke grants for this plugin” shortcut when an error message looks capability-related. Per-plugin audit page at `/papercusp-marketplace-ops/plugins/<slug>` aggregates every audit row across all action names with per-action filter chips. Top-of-page sticky nav links the four sections (Stats / Recent / Plugin grants / Action failures) with a red-pill count when there are recent failures. Webhook subscriptions are managed inline (operator-token-gated; create with event-type chips, disable/enable/delete per row, expandable per-row delivery log). `papercusp lock {check,upgrade-all,prune}` closes the lockfile-hygiene loop on the CLI; `lock prune` cascades transitive-orphan removal. Capability- aware install diff shows `+added` / `-removed` per cap before the consent prompt fires when there’s a prior grant. Per-harness audit page mirrors the per-plugin one — drill in from the harness column in the grants table to see every action invocation across all plugins on that harness. Both the per- harness and per-plugin pages show a cross-pivot grants table linking back to the other axis. History tab surfaces a per-row “vs prior” diff hint (same / +N / -M / \~K) so flaky-but-equivalent vs flaky-and-different is visible at a glance. Webhook deliveries sub-table is sortable by status / attempt / ts and gains a per-row replay button that resets a delivery to attempt 0. The drawer is deep-linkable via `?drawer=<auditId>`; back/forward syncs the open state naturally. Grants table supports multi-select + bulk-revoke and renders capability pills color-coded by tier (high=red, medium=amber, low=grey). Recent-action-failures table is now substring-filterable by harness, plugin, or error message. Persistent operator audit log (`audit.operator_actions`) records every operator-token-gated mutation and surfaces in a new dashboard panel with substring filtering. Grants table supports tier filter chips (high/medium/low) so operators can isolate the dangerous grants. Audit log + grants table both have CSV export for offline records. Webhook subscriptions can rotate their HMAC secret with a one-shot reveal modal. Marketplace Ed25519 signing key has an inspect + rotate surface that archives the old key (timestamped) and continues serving signatures already minted against archived keys. Test coverage: 27 plugin-loader action tests + 7 hot-reload + 12 lockfile + 7 lock-resolve + 15 consent + 7 plugin-cli + 9 grants = **84 passing**. Bonus operator surfaces: `papercusp plugin invoke <slug> <action>`, `papercusp plugin watch <slug>`, `papercusp upgrade-pin <slug>`, marketplace-ops Action-executions card + Recent-action-failures table + per-row drill-down drawer, a 30-second poller that emits `action.failed` / `action.timeout` webhook deliveries from `audit.action_executions`, and a **Plugin grants** card + per-harness table with revoke + sticky “extended to all” un-stick. Live state: `audit.action_executions` migration applied to the running `papercusp` Postgres DB (incl. `webhook_emitted_at` column for scanner idempotency); `/v1/admin/overview` includes `actionExecutions`, `/v1/admin/action-executions/:id` returns full row detail; the grants dashboard reads `~/.papercusp/{granted-capabilities,extended-grants}.json` server-side (no token needed; operator filesystem is the boundary). P9+ open (publishing the in-tree reference plugins, more reference plugins, action history view inside the drill-down drawer, retry-from-drawer). ### Phase P1 — Add `kind` to publishes (\~2h, completely additive) ✅ shipped [Section titled “Phase P1 — Add kind to publishes (\~2h, completely additive) ✅ shipped”](#phase-p1--add-kind-to-publishes-2h-completely-additive--shipped) * Schema: `ALTER TABLE packages ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'template'` * Server: read `manifest.kind` on publish, default to `'template'`, store in DB + Typesense * Marketplace site: `/marketplace/?kind=plugin` filter;
